Chocolate lucuma - its like a mousse au chocolat and a smashed oreo and corn flakes had a really beautiful triracial delicious lovechild. I don't care if that sounds racist, foodist(?). Have it.

Ok, now on to drinks.
I had a couple different ones. I'll be honest, I can't recall them on the menu anymore.
The first involved pineapple, it was crisp and delicious and a great way to open the meal with. The second, was rainbow colored, and even though it was gay pride and I am obnoxiously queer - it was nothing to write home about.
They have a beautifully stocked full bar, so in case of doubt, lean on the bottle name that is tried and true to you.

Venue. Whomever designed this place was smart af. It's large open corner street space, with a gorgeous open kitchen as a result. We sat at a table in front of the kitchen. If you're coming as 2 people, I recommend you sit directly in front of the kitchen because it is a sight for food hungry eyes. If I must point something out that ticked me off entirely, because I'm that kind of restaurant OCD, the toilet paper rolls slip off the holders, so hold the roll in place! 

Service. You'll end up with someone different any time. So my small grain of salt is, you will NOT be ignored, however, you may find it lightly overbearing. We were asked how we found each course, one too many times (or more) but more as result of there being more than one person checking in.

I'll leave it at that. Eat in front of the kitchen, eat as much as you can spend on. Be delighted.
Great vibe and excellent food. Bartenders are passionate and skilled with their craft. The open kitchen serves beautiful, tasty dishes. Tried several seafood and lamb dishes and loved them all.

I love reviewing restaurants in my neighborhood. As a person that travels for work, I eat out almost every night, but when I'm home it is rare to find a new spot that is good enough to write about. As soon as i walked into the llama inn i was excited to start eating. It smelled amazing and our drinks were incredible to start with. we ate so much of the menu omg. We loved it all tbh! The skewers were all amazing. I could go there and eat just those! Drink and Eat and enjoy yourselves! Great new spot!

Always excited to see a new place open up in the neighborhood, and I've heard great things about brunch, so we decided to try it out for a weeknight dinner.  

Table inventory is tight - the place was filling up on a weeknight at 7pm, but if you can eat later it was almost empty by 9p. Definitely call ahead to see if there's room. Unfortunately, this place does hold the best tables (booths) for friends/regulars, even if they don't show up for hours. So, be prepared to sit at an uncomfortable hightop for your romantic night out despite there being multiple empty booths that will remain unseated for the duration of your visit. 
In short: This place has an air of unearned pretension: if they don't know you, be prepared for the least favorable seating. 

After we were seated, it took over 30 minutes for us to get a server to take our first drink and food order. On a busy saturday night I would sort of expect this, but the place was only moderately full and seemed to have a full complement of waitstaff. The servers seemed to be disorganized - there was confusion about who was covering which tables and there seemed to be several servers covering our table, which in practice meant nobody was. 
In short: very poor service. 

The food was very good - plate scraping indeed. However, the portions are very small in relation to the price - if you are out for a proper dinner with three people and a drink each expect to spend at least $60-75 per person after tip. That's with one drink - cocktails average $14 each.
In short: food is good but poor value - cost does not compensate for small portions and poor service. 

Based on this experience I certainly won't be bringing a group to Llama again. I MIGHT grab a drink at the bar and order a small bite, but that's it. 

If reasonably-priced peruvian without the pretense is your thing, I strongly recommend the neighborhood standby across the street: Chimu. It will take half the time and your wallet (and stomach) will thank you.

We had the tuna tiradito and corvina ceviche -- both delicious and really well balanced, the ceviche was a particular highlight. The duck sausage was also awesome. And the grilled branzino -- AMAZING. Our server was really friendly, knew the menu and food really well, and was hilarious. And the place is super cute

TL;DR: everything is awesome. The food is great and the service is really good, cute spot.
WOW!!!  Amazing.  You need to just go and enjoy.  The food is fantastic and the wine selection is wonderful.

A beautifully designed space right under the BQE.  The staff is friendly.  The food is an inventive modern take on Peruvian cuisine.  The dishes are hand made and gorgeous.  My favorites were the raw tuna appetizer with lime sauce -- a perfect combination of flavors -- and the heavenly  sous vide strawberry dessert with poppy seeds -- tangy and sweet all in one.  Will have to come back for brunch and to try the rooftop for brunch!

We had a 9:30pm reservation and weren't seated until 10:20pm. They didn't even offer to comp the one round of drinks we had while standing near the bathrooms and waiting for 50 minutes until we insisted after the check came. Having said that, the food was amazing. Every single dish we tried was delicious. I can't even pick a favorite. The service seemed a little subpar-- less than friendly server, confused waitstaff bringing out plates to the wrong tables, and a manager who rolled her eyes when we suggested that our first round of drinks should be on the house (though she did oblige). We still had a great time because we had good company and as I said before, the food was excellent! The only food choice I would NOT recommend would be the donuts for dessert. It tasted like a giant cheerio covered in soy sauce. Blech. Overall, I would recommend it as a one-time visit, but I don't think that I will be back.

This is just opinion.  Most wealthy people who want to pay $150++ for a little scrap of food in Williamsburg should love it.  The food really tasted delightful.  Service was wonderful.  But this place not for me.  I like red lobster and hate booze.  A cocktail is $14!!!!   WTF?!?!

This was not my time.  Not my place.  And we go to a Peruvian place in MONTCLAIR NJ that we adore but this is nothing like it.  

I will say that my wife made a reservation and we ended up on the bar.  That's a little ridiculous.  

Worse yet barely anything for vegetarians.  I

We asked to sit on the rooftop and they said the menu was limited up there.  I thought the menu was limited downstairs too.  

Look this restaurant has great food.  But it's a trendy place that requires waiting and some personal sacrifice for people who aren't into meat.  

I recommend for some but not for me.  It's in the middle. Three stars.

Great bartenders, and a very casual place to be enjoyed with friends. The pork belly appetizer is quite good, but a touch pricey. My favorite plate was the steak for two. The avocado, fries, and pancake type tortilla are a great treat. Steak was flavorful, fries crispy, avocado perfectly ripe and pancake/tortilla soft and hot!

I've been here twice for dinner now and have enjoyed every single dish and drink I've tasted. The pork belly skewers, the tuna, and the scallops, oh the scallops, these were beyond. The other dishes were solidly good - the duck sausage, the baby gem salad, the chicken skewer - all very good. The cocktails are creative and delicious. It's a happy, friendly atmosphere, nicely set up and decorated without seeming pretentious. Yes, it's pricey, but worth it. These guys have mastered the art of combining flavors in unexpected and delightful ways. I can't wait to go back and try everything else on the menu.
Some of the best oysters I've had in the city, and the best scallop dish I've ever had. Great drinks. Only downside was we had to wait an hour for a table that we'd reserved ahead of time.

My date and I paid $120 for our meal...
We're still hungry!
Pretentious, expensive, it's like a gentrified Peruvian restaurant.

Wow, I shared a beet salad and branzino with two other people, one of whom was a tourist to nyc. She told me it was one of the best meals she's had while in nyc and I think I would agree! It was perfect. The staff is very friendly and accommodating, although be warned it can be difficult to get a seat at a table without reservations. I also had the "llama del rey" which is basically a sangria. It was a bit on the cinnamony side, too much for my taste, but the cherimoya cocktail my friend got was delicious and perfect. It's definitely worth a stop, whether you live in the area or are a visitor to NYC!

waiter judged us hard for ordering a lot of food.

it tasted like heaven.

we ate it all.

he was embarrassed. 

we were & are happy.

If I could give Llama Inn 4.5 stars, I would. We had a wonderful dinner here last night. Our friend who lives in Manhattan took us. The beet salad and whole Branzino were highlights. The fish was cooked to perfection and served with accompaniments that weren't necessary (that's how fresh and moist it was) but were delicious nonetheless (charred lemon, supple butter sauce, etc.). Drinks were fantastic and service was solid/attentive. The only annoyance was the wait.

Went for brunch. Food was decent, but the options are lacking compared with the rave reviews and photos I see for dinner. You won't have to wait in line or make a reservation ahead of time, the food will be fine, but you'll probably need to return for dinner to get the true feel.

I went to Llama Inn last night... before I write this I am going to say if you are looking for traditional Peruvian food, this is not your place. I have been to Peruvian restaurants all over the city (and in Peru) so this is based on the fact that this is -contemporary- Peruvian food with a Brooklyn flair and I will not compare this to traditional Peruvian cooking.

Food: We ordered the ceviche corvina and all 4 anticuchos to start (pork belly, chicken thigh, beef heart, and octopus). The leche de tigre (tigers milk) for the ceviche was excellent and I enjoyed the plantains and bananas added in, the fish was marinaded perfectly. Out of the skewers, I enjoyed the beef heart and pork belly the most. For dinner, we ordered the lomo saltado ("beef tenderloin stir fry" on the menu) to share. The fries, tomatoes, onions were all perfectly marinaded in the soy sauce/vinegar sauce. The beef was very tender. On top they had a rocoto crema which was very tasty and even gave a small bottle in case you wanted to add more... which of course I did. :) The plate came with scallion pancakes which were DELICIOUS and we used those to wrap the food in. A waitress came by with white rice to put on our plate when we were about halfway done to sop up the rest of the juices in the lomo saltado. AMAZING. 

Drinks: Inca Kola shouldn't be $4 but it's NY so I'll let that slide. I ordered the Flying Purple Pisco drink... it was DELICIOUS. It was a twist on the traditional pisco sour, and I really enjoyed it.

Dessert: We ordered the lucuma ice cream dessert. Very good!

Service: I wish I got the name of our server but I know he was Dominican. Nice, funny guy and prompt service. Thank you!

Only reason I give this place 4 stars is because we were burning up and it was uncomfortably hot... makes it hard to fully enjoy the meal. However, it was one of the hottest days of summer but the AC definitely could have been turned up more? Other than that, the food/drinks/service were all 5 stars.

It's been awhile since I've enjoyed a dinner as wonderful as Llama Inn's Monday night roasted chicken special. Should you ever visit Llama Inn when they are offering this special - a whole roasted chicken, fried potatoes and a sampling of inventive, homemade sauces -  you MUST order it. It's succulent, juicy, perfectly crispy (sorry but only the most creepy adjectives are fit to describe just how good this chicken is).

In addition, the service at Llama Inn is consistently friendly and attentive. In the ultra-hip restaurant scene of Williamsburg, such pretension-free (aka: NOT "too-cool-to-care") service is hard to come by.  I recommend sitting at the chef's counter, as it is a unique and educational experience.

Just great. The food. The service. You need to come check this out. I've been to this place at least 5 times and every time it delivers. The food is Peruvian street food elevated. Tons of flavor. It's a great departure from everything else in the neighborhood. I love the fun spirit beyond the llama brand too. My taste buds always bring me back and I bet yours will be singing once you've checked this place out.

First visit: Had a reservation for 5 but crammed us into a 4 person table due to their mistake.  Were apologetic but couldn't move us.

Second visit: fine

Final visit:  Seated 40 minutes late.  No apology.  Ordered coffee at end of meal.  Had to ask for spoons and cream.  Used the cream and it was curdled.  Asked for replacement coffee.  One mug was dirty with dried chunks on the inside of it.  Asked for a new mug.  Noticed it was dirty too after it was too late.  Nothing off the bill, no offers of free drinks, just a general frazzled-ness that rubs off on the patrons.

Really cool rooftop bar! The restaurant is amazing! Chef Erik is the best! You will not leave hungry and you will try very unique plays on some Peruvian classics. I highly recommend the llama inn to anyone near Williamsburg or near NYC.

WORST SERVICE I've experienced at a restaurant in a Very long time. Staff is incredibly rude. Our experience here was absolutely miserable. We sat on the roof - bartender was beyond rude, went out of her way to be unpleasant. Took away our drinks before we were even half way through. Can't believe a restaurant can even function with such awful service. Would give 0 stars if it were an option.

I feel like I have been giving a lot of 5 star reviews lately which may start to discredit me, but I promise this place deserves it! 

The food was fantastic and service was very efficient. We arrived 30 minutes early and were seated right away, at the chef's counter. If you like to watch your food being made, it is a fun experience and you get to hear all the orders being called out. It is a little warm since you are in the kitchen so don't sit hear if you are prone to getting hot. 

That said, the food was innovative and exciting, each dish with its own unique and flavorful sauce. I highly recommend the lamb belly (the meat was like butter), the pork belly anticucho, the heirloom tomato salad (sounds boring but it was fresh, with a nice balance of sweet, salty, and crunchy), and the sea bream tiradito (swimming in the most delicious sweet/sour fruit sauce). We lapped up all the sauce once the fish was gone.

The only dish that I was not crazy about was the duck sausage with rice. The rice had more flavor than the sausage so if you are looking for just a good bowl of rice for $20+, this is the dish for you.

Overall, this was an amazing dinner with new and interesting flavors. Definitely worth checking out.

Food tastes good, but EAT before you go because if you don't, you will leave hungry. 

The masters degree level of theatrical Williamsburg service was both annoying and comical, but ...

the kicker is that they don't accept CASH.  No money. And while they don't tell you this until the bill comes, they say this with a straight face.  Suddenly they lose all the dramatics and prose.  No cash.  

Do Peruvians only pay with credit cards?  I've told my neighbors, born and raised in WB, about this latest addition. Lots of shaking heads... Take it back to Lima. 

And water your plants...

llama inn is excellent. went for a friends birthday dinner on a sunday night. service was great. food was amazing, flavorful and inventive.
we ordered the below dishes and loved them all, especially the beef stir fry which is their take on traditional peruvian dish "lomo saltado"
- quinoa, banana, avocado, bacon, cashew
-beets, muna, goat cheese, gooseberry, cancha 
-ceviche, gooseberry
-octopus, aji amarillo, cabbage, quinoa
-beef tenderloin stir fry
-chocolate, lucuma, coffee 

go and enjoy!!!

Really great place.. The staff are above and beyond attentive and all seem passionate about the food and your experience. The décor is very Brooklyn small trendy etc. The food was delicious and different. For starter we had the quinoa which was interesting the combo of banana and bacon giving a creamy and crunchy texture , the cashews were nice texture change while the avocado was lost completely. Next we had the anticucho pork belly a little salty, you definitely get the spicy on them,chicken thigh very flavorful and tender, and the octopus delicious well cooked and seasoned very much enjoyed would order again for sure. Next was the duck sausage which was good different for me but a welcomed surprise,spicy and fresh tasting the English peas were a welcomed veggie with the dish.  Last we had the beef tenderloin meat was tender and delicious the fries were fries and the scallion pancakes were very good more like crepes to make a taco of the tenderloin...the sauce it came in was on the salty side (like drink a glass of water salty) they even came and put rice over our sauce which was a welcomed surprise the cut the salty a bit. We did also get dessert the chanvaca which was nothing crazy, they were doughnuts in a molasses sauce,I wouldn't recommend them honestly. Over all there were 3 of us and this filled us but we weren't stuffed. The plates are extremely small for the price. We also ordered drinks all were tasty not very strong though.The sharing aspect was really nice and fun and the knowledge our waitress had was very helpful. There is a roof top it was raining but I'd expect it to be nice. Overall great experience I'd go back but I'd probably go just for snacking.

I came here on a Sunday for brunch the host looked very tired/ hungover not friendly at all. In my opinion the food was tasty but overpriced. You can probably get the same Peruvian brunch in Queens for half or even 1/3 of the price.

Sunday was my second time here, and the experience was beyond awful. We sat at the roof, where the server went out of her way to be rude. She slammed onto the table every dish and drink she brought to us. She took my drink before I was even done and when I went to ask her for my beer she immediately answered "it was too far from you". When I told her to repeat what she said, she answered "well, at least you are getting another one for free". Not the right attitude when you are trying to enjoy dinner with friends. On top of that, they charged my card twice and pass it as one bill. I signed a receipt for $41.15 but then when I saw my bank statement she charged me $82.30. I'm never coming back to this place.

Decadent Peruvian fusion experience. Each plate on its own is magnificent-- a unique beautiful experience. Flavors are excellent.  The only downside-- the small plates don't necessarily match each other to create rich and light notes in the menu. Also too much juice at the bottom of the ceviche dish. All in all a great fusion experience.

Authentic Peruvian food presented with a sophisticated feel but without the arrogance. We ordered almost the entire menu and enjoyed every bite. The staff and atmosphere here are wonderful. Williamsburg is filled with great food and this place is one of the best for sure.

Unique food and cocktails! / tried the octopus and pork belly skewers / amazing / as well as the ceviche with plantains and one of the bibb salads - all very delicious and fresh with lots of complex flavors. Will definitely be back to try more dishes!

During a vacation stay in Brooklyn, we went to the Llama Inn. This was one of the most wonderful dining experiences I have had in a long time. Service was outstanding, the noise level was acceptable, and the food was exquisite. 
After a delicious tomato salad, and some grilled octopus, we shared one of the big plates, a beef stir fry topped in French fries. (Not sure how Peruvian that is) but coupled with the green onion pancakes (soft taco-shellish) the trender, juicy meat and mixture of vegetables had flavor leaping off the plate.

Contemporary Peruvian food at its finest! Small plates, so don't come starving but leave you with a lasting flavor. The anticuchos were amazing! I would recommend that beef heart any day! (The octopus was overcooked so maybe skip that one). 

Lomo saltado comes with a side of a Peruvian rendition of a tortilla and it makes it so delicious. 

Great service. By far best Modern Peruvian cuisine I have had.

Omg, that lomo saltado! Super delicious with tender, medium rare pieces of tenderloin, onions, scallions (some of them were pretty harsh though!), tomato, and topped with fries. LOVED the scallion pancake lomo saltado hybrid--every bite was salty, meaty, potato-ey, and creamy with the avocado and crema. For $56, it's a high price to pay, though, but worth a try. And definitely filling! Our waiter also came by at the end and placed some rice into the leftover sauce...I thought it'd be amazing but somehow tasted saltier? Hm.

Also, the quinoa with banana, cashews, bacon is way more delicious than it sounds. Crunchy red quinoa mixed with regular quinoa, cubes of bacon (yum!), and the crunch of cashews--the textures were so great. I wasn't in love with the sweetness of the bananas but that was okay and didn't take away much from my enjoyment of the meal. I can honestly say I've never had another dish quite like this. $15 or $16 (can't quite remember.)

Service was okay but the restaurant was louder than I like. I loved the atmosphere with the plants hanging over the counters and the fact that three of the restaurant's walls are basically all windows. Wish the view were a bit better though! Maybe they could transform that big sidewalk space into a cute garden :)

Anyway, the food is delicious but the prices are high. Go if you've got deep pockets and take me with you.

Really impressed with this place. The pork belly skewer was perfect and the paella was also very tasty. We had a group of four so we shared everything which I would suggest. Had a special empanada that we split two and also a beef tenderloin dish, that when we finished the meat, our server came by and mixed rice into the remaining sauce and veggies....that was ideal. Interesting cocktails on the menu...try the El Choppo! Great service (go Victor!!) and staff is very attentive. Will be back!!
Wonderful ambience.  Excellent service.  Intriguing food combinations.

This place deserves a review - my girlfriend

Everything we've put in our mouths has exploded with flavor.

The decor is fantastic and the ambiance is critically acclaimed. 

If you want Pisco... Come here.

If Spencer is at the bar, you're covered. Very personable, attentive, and inviting.

Will return frequently.

Sadly, the Llama Inn seems to go down fast. The food went from innovative to pretentious. We ordered beef heart, octopus, beer salad, and scallops as the main to share. First up was the beef heart, two pieces, drowned in mayo and spicy sauce and unrecognizable in taste. The beet salad was divine. When we asked for the octopus dish we learned that the mayo piece on the same (!) plate as the beef heart was it. The waiter turned around and made a face, not only bad dish but also bad attitude. Two (!) scallops were offered as main dish, cooked to perfection but with another creamy sauce. Boring and over priced. Time to move on.

My daughter, who is a Brooklynite, took us to the Llama Inn which she said had a good reputation.  I thought it was unpleasant and served bad food masquerading as clever variations of more familiar dishes.

To begin with, the place operates as much as a bar as a restaurant.  The one room is dominated by a large square bar which is packed.  The millennials seem to love this place and favor the bar as much as the restaurant food.  The noise level is deafening.  I could not hear my wife unless she turned to me to speak, making the dining experience less than comfortable.  But then comes the food.

I liked the salads, which were a bit skimpy, but fresh and flavorful.  Everything else was annoying and badly conceived.  If this is what expensive food is in Peru, it is no wonder there are so many Peruvians in the States.  The main dishes are "large Plates, which are dominated by french fried potatoes with seared meat and onions and peppers on top.  I could make this strange dish for about $5 or $6, but they charge $58.  The sea food mix was equally strange with a mix of seafood in a red sauce of undistinguished flavoring that looked like a gloppy mess.  The small plates were skimpy, as in 2 bites for $6 or $7 each.  To ease our meal, we each had a drink from the bar.  They have many mixed drinks which all seem a bit strange, but, what the heck, let's see what they drink in Peru.

Well they drink a lot of rubbish, if these drinks are an example.  The bartenders again try to be clever and "different", in mix alcohols that do not blend properly.  Every drink was off tasting, so I do not know why the bar does such a good business.  Millennials seem to like the scene more than the ambiance, the food or the drinks.  This might have its rewards, but at $80 a person, including tip, this restaurant is a bad value, and, more importantly, a bad product.  But, Hey!  It's Brooklyn!

On one good note, I should comment on the excellent service by the host and waiters.  These are seriously nice and warm fellows who really want you to be comfortable and have the service you deserve.  I left a good tip to reward their excellent service, despite the poor product they serve.

One of the best meals I've ever had. My boyfriend and I went here last night for our anniversary and I was blown away. I left thinking I might have to travel to Peru. 

We ordered the pork belly (GET IT, please just try it) to start and made our way through the quinoa/banana dish and the beets and goat cheese with gooseberry. So many flavors I have literally never even considered together tasted fucking amazing. Quinoa, banana, avocado, and bacon? YES. Give me all of it. We had some sort of tuna ceviche with bananas that was unreal and ended with the rock shrimp, calamari, and clams dish, which had sooo much flavor.

I can't recommend this place enough, not only for the food but the drinks and service as well. We ended the night with delicious picarones and coffee/tea. I walked into work this morning already blabbing about this place and I can't wait to come back and eat again! 

Thanks for a great night :)

Everything at the llama inn was awesome!  The vibe and ambiance is great - Fun decor and perfect for a date or friendly get together.  The service was also wonderful!  

Every single thing I ordered was flavorful and unique.  My roommate and I shared a pitcher of the Llama Del Rey which was a good size serving and got us buzzed :)  It was a little on the sweet side but the frozen grapes on the side made it a unique twist.  We also ordered the Pork Belly which was really good but a small serving. I wish we ordered multiples.  We then got the quinoa and ceviche which had such unique flavors! I just couldn't get enough.  Lastly, we ended with the Beef Tenderloin "Stir-Fry" which was BOMB! But also huge! You can share with with 3/4 people! 

Lastly, we ended with some chocolate ice cream cookie crunch thing! I dont know what it was but I know it was DELICIOUS! 

Love this place!

Arrived early for a weekday window counter Monday reservation and they graciously sat us immediately at the chef's counter instead (by request), which was a nice experience.
Their site is awful but the service inside and the food made up for it. The beef tenderloin stir fry (renamed on the menu from the Peruvian 'Lomo Saltado') was excellent, and certainly a nice profit for them @$56 but in our opinion satisfying and filling enough for 2 to split that it seemed worth it. The addition of rice near the end is a great touch, as was a cook checking how we liked it. Complimentary sparkling water (refilled often) helped wash it down throughout.

beef tenderloin stir fry

It's 12am and I am already thinking about eating my leftovers tomorrow. Yeah, I'm that trashy guy that asked for my food to go, but only because this food was the absolute bomb. My wife and I had heard rumors but tonight we decided we would go all the way. Sweet Jesus was it incredible. The service was terrific. Both server and bartenders were great. Especially Dan, Spencer, and Kasia. The food was to die for. If they had offered me a choice of my favorite entree and leaving my wife, I would have had to leave my wife and I know she would have done the same to me. I feel bad but not as bad as passing up a dish of perfection. Some standouts were the beef heart and the ceviche and banana dish (such an odd sounding pairing but so good). All of the food is incredible. And I cannot wait to come back. But for now, at 6:30am, I will settle for my leftovers and dream of a night where I can revisit the Llama Inn.

Most of the dishes were great except for the beef tenderloin. I'm not sure what the fuss is about. It was literally 4-5 cubes of beef, some veggies and fries, with a few "tacos" on the side for nearly $60. They come around with rice after a while and plop it on your plate to soak up the meat/veggie juice but by then you're already in a carb coma. Definitely worth visiting but would stick to the other dishes.
The flavors were good, but the portions were disappointingly small for the price. I finished my meal knowing I'd need a pizza supplement later in the evening. Nice atmosphere overall.

My friend and I were there last night and sat at the bar for dinner.  We were starving and got the empanadas, ceviche, chicken and pork belly skewers, short rib and beet salad.  It was not too much food and the chicken skewer is unmissable!!! Great drinks and cool atmosphere.

This is a real palette-resetter - fantastic. Big fan of this place. 

FOOD
We've been here about 4 times now, ordering different items each time (as well as a few "standbys") It's hard to describe the food, but overall, it's simply fantastic. 

The cocktails and sangria-on-tap are also truly amazing. 

ATMOSPHERE
Nice atmosphere. Building is on a corner, so there's a lot of light all over. It also has a small bar upstairs. Very nice. 

SERVICE
Good service.

My friend and I had dinner at your restaurant on Saturday evening. We had a 10:30 pm reservation. We arrived a bit early. Your gracious hostess/Maitre'd informed us that we could sit at a kitchen counter or wait a few minutes for our table. We opted to wait at the bar. We ordered our drinks and almost immediately the hostess informed us that our table was ready. 
A corner table. Banqet and all. Sweet. We had the best view in the restaurant. Rene was our server. He was great. He explained the menu, went over the specials and guided us in the right direction. 
Getting to the point: My mother is a chef. She had a restaurant for 25 years called La Furia Chalaca in Jersey. Comida Criolla. Authentic Peruvian cuisine. I'm consistently dissapointed in Peruvian restaurants in the U.S. on a regular basis. Maybe I'm just biased but honestly nobody cooks like mom. Well, I was fantastically surprised, amazed, astounded and genuinely overwhelmed at how good your food was. Not only did it match moms food but the Ceviche, the Anticuchos, Umitas and the heaven sent Picarones were actually better then hers. Wow. I genuinely felt like I was in Callao, in La Avenida De La Marina, in el Mercado eating food that I would've eaten as a child. It was breathtaking. Sublime. Authentic but elevated. Way way elevated.
THANK YOU. It was a marvelous experience. Thank you to your kind and generous staff, your eloquent and passionate Sous Chef who took time out to talk to us and your beautifully I'm appointed dining room for inspiring a warm and inviting atmosphere. Most of all thank you for an amazing dining experience. 
We will be back! Regularly. With mom. And she will experience the same sublime beauty that I now have. Thank you. Truly. I will tell everyone. Everyone shall know. 
Sincerely.

Overpriced, fun, and tasty place to eat. In terms of food, it really is good. The quinoa is great, and the skewers are pretty appetizing as well. The group I went out with also enjoyed the stir fry, which was basically Pique Macho, a Bolivian dish, but cost around $50 (which is absurd). Was it really good? Yes. Is that a fair price? No.

The most impressive thing offered here was their cocktail selection. I particularly enjoyed the chicha cocktail.

One of the best Peruvian places I've been to . This review is brunch but will come back for dinner ! The lomo Saltado is flavorful , tender , and everything it should be . Their take on chicken and waffles is unique but also really good ! The Tia Julia and Llama del Rey are great cocktails as well . Can't wait to come back for dinner and see the other menu . Great service & food .
Service not so good. Our waitress was having a bad day. The food and drinks are amazing. Will return for dinner.

The food here was quite good.   A shout out for the fries.  I am not one to eat French fries, but I couldn't put the down.  The chicken was extraordinary.  Desserts could improve, but they were satisfying.  Ate here with a party of  five.  Everyone had a good experience and found the food tasty.  Dishes are meant to share.

Really wanted to love this place but I just didn't. 

Service- not good. Even with a reservation we had to wait about 45 minutes & just to get a drink at the bar during our wait took a long time. Can't say the restaurant was extremely busy either since we were the only individuals in the restaurant who were standing around. Then our waiter was just rude. He brought us two dishes we did not order and was not someone we enjoyed communicating with throughout our meal. 

The drinks- were good! Unique and tasty. 

The food- the skewers were good, we all had 1 of each and enjoyed them. The quinoa was a commonly disliked dish amongst the party I was dining with. The corvina ceviche had plenty of juice but not enough fish, it was more like a soup (although the fish was tasty in it). The beef tenderloin stir fry was great!! 

Overall it was average but wouldn't come back or recommend this place to others.
Went here for a girls night dinner and it was good but not a must hit spot, there are better places. The service was average and so was the food. Nice atmosphere though.
How does this place only have 4 stars??? This is a straight As, 5 stars kind of place. Best Peruvian restaurant in the metropolitan region.

Best restaurant in Williamsburg. Hands down.
The beef for 3 person is so delicious and the scallops and the quinoa are out of this world.

I went this monday for my birthday but the restaurant it's not what I expected. When you talk about Peruvian food is usually diverse food and generous portions and this place doesn't have that. We tried ceviche, rice with seafood, chicken and anticuchos. The portion of the ceviche and anticuchos was very small. I think was just 6 pieces of fish in the ceviche and a lot of onions and sweet plantains and was overpriced. The anticucho was a  very small stick for  $6 . Also they are not family friendly because they don't have food for kids and we asked to our waiter if is possible to cook just rice with fried chicken for my niece. Fortunately they cooked but they gave us a small portion and charged us $16 + taxes of course. About the taste of the food, was good and the service also good.
About the drinks also are overpriced and served in a small cup.
This is not a traditional peruvian restaurant.  The menu is really small. For me, this restaurant is more like a bar and for order some app but not a restaurant for a dinner.
Best Peruvian food in NYC pricy but worth every penny. Love sitting by the kitchen and see our food being prepared.

Love Llama Inn! Food and atmosphere are excellent! If you plan to go Thurs-Sun definitely make a reservation and plan to have drinks at the bar before even with a reservation.  It's very popular because it's so delicious!

If you want horrible service this is the place to go.  Food delivered by someone who absolutely stunk from cigarettes.  Did not even wash her hands!   And charged for a drink I did not have, without any apology whatsoever.  Deserves no stars.

The llama inn has a lovely decor with vines and plants lining the windows that frame a warm central bar. If only the food was up to par. Antecuchos are Street food skewers in Peru, but overpriced over-chewy over-sauced dishes here. The quinoa banana salad had a nice texture, but lacked any sort of depth. You go to get Peruvian small plates, you leave craving Peruvian street food, for a couple dollars from a cart on the side of the road.

I'm writing this review late, so my memory isn't great, but I'll write about the two things that stood out.

Came here for brunch, food was really good and original.

The place desperately needs blinds. We were seated in a booth next to the window and the sun was shining on us the entire time so not only was it annoying in our eyes but it was really, really warm and very uncomfortable to the point beads of sweat began forming on my forehead. We brought it to the attention of our server and she said something like "oh yeah that happens this time of day but it's only during this time of day that it's a problem." I wanted to say yeah well it is that time of day and it is a problem so why don't you install blinds to fix it? Brunch is one of Llama Inn's things and this is a problem during brunch so you should fix it!

I'd go back for dinner, and I'd go back for brunch with a reservation to not sit in one of those tables.
The service and food were spectacular. The flavors of the food were so delicious that I could eat this food every day.

The decor and atmosphere was great inside and had fantastic music selection playing throughout. The restaurant however was out of two of the three large entrees that we had hoped to order for our meal, as well as one of the wine bottles we had tried to order. With a small menu, and three things we ordered that we were unable to get, this place did not live up to expectations. The food was tasty, but for what you pay you can get just as delicious a meal for less than what you pay here (and with all menu options available) somewhere else in NYC.
The food, atmosphere, and service is amazing!! Best ceviche I've ever had! Highly recommend to anyone in the Brooklyn/Manhattan area that likes South American cuisine.

The grilled cheese had a fabulous cheese blend on very good bread. Went nicely with the chips-also the perfect amount of food. Honestly was a good lunchy thing to eat at brunch time; sometimes you get something too lunchy and regret it. I would eat this again FOR SURE. Also it's so beautiful in here, greenhouse-like and sophisticated.

This place is for meat eaters! Vegetarians, know that there are only four small plates you can order here (they take the bacon out of one.) They are tasty but not very filling and not worth the price. They all feel like salads. The service is great and the cocktails are great. The ambience is cool as well, just wish there was more flexibility with the menu.
another great brunch today. took 3 friends to enjoy this splendid eatery. got the chicken and donuts again.

I've been here before for brunch. It was a while back when they opened November 2015. There aren't as many options for brunch as dinner, but I recall that everything I had was delicious. The chicken thigh sandwich in particular was outstanding. I probably owed this place a review back then, but I forgot. Sorry!

Since then, Llama Inn has been on my mind. When my friend suggested going to Pio Pio, I immediately thought of Llama Inn. Needless to say, it was impromptu so I couldn't get a reservation for three. I spoke to the manager on the phone and he said that certain areas of the restaurant are first come, first serve. Moreover, since I was coming at 6pm, I shouldn't have an issue. He was right. When we walked in, the place was virtually empty. 

We wanted to sit by the kitchen. It's an awesome experience to watch them cook. Unfortunately, the hostess said that area was reservation only. Fast forward a bit...we had amazing chicken thigh anticuchos, ceviche and a beautifully brined and roasted chicken. 

The service...concierge customer service barely begins to describe our waitress, Elisa.  I never even saw the bottom of my water glass. She was so attentive and ran through every item on the menu. She was spectacular. 

Good food and good service isn't quite 5 stars. It's that extra special bit that really does it. And here's where it comes in. I spoke to some people who were sitting by the kitchen and found out that it wasn't reservation only. Naturally, I felt slighted. The manager personally came over to the table to chat and apologize for the misunderstanding. He comped dessert and gave us his card so we would definitely be set up nicely in the future. I've been in situations where managers have been dismissive. It was a perfect close to the evening to have great food, a wonderful waitress and a restaurant manager that makes the extra effort to ensure his patrons have a lovely dining experience. Thank you, Lama Inn!

Excellent meal with great service, although definitely not cheap.

Came to meet up with a friend who lived close-by for dinner. The place was definitely lively and packed, even on a weeknight. There's seats you can take around the central bar, stools along the window, and also some booths and tables as well. We opted for a seat at the window. We started with the Llama Del Rey which was a delicious drink - kind of like a fancy sangria. If you can drink more, can opt for a pitcher of the stuff as well.

Food wise, we went with the following:

Quinoa: Delicious and flavorful, but it was a tad bit on the heavy side (maybe it was the banana in there?). Serving size is pretty decent, and can be easily shared amongst two people

Fluke tiradito: Loved this dish. Served slightly chilled/room temp. Very bright tasting, fish was fresh. Simple but nice depth of flavor (if that's possible). Recommend this for sure.

Beef tenderloin stir fry (Lomo Saltado): the pièce de résistance of the meal. $56, but easily fills up two people. The meat was cooked perfectly, and was so tender and moist. When you get close to finishing your meal, they come by and dump rice on your plate to sop up the sauce - def a nice touch. Highly recommend.

Ambiance is great. Dim lighting at night, exposed kitchen, large windows, nice greenery. Service was friendly and attentive. We spent a good chunk of change on the meal, but all in all had a great time. Would definitely come by again!

What a gem tucked away in Williamsburg! The vibe is on point, and the food is incredible! Not to mention the ahhmazing service:) The quinoa salad and chicken pot pie were some of the best dishes I've ever had .. I can't wait to go back!
Terrible services. There were 20 tables available and they didn't want to sit us any where other than the bar! Seems like a pretty racist spot!

Went back to this place for the second time tonight. Enjoyed my experience, but the meal wasn't quite as mindblowing as I remembered (though the vibe was just as hip!)

Sweetbread w/ chimichurri -- off the anticucho menu; charred just the right amount and the chimichurri sauce was chunky and flavorful

Corvina Ceviche -- delicious!  appreciated that the habanero was not overpowering. topped with crunchy plantain chips and w/ sweet raw plantain slices were both nice surprise additions to their take on a more traditional ceviche (Note: they also have a fluke ceviche with gooseberry, ginger, etc which I wasn't feeling quite adventurous for) 

Rock Shrimp Paella -- this dish was "a waste of time" as my 24 year old cousin bluntly put it. (she has a more sophisticated palette than most millennials, I swear). The dish was topped with red onions that were pickled and very acidic; they almost tasted like leftovers from the ceviche.  Also, disappointed in the misleading name -- as the amount of shrimp was very much lacking and instead there was a surplus of mussels and breaded calimari

Whole Roasted Chicken -- definitely the highlight of the meal, and the only item I repeated from my first time. Cooked to perfection, simple, delicious peruvian chicken. Topped with crunchy home fries that were SO good -- crispy and perfectly seasoned w/rock salt and possibly some garlic. Served with 3 sauces of varying spice degrees. YUMMMM. Also FYI this used to be on the menu full time but is now only available on Sunday or Monday!

No drinks or desserts this time because we obviously already over-ordered for two! Piggin' out together since 1992

I went in there with high expectations and was satisfied with the food, décor and epically service. The lobster was amazing especially with the melted cheese along with the lomo for two amazing stuff. The pisco drinks were good, little pricey for no reason but whatever. Only confusion/misunderstanding I had with the waiter was I wanted a traditional ceviche mixto or whatever came close to it. The waiter I guess misinterpreted my request and brought me out a different ceviche that was similar to a soup than anything else LOL no complains just not what I wanted.

Had another incredible meal here last night, really made us wonder why we don't come here regularly, though it is a little pricey. 

We have not had any misses over the course of two meals. This time around we skipped the quinoa salad and tiradito, though both are excellent starters.

We had the Corvina Ceviche and two anticuchos to start. The corvina ceviche is delicious, best ceviche ive had, with a very drinkable fish jus as gross as that sounds. Thin fried plaintains on top and the raw sweet plaintains underneath the fish are a nice twist. All anticuchos are highly recommended, though I'd avoid the sweetbreads if you haven't had them before.

The beet salad is very simple but delicious, with some crushed nuts, gooseberries and onions to provide a change of texture and flavors. It was a nice palette cleanser.  

I was leaning towards the short rib but we went with the seafood and rice dish, and I'm glad we did. Not initially a ton of seafood, but hidden in the rice and tomato broth were shrimp and mussels, plus a few bunches of fried calamari tentacles on top to provide some crunch. 

We had the lime pie for dessert, and it's out of this world good. Coated in a thick layer of burnt merengue, its a simple yet inventive take on a classic dessert, id say skip the picarones for this but understand if you choose to go for the donuts. 

Overall great place, for a special occasion you can get out of here at around $150 with the a lot of food and 1-2 drinks each. A regular weekday meal I'd expect to spend less. cocktails are good though many are on the sweeter side for me. Would like to try a Peruvian beer next time, and I am dying to try the large format Branzino and Lomo Saltido but would want to be in a party of 3 to take one of them down. I'll be back very soon and often.

Food Nazi - take two.   Jerry Seinfeld would have had a kick had he visited this restaurant. Of course, provided, he would make it past the host at the door who seems to take cue from the famous Seinfeld's episode. If you still didn't loose your appetite after getting a healthy dose of abuse and rudeness from the host, then good luck with the food. We couldn't.

THIS IS NOT A RESTAURANT. This is a bar that serves over priced appetizers. You're better served going to a nice tapas place like CATA instead. Do you like steak? How about paying $56 for 6-7 small pieces of beef tenderloin smothered in a mountain of fries, served with 8 scallion pancakes and topped off with under cooked rice at the end? Everything up until the entrée came out was pretty good. We expected the place to expensive, but we enjoyed the 2 skewers we had (squid and chicken thigh). We were told they had a special tonight, and their special was a GROUND BEEF EMPANADA! That's it! That was the only special!?!

The drinks we had were good, but they were $12-$14 for small cocktails. The décor was ok, but the bar is huge. Small tables line the windows because there is simply not enough space to seat big parties. 

The server came over to our table to ask how things were, and I said everything was pretty good up until the entrée. We had some serious issues with it. He said your problem is my problem and I will get the manager to come over and help.

The pretentious manager came over to try and explain it was high quality beef and how the chef butchers it himself. Great, but you can't tell me if the beef is grass fed? Organic? Wagyu? Angus? She kept repeating herself about the quality of the beef, but couldn't give specifics. Look at the menu, the first ingredient of the dish is Beef Tenderloin...shouldn't that mean the main portion of the dish is beef? She started to explain the dish was Lomo Saltado...I cut her off. I've had Lomo Saltado many a times and if this what they think Lomo is, or if the chef is Peruvian, then they should be ashamed. She started talking about the chef's vision and the ambience and how that is part of the price...Bitch, please. The chef's vision is to rip you off, and the ambience? Do you mean the view of the underpass of the BQE and row houses across the street? She left and the General Manager came over he explained that each dish is portioned out to 10-12 ounces of beef. I then asked him why is that not specified on the menu? (Because if it was, no one would order it!) They comped us the beef dish and brought out the short rib to appease us. We gave the wait staff a good tip because the service was good. They asked us to come again and we said we wouldn't.

As a Peruvian that grew up in Miami I've had my fair share of amazing Peruvian food from fine dining to hole in the wall.  I have a couple of spots in NY that I have frequented for my Ceviche or Lomo fill but nothing that really thrilled me and have always found myself craving a trip home to satisfy my craving...until Llama Inn came to the hood.  The Ceviche quality is amazing and full of flavor.  Their take on Lomo is not only unique but full of flavor and definitely the most tender, juicy tenderloin I've had in the dish.  Anticuchos are super tasty.  Rock shrimp dish is another fave.  Cocktails are on point and I can have my fill of chicha.  I've taken so many friends here and everyone of them have loved it.  Even my hard to impress Dad, who grew up on my grandmother's traditional Peruvian cooking, loved it.  I don't fully understand the complaints regarding pricing in other reviews.  For example, I've had the Lomo multiple times between 2-3 people and we are either STUFFED or have leftovers which works out about to less than $20 pp for a really flavorful, filling dish made with quality ingredients.  I've only been to brunch once here but it was AMAZE.  And all the big sunny windows filled with greenery make me super happy to be out of bed on the weekend.

Staff is always sweet and very accommodating and I love the overall atmosphere, it's relaxed and feels a little communal.  I kind of love sitting by the kitchen and watching the crew do their thing.  Music is always chill and often classic hip hop which is great by me!  

Bottom line, it's a great restaurant and a welcome addition to the neighborhood which I find lacking in quality Latin food. If you're looking for a cheap meal with less quality ingredients there are other Peruvian spots. If you have a more advanced palate and are looking for some next level modern Peruvian cuisine, go to Llama.

Excellent beyond words, truly. One of those meals where you have to close your eyes and ignore the people you're with for a few moments every time you taste a new dish just to savor every bite. We sat at the kitchen bar and watched as Chef Erik and his GM made sure every last detail was perfect before we were served. By their recommendation, we started with the ceviche, tiradito, anticuchos and lobster a lo macho, which were all fantastic. It was the lomo saltado, however, that left it hard to remember how great the starters had been. I had seen photos of this dish and decided we needed to try it during our visit to NY and wow, it was seriously one of the highlights of our trip. The beef was perfectly cooked, the sauce was so savory yet not too salty, fries crispy on the outside but soft enough to absorb the sauce and then they come and top it off with rice at the end to make sure you get every last drop... not to mention the awesome scallion pancakes which were just a bonus by that point. As someone born and raised in Miami, surrounded by a LOT of great Peruvian food, both authentic and up-scale, I am quite spoiled when it comes to this cuisine and this was still by far one of the best Peruvian meals I've had in my life. To top it all off, the service, the drinks and THE DESSERT (lime pie) were all equally excellent complements to the delicious meal. Thank you so much for an incredible experience, guys! Well done!

Everytime I go to NY and Brooklyn I eat an incredible meal every night and on my most recent visit I found the best experience lingering with my taste buds from Llama Inn. 
As a lobster lover their dish was delicious and full of flavor. Followed with the Lomo shared with a few friends. The Lomo was a delicious presentation with generous portions of steak and juicy onions. They finish it off with white rice to blend all the sauce and every last bit of flavor from the plate. I left with that most satisfying full feeling that makes me want to go back again soon!

I knew this was going to be a memorable meal when I first laid eyes on their llama mascot (who doesn't like llama's?). First off, you definitely need a reservation unless you don't mind bar seating. Second, go with a group because some of the portions are pretty massive, and the menu is so varied that you definitely want to try as much as possible. 

Skewers: cannot go wrong with any of these. My favorites were the pork belly and chicken thigh, amazing char and so much unexpected flavor packed into a little skewer. 5/5

Quinoa: not exactly a "vegetable" with its high ratio of grains to veg. Really fun and interesting mix with bananas and cashews. 4/5

Beef Empanadas: "the best empanada I've ever had" was spoken by 3 ppl at the table. Probably also the most expensive -- but maybe worth it? 4/5

Corvina Ceviche: I'm rarely a fan of ceviche, but I loved this! The liquid is so well-balanced with a good kick (I went back for several spoonfuls of it alone), and crispy plantains add great texture. 4.5/5

Rabbit Pot Pie: not too rich but tasted luxurious and the portion is smallish. I did miss a traditional flaky poof of pot pie crust, but the accompanying little biscuit sandwiches were a nice touch. The consensus for the filling was some kind of pate. 3.5/5

Whole Branzino: nice and rather elegant, I love whole fish. File under a "healthier" menu option. It is quite large, so best for serving 4+ ppl. 4/5

Beef Tenderloin Stir-fry: lomo saltado? fajitas? Sizzling beef? Doesn't matter really because it was so good. A skillet of asianized tender beef piled high with fries. Make yourself a scallion pancake taco and eat in bliss. p.s. they plop rice onto your finished skillet to sop up the sauce. 5/5

We tried 3 desserts, all of which were fine but unmemorable. 

Not sure how "traditional" it is, but the food is creative, big on flavor/texture, and executed nicely. Service is excellent and attentive, bringing fresh plates between courses. Highly recommend this restaurant for a group dinner -- you're gonna have a fun time at a place called Llama Inn.

Love!!! Best meal I have had in ages. Cool space, great design, nice staff and innovative delicious take on Peruvian cuisine. Quinoa salad was superb, Branzino was outstanding. From drinks (pisco sour) on, was amazing. Will definitely go back.

I went there with my roommate a few nights ago. We had the chicken anticuchos and the branzino fish, an order of pisco, and the ice cream-based desert. 

Excepting the ice cream, the quality and taste of the food was excellent. The ice cream desert was good. 

The food was slightly expensive for this neighborhood. 

My bigger concern is that the music was too loud. While you can hear the other person across from you talking, the music is too loud. And the music wasn't that interesting or particularly good. 

I'd recommend this place for those who don't mind a loud stereo and aren't looking for a super deal.

When you walk into Llama Inn one of the first things you see is a giant chalkboard hanging above the chef's counter. Written upon the chalkboard is the inscription "Food is symbolic of love when words are inadequate."  At Llama Inn you feel loved. Everything was excellent. The servers were swift and professional, the environment was trendy (but not overbearing), and then there was the food. I ordered the quinoa, civiche, chicken pot pie, and short rib. Each dish exceeded my expectations. I honestly cannot think of anything negative about this restaurant.

Came with a party of 5 for the brunch menu. Of all the sandwiches, I recommend the charred squid with aji amarillo.

The corvina ceviche was unbelievable. Fresh fish which paired perfectly with the sweet potato, which evened out the acid.
Pro tip: Take some of the left over sauce and pour into your beer.

Also ordered the swiss chard empanada, which was perfectly cooked inside and out. 
I'll knock off a quarter of a star for the lack of shades or curtains. I was there on a sunny afternoon, and the soon was pouring in directly onto my table, it felt like being in a greenhouse. 

But it makes that star back up for having gender neutral bathrooms.

What a major disappointment! This place is so overrated that I just don't even know where to begin!
Yes, the ambiance is fancy! Ok, that's a given. But the food's quality, authenticity, and - I wish this wasn't even something I have to mention but yes- QUANTITY are just not commensurate with the prices here. The ceviche is meager and not satisfying- and this coming from someone who's had a fair share of ceviches. The biggest disappointment was the Beef Stir Fry - it was probably 3 tiny meager pieces of meat covered by French Fries. I mean, really. $58 bucks for something so small and of quality below that of a random street vendor. It was just staggering - and the waiter has assured us that this is a great choice to share as a main course having had 2 apps. Nope. Unless you consider the French Fries your main course. I get that they're trying to "elevate" Peruvian food but besides their chic interior the food is just subpar. Really really pretentious and undeserving of the high reviews. I've been to many Peruvian places that offer much better quality- not to mention quantity- and were by far more authentic and felt genuine.

If I had to describe this place with one word it'd b OVERRATED. I had been trying to eat here for some time but there's always a wait. Very small menu with even smaller portions considering the prices but still tasty. Our waiter was very nice and knowledgeable. It's a cute place but quite smaller than I expected. Could be good for a nicer date but wouldn't recommend for friends &/or family. I probably won't be returning.

My wife and I eat out often.  This is one of the better restaurants we've been to in a long while and the service was extraordinary.  We had the ceviche/raw dishes and whole fish and was highly memorable.  Highly recommend the restaurant.

Amazing food and amazing service, especially by the GM Alex. We had the branzino and a wood fired mushroom tamales type of dish, and the combination of flavors were really atypical and delicious.  I was starting to feel like most restaurants in Brooklyn, though great, were all essentially the same flavors, but this place breaks the mold with its flavors and spices.  And I can't say enough good things about Alex - you don't get that kind of service these days, where the customer actually comes first and they act as though it's a privilege to host you, and not vice versa.
Love everything about this place!!! Delicious food, gorgeous setting!!! Definitely want to come back and try dinner too!!!

Amazing Anniversary Dinner! Thank you Steven and Hector for all your suggestions! We truly enjoyed our evening! The dinner and drinks were a delight! The servicw was truly Superb! We thank you for helping make our evening unforgettable!

I loved my evening at Llama Inn. It was on a Friday night and for two we got seated right away at the bar on a Friday night. The place was packed and had a very fun vibe. The bartender responded to all of our questions. I got the Pisco Sour and it was delicious!! We ordered the pork belly anticucho, the quinoa salad and the short rib. They did forget to put the avocado in the quinoa salad but it was still delicious. We got a dessert, I remember it being delicious but can't remember what it was, the cocktails were too good. This place just has that energy and fun. Will go back hopefully again and again.
Went here with a couple of old skanky friends and we lost our shit, so so so good, we rolled out happy carbtastic! Rice and fries and pisco cocktails, heading back soon with my filthy pals.

Amazing food. Every single thing on the menu was absolutely delicious.

The space is soooo beautiful.
Good vibes and amazing food

Four starts only because of over priced items.

Llama Inn takes dining to another level in Williamsburg. Greeted at the door, the hostess was able to give my wife and I a seat along the window which gave us a great view of the restaurant. The decor with the addition of the plants added a homey feeling to the night. This restaurant unlike a lot has a open lay out so every time the flame got high in the kitchen it gave us excitement. Windows all around which makes me imagine the lighting during the day is great. Our waiter was one of the best we have had. Very attentive and explained everything we had questions on. My only issue was with the menu. I felt like some items could be lowered due to portions.

A few nights ago I visited Llama Inn to get some celebration drinks. The ascetics of this restaurant is spot on but my favorite thing about Llama Inn is the service. While I don't quite remember the name of our waiter I can say with certainty that he was exquisite. The only con in my opinion is the price for food.

I enjoyed this restaurant.  The food was very tasty.  I had the quinoa salad and the chicken and pork skewers.  All was very tasty.  They were very nice and gave us an appetizer on the house which was a grilled and fried calamari.  The interior was very nice.  We sat at the chefs table so it was fun to watch them cook.  It is a bit pricey; not your usual inexpensive Peruvian.

I have heard that Llama Inn is really good for some time now and finally went in. It is one of the best meals I have had in a while and I can't wait to go back. We started with the squid, sweetbread, and pork belly from the Anticucho section and all were so delicious--These are small bites on skewers.  We then had the octopus ceviche-- One of the best ceviche dishes I have ever had. It was great. Get it. From there we had the beet dish and humita/mushroom dishes. They were both excellent--So tasty. Lastly, we had rock shrimp entree-- It wasn't my favorite dish, but it was still very good.

I thought the service was great-- Our waiter was Peruvian and helped us navigate the menu. The drinks were also great-- I had a pisco sour and the Cumbia cocktail. Both were delicious. This will not be a cheap meal- It is definitely on the pricey side, but the food is excellent and I will be going back soon for sure.

I'd heard great things about Llama Inn, so it seemed like an obvious pick as my boyfriend and I were finishing up an afternoon of shopping in Williamsburg. We had no problem walking in right before 7 and were offered bar seats facing the window or the bar. We picked the window, and ended up staring at a boring concrete triangle; room-facing would be more fun for the people- and bartender-watching.

As some Yelpers have noted, the prices are steep for the portion sizes. My boyfriend tried to order an anticucho and a raw dish and was told it would be much too small-- upgraded to a main instead of the raw and still left hungry. I did a vegetable and main which worked because I wasn't too peckish. Would recommend 2-3 dishes a person.

I started with the beets, which was very on trend with beets served at least three ways: crisped, marinated, and pureed. The goat cheese was tangy, the gooseberries were sweet and tart, and the corn nuts added a nice crunch. Ultimately, however, I didn't feel like it came together as a salad. It was just a collection of disparate and interesting ingredients on a very #artisanal plate.

My boyfriend's pork belly was a perfect couple of bites. Highly recommended, but again-- just a couple of bites.

My main was duck sausage rice, hidden under a layer of leafy but sad-looking greens. I didn't love the presentation, but points for creativity? The "beer" listed on the ingredients list on the menu came through very subtly and pleasantly in the rice. The sausage itself was pretty greasy and fatty, coming off as generic and low-end despite the luxury ingredients.

My boyfriend enjoyed his short rib, and the meat was delicious and tender. The crispy quinoa chips were nice to snack on, but didn't make a lot of sense in the dish.

Maybe this was a case of poor picks on our part, but I didn't feel like Llama Inn knocked it out of the part. Menu needs some more rethinking, but the foundation is definitely there. It was all a bit like my salad-- solid components with lots of contemporary techniques and a defined point of view, but somehow it didn't come together. If you're going to go high-end and high-concept, the execution needs to be a touch stronger. This was really a 3.5 star experience, but rounding down for the price and the hype.

This is a beyond sexy space. Very concrete and grownup, with colorful handmade-looking touches. Drink menu looked on-point as well, but didn't imbibe. Service was a bit slow, but waiters were knowledgeable and professional.

I would come back to ball out on someone else's dime; big share plates, shared bites, and a few nice drinks look like the move. But as a casual but nice place for a date night, you may come away with a light stomach and light pockets.

this would be a great spot for a couple drinks and a few small dishes, or a weekend brunch-the light is really beautiful in the daytime. definitely recommend making reservations (looks like there's a lot of drama with seating).

getting seated was a little awkward but service was good! the only thing i'd change is you should probably avoid mentioning that your special on a monday night is usually only offered on weekends, because it makes it feel like you're unloading old food.

the seafood is fresh and the flavors are on point, for the most part. a little weird that they insist on calling miso "fermented soybean paste", especially with the amount of asian influence on peruvian cuisine.  we finished with the picarones, and regretted it immediately. we couldn't tell if the chancaca was just burnt or what but when we asked the server what the sauce was, the look on her face said it all. please do yourself a favor and get something else.

wish the prices were a bit more neighborhood friendly, since i'd love more peruvian food in my life, but i can't justify paying $80 after tax+tip for lomo saltado. but whatever, i'm sure there's plenty of people that can! maybe for a really really special dinner? for now, i'll stick to drinks and the smaller plates.

As a fellow Peruvian I was looking forward to dinner here with my wife.  The ambiance is very pretentious as well as their menu.  Service was good but they claim this is Peruvian food, yet they don't have any typical Peruvian food. It's a modern day twist on Peruvian food including some of the ingredients that Peruvian cuisine has but the dishes themselves are not flattering.  Portions are super small and they do not even carry the signature soft drink of Peru, Inca Cola.  I found myself yelling my conversation to my wife as well as here the people across from us and yelling their innocuous conversations.  The food is ok, but if you are looking for authentic Peruvian cuisine, this is not it.  Coco Roco in Park Slope  or Panca in the west village is another option.

i love their island bar, and the bar seating next to the kitchen. great ambiance ! The service was also nice their dinner menu was awesome i had the ceviche ( which was super fresh ) , a goat with crispt quinoa dish (the goat was also cooked to perfection ) im not really a fan for their brunch i had the lomo saltado, the chicken and waffles and also some pork dish. wasnt good ...but on the bright side their mixed coffee drink was amazing. overall skip brunch and def go for dinner !
Asa and his crew were amazing servers. The hype is real. The food is delicious and I can't wait to come back.

Sad day for this place. Please if you are not of a certain ahem 'look' these folks are blind and won't see you even if you're sitting right in front of their faces at the bar waiting 5 minutes for somebody, ANYBODY to ask you what the hell you're doing there and what the hell you want. Smh. Damn shame. The day started out nice enough. I had heard great things and wanted to see for myself. By the time the characters behind the bar were done with their rude and mannerless shenanigans I wished I had just stayed home. The greeter at the door was nice and friendly, asked if I would be open to sitting at the bar. Yes of course I would,  it was just me I shouldn't be any trouble. Boy was I wrong. Sat at the bar fidgeting with my thumbs FIVE whole minutes yes I timed the tomfoolery before any of those jokers behind the bar paid me any attention- at that I had to make a pointed effort to make eye contact with the person who finally pretended to acknowledge my presence.Smdh.  I could tell you the rest but honestly the staff here are not worth that much of my precious time. They already took 20 minutes of it no refund for that ish, and by the time they were done being rude, staring at me while making disrespectful gestures to one another and making me feel uncomfortable just because i asked why no one tried to serve me for at least 5 minutes I sat at the bar, I eventually had to leave because the environment felt super hostile and no way I'm allowing those kind of.people access to my food. That was a one way ticket to some sort of food poisoning today. No I'm good. Keep your fancy brunch. I go down the street to another joint where I will be served with respect as I pay them my hard earned money. Never again needless to say.

A good friend of mine and I had gone to the MOFAD and were searching for a fun spot to go to dinner. I had heard about the Llama Inn before and was really excited to try the food. I love traditional peruvian food so I intrigued to see their representation of it. I also work for a concierge company so I am always on the lookout for places to recommend to my guests. We decided to sit at the Chef's table, which is always a great experience-However this was not. 

First of all, We sat down and the chef (or cook, not sure) started having a conversation with my friend and said he would make him "something special" since his favorite traditional dish was not on the menu. We ordered other entrees and that was a nice surprise that he was going to concoct something as a treat (seemed like an apology) The chef continued on talking with my friend and did not acknowledge me AT ALL. He gave my friend pieces of squid to try and completely ignored me. My friend seemed to think maybe it was a cultural thing, as in he was not acknowledging me because I am a woman. UMMM, Not acceptable. Did i mention that I was paying for the dinner? It was my friends birthday so I decided to take him out to eat. This place aint cheap either! That whole experience left me with a bad taste in my mouth. 

We got a few apps, entrees and a few drinks. For entrees, We got the beef tenderloin ($56) and my friend got the Short rib ($24). The tenderloin is a modern depiction of the lomo saltado, which was good but they decided to bring the rice when we were done eating (which they mentioned traditionally comes after the dish has been brought to the table) A little too late though, it was like 15 min later. 

To me, service plays into the "experience" and I did not feel too good about Llama Inn. I don't think I'll be coming back here. Especially paying $150-200 for dinner, you would think people would treat you with respect.

Visited this place last weekend, and we LOVED it! I had never had Peruvian cuisine. The quinoa salad and the skewers were delicious. The cocktails were also very creative. Our waitress was nice, and it was an all around good experience. Will go again if we're ever in Brooklyn!

This Peruvian spot was a favorite of restaurant review site The Infatuation for quite some time and I finally got to check it out. After a visit, I get why they were so in love with it. The décor features llamas, not in pajamas, and what is apparently the apotheosis of Peruvian art, string sculptures. It's cooler than it sounds. The cocktails are the best place to start and what a start they make. One simply must try the Llama del Rey based on the name and the fact that it is on tap alone. It stands up to the ballsy name. The food is also off the charts. The skewers of meat make for great shared dishes and if you order enough, you might get to watch the cook incinerate himself in the open kitchen. The small plates like the octopus and mushrooms are flavor explosions on a plate. The big dishes are harder to figure out, bit if there are at least two of you, you absolutely must try the beef pancakes which are like fajitas but way better. Prepare for argument's over who has more pieces of the succulent and flavorful meat. It's that good.
One of my favorite spots. Go with a friend and share the lomo saltado.

Wanted to try Peruvian food when we stayed in Brooklyn back in February and I'm so glad we found this place for our first night. We were a group of six and made reservations without any problems. The restaurant itself is very open, airy and the ambience inviting. Service was great and our server helped us pick out our drinks. We all loved the cocktails we ordered but the real winner was the food.  We haven't had Peruvian food in a long time, and the flavors of all the food just blew us away. We did family style and this is what we ordered: 

Anticucho
-Pork belly, chicken thigh, and squid. 5/5
It came out on 3 skewers and tasted amazing so we ordered another set. Pork belly was the favorite around the table. 

Raw
-Corvina ceviche 4/5 
Extremely fresh and delicious. The spice in this dish was not overbearing and tolerable especially for my spice sensitive friends. 

Fish and meat
-Rock shrimp, clams, mussels, squid Paella 4/5
Lovely dish, had the right amount of spice and the seafood again was fresh. 

Large
-Whole branzino 5/5 
This fish was freaking amazing. It was seasoned to perfection. The sides that came complimented the fish beautifully. 

My only qualm with this place was the pricing of the food especially with the amount of food that was given. Other than that, if you got money to burn, come on in.

Llama Inn
NY BK Willy B
6:30pm Wednesday
Four Stars

On this beautiful afternoon in Brooklyn, we sat the bar on a shady rooftop at the Llama Inn. We drank whiskey and wine and snack on some expensive but delicious food. We started with sweet bread and Head on Shrimp Skewer. Both were smoky and delicious. nothing better than shrimp brains. The pancreas was velvety. Next we had their Octopus Ceviche which thin sliced, tender, and flavorful. The avocado and citrus completed the dish. We finished with the $80 steak platter. The meat was med rare, the peppers were blistered and the scallion pancakes were delicious vehicle for everything on the plate. After you finish the pancakes they give you surprise rice to soak up all of the flavor on the cast iron. The service was top notch and whole experience was enjoyable.

I organized a birthday dinner here in May, and our guests are still talking about how enjoyable the event was. The staff was incredibly accommodating of our large party - the food was delicious, varied to fit everyone's preferences and served in ample portions. The ambiance made us feel as if we had left NYC, if only for the night. Cocktails were out of this world. We will be back!

The food was okay, but the portions sizes are so ridiculously​ small and expensive for what you get that I cannot recommend this restaurant.  Too bad, because the room is bright and pleasant enough.  The appetizers are particularly minuscule.  When I discussed potion size with our waitress, she call them Manhattan portions.  i don't know what that means, but it almost comical, except that it isn't

The wife and I were looking for a quick bite before a show and this was the perfect find . 

We had recently returned from South America , so naturally a Peruvian spot seemed like a great pick . Luckily our instincts proofed right as everything here was perfect .

The service was outstanding , and the seafood rice and charred octopus civiche were a dream . We washed them down with their pisco sours which were honestly as good as anything we had in South America . 

All in all a great , beautifully designed place with stellar food and service to match . If you're in the neighborhood don't hesitate to visit .

Wow. Wow wow wow wow wow. Although the cost per bite was pretty high (all of the dishes were pretty tiny and the prices pretty high) it was worth every penny.

It's rare you go to a place and find that every dish is on point, but Llama Inn delivered.

There are several small bites sections of the menu, split up by meats, ceviche, veggies and starters. The small bites sections will be enough for a couple of bites each while the starter section is literally one massive bite, or two-three individual bites. There's also a "large" section that has a full fish and a big stirfry- we didn't opt for one of these but they likely would be good portion sizes.

For a table of four, our waiter suggested a large and then 2-3 smaller plates, or a mix of smaller plates. We opted to do more of the smaller plates and ended up with the mushrooms, fluke, short rib, duck sausage and a special seasonal salad that they were doing. We also got one of the pork belly small bites, which was just a bite. 

All of the dishes we were literally scraping the bottom of the dishes to get as much as possible. I would say for our group as we weren't starving this was an ok amount of food, but I would say you would probably need to make sure you had 2 small dishes per person to make it a full meal. 

I hope they change their menu up from time to time so that there's always new goodness to sample!

We came by at 9:40pm to have dinner and the 2 hostess said they were done serving food. Yelp says they close at 10. Was very disappointed have been really wanting to eat here and it's my only night off this week. Such a shame
