As soon as I tried Llama Inn for the first time, I made a mental note of all of the occasions in which I would be planning to return. It's surprisingly rare to find a place like this: takes reservations for brunch, plenty of seating, excellent ambiance, and brunch food that goes above and beyond your typical Benedict and French toast. I have yet to come for dinner, but I hear it's equally delicious so I'll be back at night, too. 

So far, I haven't had a dish I didn't like. Among my favorites: 
- quinoa salad (sounds a little boring on the menu but trust me)
- beef tenderloin stir fry (it has french fries and bananas in it, that's all you need to know)
- avo toast (another one that doesn't sound the most original but the mushrooms on top make it)
- French toast (ok I know I just said that French toast at brunch is boring, but it's perfect to share a little sweet bite with the table)

Great service, awesome natural light, lots of plants, great decor, and yummy drinks, too - this place is an all-around winner. Can't wait to come back for dinner!
One of the best, most interesting dinners! Packed with flavor. Peru-Japanese success. Great pisco cocktails. Hip spacious bar!

I'd actually give this place 3.5 stars.

Went here last week Friday. First I want to comment on the decor which was a combo of desert/Latin modern minimalism (idk anything abt interior design... just a guess lol) and the wealth of plants and fun fabric art to add a pop color.
Our waiter was very attentive and knowledgeable about the menu and culture of the food. We ordered the octopus ceviche, the duck sausage with cilantro rice, and the "Peruvian" take on paella. I will say that the food is a little overpriced for the portions. The octopus ceviche was good the best part was my bite of crunchy squid and charred avocado. The duck sausage dish was ok ... just wish there was more meat for a price point of $24. The paella inspired dish on the other hand had plenty of seafood but the rice in both dishes reminded me of the boxed yellow rice by Goya or Zatarains... That aside the meal was satisfying enough. 

Overall it was a good experience, I just wish they had more options on the menu (more specifically ceviches). I prefer more traditional Peruvian food but I would come back to try the shared dish and anticuchos.

This place has a cool concept with the Peruvian inspired dishes, however my Peruvian Puerto Rican friend I brought here said nothing really reminded her of authenticity except the Beef Tenderloin Stir Fry. Her mom use to cook something similar. I felt bad because her mom said NY has the best Peruvian food in America. Perhaps I didn't research it enough because I just looked for what was around. The place is pricy for what you get. We tried two of the skewers as a starter (octopus & pork belly) and they don't have much on the skewer. I don't see it on the yelp displayed menu, but we tried the corn dish as well that was good, a little sweet. We got a few cocktails, only one friend tried a signature cocktail and it was okay (can't remember the name). The service was okay.

Went here for dinner last night. Vibe and ambience is great. I love the large windows and the layout of the restaurant with the window seating, central bar, open kitchen with counter seating, and small tables. The decor is nice and modern. It's a great date night spot. I'm excited to return for brunch to see the plants/decor in daylight. I enjoyed my senorita spritz cocktail with gin, and my boyfriend enjoyed his Peruvian beer. Favorite dishes were the charred octopus ceviche & the lobster. I wish the lobster was easier to remove from the shell, but this dish was delicious! I think it could be better if they added a few more pieces of bread to soak up that delicious sauce. For the large course, we ordered the beef tenderloin, which is supposed to be their take on lomo saltado but I think it could have used a little more salt and A LOT more meat (especially for the price of $60). This dish came with a bunch of thin scallion pancakes that you use as tortillas to make little tacos with the beef tenderloin. Love this idea! It was great until we realized we only had enough meat to make 3 or 4 tacos. Then the rest of the dish was just fries, onions and the scallion tortillas - sorry, llama --3.5 stars for this beef tenderloin dish :/  I think if we come back for dinner, we'll order more anticuchos to share and maybe the branzino (hopefully it will be meatier than the tenderloin). Other than the tenderloin dish not having enough meat, I thought that the service was really great. Glass was never empty and drinks and food came out fast.

The reason visited Llama Inn is because its owner was Eleven Madison Park's sous chef. Because of this, I expected excellence, and that's what I received!

I came for brunch. Let me start off with my favorite dish now that it's fresh in my mind. The corvina ceviche. Out of this world! My boyfriend and I tried a variety of dishes for brunch and this was totally the standout. The surprising crunch of the corn made the ceviche that much better. It gave the ceviche texture and great flavor. Amazing!

Another standout was the fried chicken thigh. It had a sweet, savory honey sauce that my boyfriend and I couldn't get enough of. The Brioche French Toast was delicious as well as the flan. All in all, this is truly the best Peruvian food I have had so far!

As far as the ambiance, big windows allow light to flood the dining space. Along with hanging plants lining the edges of the restaurant and a big art piece on the back wall make this place such a fun and great place to have lunch or dinner dates. The staff was so friendly and kind too!

The only reason Llama Inn didn't receive a 5th star is because upon receiving the check, we were told that they didn't accept cash as payment. That was very strange since after a few minutes of wondering why, the waitress returned and said they could accept the cash but they preferred card payments. 

Aside from that, I will definitely recommend and revisit Llama Inn. I can't wait to try the dinner menu!

Had dinner with a friend and it was delicious! I'd recommend getting 2-3 appetizers to share as the portions are on the smaller side. We had the sweetbread, chicken and pork belly to share and it was great, just wish there was more of it. For the main dish, I had the lobster (BEST ever hands down!!) which more than made up for the small appetizers. I appreciated the fact that it wasn't messy and I was able to smoothly take out the lobster meat out of its' shell. The pina collama (a take on pina colada w/ pisco sour) was delicious as well as the chicha morada. Will definitely return for another meal!

My first time trying Peruvian-inspired food and I was impressed!

My friends and I made reservations for a Monday night dinner and were seated promptly. Atmosphere was dim and quaint. Good for a romantic, classy evening. The bar was a nice centerpiece to set the vibe.

Our server did a great job explaining many items on the menu and making recommendations. He was easy to talk to and made our evening very pleasant.

For starters, we went with skewers of pork belly and squid. The pork belly skewers literally melted in your mouth. SO GOOD. Squid was chewier than expected. Wish there was more. Each skewer had about 4 small cuts. We also shared the charred octopus ceviche with crispy squid. I've never had octopus so tender. I'm a huge seafood lover so I could have eaten that dish as an entree. For our main, we decided to share the beef tenderloin stir fry. Absolutely delicious. Basically it was tender steak served with french fries and a creamy savory sauce. If you enjoy steak and potatoes, this is on another level. At the end, they also bring out steamed rice for you to mix in to finish with the sauce that's been left over. 

With the above shared dishes and several drinks, our group of 4 spent about $45 per person. More on the expensive-side but we left satisfied. Definitely worth venturing to.

I am almost at a loss for words for this place. This was literally the most disappointing overpriced dinner I've had in yearssss. We spent an embarrassingly high amount of money on such underwhelming food and even smaller portions. It took ordering practically the entire menu for the 4 of us to get full and those skewers were just a joke at $6 to $8 a pop for literally one BiTE of food on a toothpick. The broccoli side had like One sad piece of broccoli we were all  Cutting into tiny pieces to share LOL (also the theme of every portion)! Not one thing we ate was memorable, or even good and everything was overly salty. The only thing worse than the food was the bartender who made it a habit of being snarky with our questions and orders while we waited for a table. He curtly corrected me on how to pronounce a wine name (and not in a cute or funny way) and the white wine was warm and served in this super lame water type glass which really no one who likes wine enjoys drinking out of. The whole fish was the only thing we enjoyed (kind of- it was overcooked and no longer flaky), but at $60 for it, it should've had gold stuffed inside. I really found this to be everything pretentious I hate in a restaurant scene and lacked charm, flavor and pizzaz. Also, the decor was great but we couldn't even enjoy it bc we were pouring sweat (hello AC in the summer?!). Do not waste one cent of your hard earned money on dinner here. I would say to sit at the bar for the amazing ambiance but the bartender will just suck the joy out of that too.

I'm sorry to say it was an affront to eat here because I felt ripped off by the prices (over 300 for 4) the tiny portions, eh service, food and bad overpriced wine. The portions were so micro-sized that the waiter said for each appetizer, we should order two. The place is designed as a rip-off establishment and I've had much better high-end Peruvian cuisine. The atmosphere with the rooftop dining and lovely space below is the one thumbs up for me. If money is no object, you may enjoy the Lama Inn.

Wednesday night, the place was buzzing and inviting. The food was also very good. However, I am giving it 3.5 stars for two reasons:

1) In an expensive, more up-market, Manhattan style restaurant with table service, I expect good customer service. The tables were full so the hostess proposed to us the option of eating at the bar, which we accepted. However, there was only one bar stool so my friend had to go searching for a second stool whilst the bar men just looked on and did nothing to help and the hostess had gone elsewhere, despite having clearly seen that we were missing a seat. In a normal bar, this would obviously not have been an issue, but in a restaurant where you pay not only for food but for service, I expect a bit more of an effort.

2) The first part of the menu is the "Anticuchos". There are about 4 dishes in this section and although I did not know exactly what they were, they were all about $5 so I was expecting something relatively small. We ordered the shrimp and the pork belly. When the shrimp arrived, it was literally ONE, TINY 2 INCH shrimp! Not even a jumbo or mid-size! Whilst I am well experienced in NY restaurant prices, I was shocked and rather insulted by this offering. It was ridiculous. Offer two shrimp at least or tell the people ordering what to expect so that they don't order it! This little shrimp put me off frankly. I don't want to go to a restaurant where the chef or management team or whoever makes the menu decisions/prices thinks  that they can rip people off in such a astronomical way! Shame on you
Amazing find for a sunday brunch ! Eat on the rooftop if available, very cute and excellent service. Lynlea is very hospitable and I'll certainly be back !

We went on a Friday night for our 1st anniversary dinner. The restaurant itself is very charming, the food is interesting although we didn't love it. I definitely liked the scallops anticucho and the shrimp anticucho ($8 for ONE shrimp!) but everything is way overpriced and to justify that they have an insanely attentive staff. 
I'm not even exaggerating when I say that the waiters were at our table checking, refilling, asking, cleaning and prepping every 30 seconds. Not a relaxing date for sure.

On top of that the place was really loud and I couldn't really hear what my husband was saying but I could definitely hear the people sitting at the tables next to us.

It wasn't a terrible dinner but it was intense, not the kind of leisurely dinner we were hoping for.

Awesome Williamsburg date spot with low lighting, attractive decor, big windows, sharable plates, and nice Peruvian cuisine. We went on a Saturday night, waited 15 minutes for no reservation seats at the bar. We started with the llama del rey sangria, with pisco, red wine, and rum, and the cumbia themed drink. The sangria was great, worthy of another round. The cumbia drink was also good. Many pisco options on the menu, too.

Food was the real crowd pleaser. The short ribs were excellent, tender, juicy, and lick the plate good. The pork belly anticucho was awesome as was the small choclo and cheese casserole. The quinoa bowl was the surprise winner though: with cashews, banana, a little crunch, and other surprises, it was a perfect dish that can restore your faith that something healthy can also be damn tasty. Nice work! The only drawback at Llama Inn is the price, dinner for two with one entree, three small plates and two drinks was $125 not including tip. Not out of this world pricey, but not 'let's go here regularly' prices either. All in all, a great dinner and beginning to a night out in Williamsburg.
great pisco sours and meat skewers. be warned- the meat skewers are quite small- get a lot! they have a roof and a great dining space

Amazing brunch here. I had the tamal dish and my friend had the Huacho sausage dish and shared. They were really delicious takes on those traditional breakfast meals, enjoyed every bite. The drink of the day was Peruvian paradise and it was like a passion fruit slushee spiked with pisco. I wanna go back and try the picarones and waffles with a bigger crew (because the dish is only available as a whole chicken). The servers weren't Peruvian or even spoke Spanish, which is usually a pet-peeve of mine, but they were so friendly and called me when I forgot my credit card. Yes, that happened. 

We ate on the roof, which was beautifully decorated, plus the weather was perfect. Food and drinks were just delicious. In brief, this was a much needed Peruvian breakfast spot.

Been here a couple of times but got to check out the rooftop finally last night! It's a small space that's typically overcrowded, but the long holiday weekend allowed some room to sit down. It was kind of a chilly night but they provided these cute, comfy blankets. Only had a couple of drinks but the service was
Pricey but super worth it get the $68 steak and fries with rice and pancake tortillas amazing
Great service and cocktails. The spot itself is also very nice. The food was ok, salty. The fries and plantains were delicious though.

A hidden gem in Brooklyn. Great service, nice South American wine list and tasty food. Only drawback is the lack of table seats. We dined on the countertops that frame the restaurant.

Skewers are fabulous, very tasty--scallops had a delicious sauce, chicken and shrimp were nice roasted and the pork belly was just right. 

Crispy quinoa app with bacon and banana was unique and tasty but would have been better with a lighter touch of the banana flavored sauce.

Star of the night was the Branzino--pricey at $60 but exceptional flavor with delicious accompaniments--scallion rice was great (wish we had more!)

Key lime pie was topped with a delicious meringue. Only complaint was when you ate the graham cracker, meringue and pie in one bite it ended up being way too sweet.

Look no further- you've found your dinner spot for tonight. We got here at 9:10 PM for a 9:15 PM reservation on a Friday night -- we weren't seated until 9:30 PM, but the hostesses were extremely transparent and communicative, and offered us a round of drinks on the house.

We sat on the roof which felt like an oasis in the middle of the Brooklyn. Our server Tyler was amazing -- he walked us through the menu, gave recommendations, and was very patient with our indecisiveness.

We started with the shrimp and pork belly skewers, moved to the cold quinoa veggie dish (AMAZING, it was like a flavor party in our mouths), and had the beef dish to share as an entree -- Tyler gave us a bowl of rice at the end to mix in with the leftover sauce and veggies. We ended the night with an ice cream dessert, also on the house.

Food is absolutely incomparable and service exceeded our expectations. Highly recommend!

The food was a fine 4 stars but the service really pushed it our visit to the next level. 

Visited on a thursday night with my wife and decided to have dinner at the rooftop bar. They did a great job of creating a nook, so to speak, in an outdoor area; hanging lights and leafy fronds through which you can catch glimpses of the resplendent underbelly of our beloved BQE.

White steamed quinoa and fried red quinoa punctuated with a few lardons was completely surprising and delicious. Recommend.

Octopus ceviche in a well balanced leche de tigre. Recommend. Order a couple piscos and do a leche de tigre back. Amazing.

Whole branzino with accoutrement was probably too much food for two but we weren't upset at all. Cleaned that guy off from cheek to tail. The soy fried rice is a great salty punch to the mild creaminess of the fish.

Key lime pie. Not that fake neon lime green here. Piped torched meringue was a nice visual change from the usual glob on top. Perfectly buttery cookie cracker crust. Pisco again. 

See if you can get your hands on some of their Peruvian corn nuts. Would recommend.

We had an absolutely gorgeous meal on their rooftop, at the community table. Beautiful roof with lots of plants and hanging lights and a little bar. 

The piña collama (lol) was fruity and well-balanced. For starters we had one each of the pork belly, sweetbreads, and scallops, all of which made my eyes roll back in my head.  They're small amounts of meat on a stick so if you're sharing, get multiples.  For main course, the short ribs, which were off the bone with beans and some sort of creamy sauce. The meat was like BUTTER.  For dessert I had the key lime pie with a buttery biscuit base and the most pillowy toasted meringue. To die for. I had not one critical thing to say about the meal (except a little "oof" at the bill but WORTH IT).

I've been to Peru many times and I was gladly surprise by the menu of this restaurant. I could easily say it is one of the top Peruvian restaurants in the country. Great variety in their menu, excellent drinks, very convenient location, great decor.. Brunch is a Must!!

Truth be told, I'm quite anxious to try the food at Llama Inn, so this review is strictly for everything but a meal. 

This dynamic duo stopped in Sunday evening for a drink. What really had us crazed is their rooftop - with fall on the verge of making its breakthrough, the weather was just about perfect. Even from the outside, the place has a cozy vibe and delightful decor. 

The main space is airy and the kitchen open to the floor. As you're walking up the steps to get to the roof, you have a great view into the kitchen, if that sort of stuff floats your boat. It does for me. 

The rooftop is so dang cute. There are a few tables along with one larger communal table and lots of greenery fills the space along with an outdoor booth in the corner. 

Although we only had a couple of glasses of rosé each, the service was great. My friend had asked our waiter if they had anything to snack on and of course he brings over the most fantastic corn nuts. Fan. Tastic!

Oh, and have I mentioned how sexy their rooftop bar is? 

I'm diggin' this place for sure.

Not a fan of Peruvian but this place may have changed my mind.  Very nice to be able to
Sit in front of the kitchen and watch them work and the food is as good as the work they put in. The corn grits are amazing and the ribs were very tender just a little fatty.  The key lime pie dessert was unreal.  Make a reservation as it gets really busy

Llama Inn has the best upscale Peruvian food I've ever had the pleasure of experiencing. 
Everything is fine-tuned, from the selections of ceviche, the anticucho (appetizer skewers), the main, and the large dishes. Not to mention, the fantastic cocktail menu and large selection of Pisco (of course!). 

If you're open to raw seafood, try the ceviche! No matter which one it is, it's always extremely fresh, with subtle flavors that tie into whichever raw fish is used in the dish. Save some of the jus (leche de tigre) to take as a shot with a shot of Pisco after you're finished! 
For the main, a group of friends and I always order the Lomo Saltado (the large steak and fries dish). The beef tenderloin is perfectly cooked, stewed like stir fry in a pot with onions and tomatoes, topped with french fries, with a side of scallion pancakes that act as tortillas, with sides of avocado, spicy pickled chilis, and their homemade spicy creamy sauce. It's mouthwateringly delicious, and extremely filling, so I recommend conquering it with 3-4 people. 

Looking for vegetarian? Their vegetarian dishes are unbelievably good. Hungry? Try all the vegetable starters!

For dessert, you can't go wrong with any of it. It's usually experimental and overwhelmingly delightful. It changes seasonally, but the Peruvian-style donuts are always a great go-to. 

The only thing that's missing is a better after-dinner hot beverage selection as their espresso is really not very good. But, who actually wants espresso after a heavy Peruvian meal? Crazy people. (Like me with habitual tendencies.)

Oh yeah, if you're not convinced by the food, the ambiance is wonderful. Beautiful and comfortable (which is a difficult feat to do both), lively plants surround the perimeter, a beautifully designed bar in the center, and an open kitchen with hard working, friendly and occasionally hilarious chefs. (The rooftop is also beautiful and comfortable-- how do they do it so consistently well!)

Really fantastic neighborhood place in Brooklyn and definitely worth traveling to.
Excellent small plates. We ended up ordering several seafood dishes (ceviche, grilled octopus, mariscos). Everything was super fresh. Also enjoyed the pisco on ice!!

Where do I begin?

Cool sceney space with fun vibe? Check.

Awesome roof deck that gets shade during the midday sun? Check.

Delicious food? Check.

Fun and tasty cocktails? Check.

That's enough checks to get this guy over to Brooklyn more often.

Everything on the menu--and I've had just about all of it--is fantastic.

And the drinks--wow--it's been a while since multiple drinks on the menu really blew me away, but this place really knows their stuff.

Overall, this is a great new spot worth the trek out to visit whether you're catching up with friends, dining with your parents, or going on a date. Food is delicious, drinks are outstanding, and service was impeccable. Definitely worth checking out.

First of all, the food is AMAZING! It's so fresh and prepared right in front of you. The drink options are creative and delicious. The service was impeccable. Alyssa was or server and it was some of the best service I've ever had! Thanks girl :)

This was a delightful find!  The food was creative, and very very tasty.  I enjoyed everything from a cool cocktail sort of like a margarita but made with quinoa and cinnamon, (sound odd?  It's perfect!) to sweetbreads with raisins and chimchuri..  we each had a starter, main course and desert, and drinks, and it was under 150.  I thought it was a bargain too.
Try the short ribs, try the key lime pie!  We sat at the counter watching the kitchen, and could have our own conversation and be part of the action.  A wonderful experience.

One of my favorite restaurants in Brooklyn. Great vibe pretty space wonderful inventive but still Peruvian food and amazing cocktails. I come here all the time and really love it! Oh and there's an outdoor rooftop with a bar snacks blankets and great music...what more could you want!?

I came in on a saturday for brunch. Vibes and space are cool. The food tastes good. My issues were that:

1-I asked if the brunch dishes were good for one person and were well served (i had an appetite but was not starving). The server said they were. Well...it was more of an appetizer size.

2-As soon as they brought the check they rushed me out the door. I still had half my coffee to finish and the place was half-empty so I didn't understand the hurry.

Tip:when your client signs the check just leave it there until they walk out. Or else it feels like you're pushing them out the door.

I hosted a birthday brunch here, and everything was perfect: they were great at accommodating my group, the food was flavorful and not your typical eggs Benedict (yawn), they were cool about serving a cake we brought in, AND! the lighting and plants are great to look at -- and even better for flattering photos.  All around win! Can't wait to come back!

I thought the quinoa fried rice was (surprisingly) excellent. It had a great combination of textures and flavors. The short rib entree was perfectly cooked and melt in your mouth delicious. The appetizer kebob things only come with 1 small bite-sized stick-- good but I would probably not order these again.

Overall, an expensive spot, but the servers and the hostess were wonderful and the food was upscale comfort food. 

Make reservations ahead of time, they always have a wait. We were quoted an hour and a half for Saturday night around 8:30pm.
Perfect for brunch ..... cool take on common meals turning steak and eggs into a plate of robust flavors and intriguing to every bite!

Delicious Peruvian food, but to top it off, amazing personable service. If you want a table, make sure to book a "Table". Otherwise, you will have to sit at a bar, even if you've made reservation.  I would recommend sitting at bar looking into kitchen. We've got to watch the chefs at work and even speak to them a bit!  Highly recommend.

Popped in here recently for a bite to eat. Very cool decor and atmosphere.

The beet salad is excellent, really really tasty. The small single pieces of chicken, pork belly, shrimp etc are very tasty but the price point is a little off here. They are prices between $4 and $8 for a small single piece of shrimp, scallop, chicken etc. They are very tasty but I think the pricing is all off. If you pick 3 of them you're up at over $20 just for a teeny tiny little taste of something. I'd expect something more substantial for the money but anyway, it is tasty but just the price model on this dish is off.

The wine glasses are HORRENDOUS! They are there terrible cups that children drink apple juice out of. Wine glasses are one of those things that should not be messed with. The tried and tested traditional wine glass is preferred by almost everyone and anytime I am in a restaurant that uses glass ware without stems it always becomes a topic of conversation that the place is trying too hard or over thinking it. Just give me a regular wine glass! Some of the wine options are not cheap so if I had ordered a $100 bottle of wine I would have sent it back and ordered beer or a cocktail instead. I couldn't drink good wine out of their glasses. No way.

All in all I like the food and vibe but there are definitely some improvements to be made....but proper wine glasses!

$70 for this food and wine below including tip...?
Dinner rules. Service was incredible, food was incredible, drinks were incredible. And if you're lucky enough to have Derek (sp? "Michael Cera") as a waiter, you're all set. 10/10 would again

Was here on Wednesday and had a great meal. So great that we booked for our parents who were visiting from out of town, just a few days later. 

Then, Saturday comes, and 2 hours before our reservation, they called us saying they overbooked and can't seat us any longer. No joke. 

Never rely on reservations you make here. They're bound to cancel on you. Good food, horrible customer service.

Ordered the omelette with fried rice and sausage which took quite a long time to get here and was luke warm. Was highly disappointed because it came with only four little pieces of sausage and far too much fried rice. The eggs were mediocre and very thin. The two stars are entirely for the atmosphere which is quite creative but can't make up for the food. I would not come back or recommend this place.

This is a happening place and rightfully so. The restaurant is laid out in a way that gives it a certain coziness yet with tables not too close to one another (a luxury in New York). 
But the real gem here is the food. 
Our large platter of beef tenderloin stir fry was the bomb. Juicy, succulent meat with fries. Large enough for the three of us. The anti-cochus were delicious. 
The ambiance is enjoyable. 
The table service was efficient and caring. 
I, however, was disappointed that they also revel in playing the universal game of keeping guests waiting even when tables are available. We arrived at 7:30 pm and were told that there is a 45 minute wait. After a little bit of negotiating we were seated at a table that had reservations for 9:30. This is ascinine. 
Anyway, overall a positive experience.

Jeez what just happened! Llama Inn was one of the finest meals I've had in 2017. Space was relaxing, we asked for chef's table and the vibe in the kitchen was extremely positive. There were like 7 or 8 professionals operating seamlessly in this open kitchen layout, focused on this ridic food and still laughing and warm and happy. Service was impeccable, our server was a pro salesmen. We ordered everything he suggested and each a sincere success, the special brined chicken was *outstanding* as promised take it from me avail on Sunday's Monday's I think he said. It was perfect dish after dish, quinoa veggie appetizer was crazy, corn mushroom was epic. We also each had two different pisco cocktails and got wasted and all four were excellent. I can't remember the drink names still buzzed sry. Those antiuchos skewers! We got shrimp and pork belly to start wow those were amazing too
Good food. Shared plates. Experimental and fun. Loud music and rooftop terrace. Check it out.

Cons: Limited number of tables. 30-min+ wait time for dinner even with a reservation. Lean menu and lean portions at a high price point. "Large" entrees not portioned to justify price tag. Rice accompanying these dishes tasted under-cooked. 

Pros: Beautiful dining area. Striking and lively bar area. Charming hostess. Delectable flavors. Delicious anticuchos and whole branzino. Concise menu speeds up decision-making.

The location and decor are very lovely. However there are a few things that irked me about this restaurant. 

1. I made a reservation online through some approved third party. When I got there they showed me to a window seating arrangement, I asked for a real table (since there were about 3-4 open) and they said no, that's only for customers who make reservations directly with the restaurant. Great, next time state that on your website clearly. 

2. While the food is tasty, the portions are ridiculously small. Don't come to this restaurant if you're expecting to be filled up with just dish (like in most restaurants). Overall the food felt like Peruvian food made for hipsters, not for Latin Americans. If you are Latin-American, don't expect any of the traditional flavors you love.

Had an absolutely amazing experience!

My friend made a last minute dinner reservation at this place and it got lost somewhere in transit. We got to the place around 7 and it was packed: only a few tables open waiting for reservations. The hostess and the manager (I believe her name was Kasha, I hope I got that right!) were extremely professional and accommodating and soon enough we were able to move to a table!
I was very impressed with the amount of attention we have received in this situation: by no means this lost reservation was their fault, yet the ladies figured everything out for us and made the dinning experience truly exceptional. 

Food and service were great, we enjoyed atmosphere and decor as well.

Next time I'm in Williamsburg I'd definitely come back.

At first, I wasn't too pleased at this restaurant the first time I went because of how we were treated, but this time things have changed. The service was great, not sure what the waiters name was but he was very detailed. There's no way I can ever eat Peruvian food again without only coming here, that's how good the food is. Beef tenderloin is pretty big for 2 people so don't get scared with the small portions of appetizers, cause there's a lot of food on the main course! Well worth it, will go plenty of more times!

A *creative* experience to say the least. I have absolutely nothing bad to say about any of the dishes we ordered. We all know the food is amazing here but let's take a minute to talk about the decor!

Llama Inn must have the best smelling bathrooms I've ever been in. I'm actually inspired to get whatever scent was in that bathroom and have it in my home. Whoever designed this place put thought into every. small. detail. The coasters, planters/water chillers, each lamp shade, abstract art on the walls, panels on the ceilings. I loved every bit of it and we couldn't help but sit back and enjoy the aesthetic of the restaurant. The attentive staff kept asking if we needed anything because we were literally just sitting there staring at how beautiful everything was.

Anyone who appreciates a great ambience will love this restaurant. Worth every penny.

Based on previous reviews we ordered the ceviche, skewers, and grilled short ribs. It seems like every time order something random it ends up being the sweetest surprise. Tonight was no different. The duck sausage rice dish was divine.

Great design, upbeat cool vibe, late dinner service (we arrived at 10pm mid week and the place was hopping), really great food, AMAZING attentive service served by a team of well functioning, friendly and professional young staff.  Will definitely be back.

Very interesting spot. Peruvian food with a pretty limited menu - they do take their food seriously and are very knowledgable regarding the dishes.
Price point is a bit high but if you're big on Peruvian it's worth it.
Vast selection of cocktails and wines.
Split a few dishes with my friend, the ceviche was our favorite. Also shared the short rib and beet salad and the lime pie for dessert which was probably my favorite thing.
Ambience and decor is really nice - I think they were burning palo santo in the restroom. 
I probably wouldn't come back only due to the limited menu however it is a cool place to check out or even go for a cocktail.

Wonderful food - selective menu. Real mixologists and even better Bar backs.    Our Bar back, hector, was the character of this Brooklyn hipster spot. Incredibly attentive and an incredible conversationist - he really kept us so happy up at the bar. Our bartender was a little more busy but he was so knowledgeable. His name was Spencer and he's as professional as any restaurant could hope to have for an employee. He threw out old champagne the minute he saw. I can't stress enough that he's a mixologist. Another bartender, Zach, got my tea which was awesome that there was a designated tea person but the experience was totally non pretentious. I really liked this place. Expect hipster Brooklyn.

Llama Inn, although a little pricey is well worth it! There is no other restaurant like this in New York with this style Peruvian food and unique decor.

 I had a few of the "street food" dishes and the shared platter with Steak covered in french fries and the most delicious tortillas on the side. The flavors were very memorable and even though by the end I was full, I didn't want the dinner to end.

Nice place! We had the fried rice omelet and the stir-fry beef (lomo salteado) for brunch, and everything was delicious. I removed the jalapeños from the top of the omelette as I don't enjoy spicy food that much.

We also had non-alcoholic beverages (Llama Side, Chicha Morada and Latte) and they were all pretty good.

We will try dinner here soon!

Flavorful modern take on Peruvian food in a big space with cute plants adorning the windows.

Happy hour is until 7pm with cocktails at $11, down from the original $15. Touch of Evil was delicious. 

Portion sizes are small except for the larger format dishes, but the server did an impressive job telling us exactly how many bites were in the smaller dishes. Between the four of us, we shared:

- Fluke ceviche with crispy plantain chips and soft plantains: delicious. I could've eaten this whole thing. 4 people basically shared 2 tiny pieces each.

- Pork belly char siu: one small skewer of delicious pork, a bit crispy on the outside and fatty goodness on the inside. Good size for one person or 4 ants.

- Grilled romanesco with fresh cheese - I'm not a big veggie person and found this to be so good. Good for sharing.

- Beef tenderloin stir fry: This dish was the star of the meal. Super tender beef in a umami-rich soy and oyster sauce with crispy fries on top and chive crepe, avocado and some mayo sauce on the side. The meat and fries are meant to be wrapped inside the crepe but the crepe ended up getting soggy from the sauce. Towards the end of the meal, the server brings rice and dumps it in the remaining sauce so you can lick it all up. It's pricy at $72 but can easily be shared between 4 people and is very filling. It can also be shared between 2 people if that was the only thing they ordered.

- Toffee bread pudding with cheese-flavored ice cream: delicious 

Overall everything was delicious and service was great. I just docked off one star for the tiny portion sizes.

Hands down, this place is amazing! The food was absolutely incredible. Tied for the best meal I've ever had. Everything we ordered was delicious. Plus, the atmosphere was really nice and our waitress was friendly.

This place is llama-zing!

If you're still reading, thanks. Llama in is absolutely worth a visit. It's got a hard-to-find combination of great ambiance and great food that makes it perfect for anything from a first date to dinner with your parents. We actually came here with a small group for NYE and had a great time -- their prix fixe menu was reasonably priced and delicious, and they stepped it up on presentation and threw in some fun party toys to amp up the celebration. 

I *almost* don't want to mention their adorable rooftop because it's adorable and tiny and feels like a little escape from the city and if too many people find out about it it'll ruin it. I should probably delete this sentence.

My sister has been raving about Llama Inn for a long time. Since I was pregnant I couldn't really enjoy a place like Llama Inn that serves Ceviche, it would be such a tease for me.. So finally, I gave birth and my sister hosted her birthday dinner here. The restaurant is really nice, I love the space, very open and warm. I am sure it's super bright during the day since it has windows all around. The drinks are delicious, one of the bartenders made a Peruvian style Moscow mule..it was really really good. I wanted to keep having more drinks but unfortunately I couldn't, my husband did enjoy the happy hour though. The food was really good, if you're not into spicy then i don't think you'd enjoy this place. Everything was pretty much spicy and hard to avoid. I love spicy so I enjoyed it every bit. I ordered the beef hearts, shrimp and they were delicious, a bit pricy for the portion but really good. For dinner, I shared the Bronzino with my husband, it was flavorful. We really enjoyed it. It came with a side of rice which I believe the portion is not enough if the Bronzino is meant to be shared. I asked for more rice on the side which they provided with no problem but it did not have the pieces of corn as they provided with the meal..I would definitely go back to this place and try some ceviche and some other meals and of course treat myself to a drink. Great place!

Llama inn is my favorite restaurant in Williamsburg. The decor is so cool and fresh (I wish my apartment looks the same!!) and the food is delicious. The ceviche, the quinoa salad and the empanadas are my absolute favorites. Main dishes are very good too - though quite heavy so better be hungry. Deserts are just delicious.

This is a restaurant I would go to again and again.  I looOved it here.  I had a 9:30 reservation and there were a little jammed up which can happen.  The tall pretty hostess was so cool she bought us drinks and even wanted to buy us a bottle of wine.  The food was amazing.  We had a mix of everything.  My favorite was the beef tenderloin but we also had the ceviche, the beets, the quinoa and the pork belly.  I forgot the deserts which was the lime pie and the chocolate desert everything was amazing!  I just ate there last night and I am going to take my kids there tonight that how much I loved it there.

I love the the decoration of the restaurant! Make you feel you are on vacation. Drinks here are amazing. Cevechi is delicious but portion is too small. Like the fried beef. Did not like the pork sandwich as much. Service is great!

This place was great!!! 

The food was great and the drinks were even better. I found this place on brunch boys Instagram and from the photos and their review I knew I had to come. The decor was super cute and the good vibes were there (If ya know what I mean). Totally recommend this place, there isn't a lot of places that have both great food and drinks!

3.5 stars. I came here expecting to be wowed, largely based on all the positive media reviews I had read. I found the reality much closer to earth.

We started off our brunch with the chips and dip - house made potato chips without particularly much flavor and some sort of yogurt dip. It was fine, but frankly I could have made it at home. We moved on to the beef stir-fry, which was good. It was very poutine-like, with French fries and a gravy-like sauce at the bottom. It did not strike me as anything particularly revolutionary, although the meat was cooked correctly and the onions had a nice flavor. The bread pudding, although quite small, may have been the best thing we ate. It was very simple, but done exquisitely well.

Why the relatively low rating? Service issues. I attempted to order the signature cocktail (the Llama Del Ray), only for the server to tell me they were "currently making a batch." That's fine, I said, I'll wait. The waiter clarified "it will be like 15 minutes before it's done." We had just sat down and had barely looked at food. "That's fine," I repeated. The waiter expressed he really couldn't sell me one. Could he recommend a similar cocktail, perhaps from their evening menu? (The brunch cocktails are quite limited.) The other brunch cocktail was kind of different but not toooooo different, he said after a pause. Could the bartender at least make me something with chicha? Maybe, he said, if it was something simple like a sour. Fine, I said. Not ten minutes later, a pitcher of Llama Del Rey arrived for the table next to us (who had been seated at the same time as us, but with a different waiter). Our waiter never apologized for what was clearly an incorrect assessment, or even asked whether I liked the cocktail he made up... or offered another opportunity to order a cocktail for the remainder of the meal. 

This is certainly not a bad spot if you're in the mood for slightly overpriced meat-heavy food. But the service puts a damper on the experience, especially at this price point. I doubt I'd return given the other options in the neighborhood.

It's the first review I write but I guess it's totally worth it.
I used to work in hospitality and it's nice to see that people are still doing their best to please the customers. 
In fact the service was outstanding, we had two very sweet bartenders taking care of us; and even the manager came a couple of times to check on us. 
The food " chef " was also delicious. Never had beef cheek before and highly recommend it.
So just a big thank you guys, and keep up the good work ! 

Margot

Yes, the portions are small and some might even say this isn't "traditional" Peruvian food, but as a fellow Peruana, I can honestly say this place is AMAZING! The food is on point, the cocktails are TO DIE FOR and the decor is perfection. I have been here for dinner and brunch a couple of times and I can't wait to go back!

Llama Inn is an INCREDIBLE dinning experience! Hands down the best food I've every tasted in my life! The customer service and dinning experience was out of this world! Highly recommend this to all! Special shoutout to the chef Merril and the waiter Ian!

Came here for brunch on Sunday afternoon. Wonderful waiter, the food was delicious (I had the "tamal, fried egg, shrimp, aji panca") and the space is welcoming with lots of plants and sunlight from all the windows.

Pretentious, overpriced, loud, poor service. I would not recommend the Llama Inn for groups or special occasions (they will disappoint). And, you will likely leave hungry! I'm very confused why people like this place. We had a reservation for 7:45 and waited until 8:30 to be seated. We were told we had to put in our order for everything at the same time (not sure why...). We did what we were told and still didn't get all of our food by 10:30. We were about to walk and just pay for what we had eaten (a handful of smaller plates), when they suddenly decided it was time to try really hard to please us. It took my friend speaking to the manager and the threat of our departure to suddenly get wonderful service. Not a great strategy. My poor friend kept apologizing, because she had taken us here to celebrate an engagement and a birthday. Certainly not her fault! There's really nothing interesting or unique about this place. The city has so many lovely gems, but this isn't one of them.
Wow, bomb food, beyond amazing and friendly service. Great mixologists and fun staff. Kitchen is super experimental with there flavors and they nail it everytime!

Such a great spot and fun way to experience Peruvian cuisine; one which I wasn't previously to familiar with. 

On my last visit we had a party of 8 which can sometimes be a downer because of so many different choices, menu style, 8 different opinions, and service can be a bit harder to execute...but!

No Sweat: The Menu is great to share, we had the right group and our server was a true professional. 

We pretty much at the whole menu and it was all delicious( which tastiness has always been top notch on all my visits to Llama) 

A couple highlights though are anything from the top snack portion of the menu that comes off the grill, the quinoa with banana(trust me it sound weird but it works), and the ceviches.

The wooden doors when you walk in are very beautiful hand carved with intricate patterns. When you walk in it's a open space with a bar in the center of the restaurant lighting is dimmed. MUST do reservations, the food is amazing the appetizers are small skewers but jammed packed with flavor. Loved the calamari, beef heart, pork shoulders appetizers. All the entrées are very delicious some you can share with 2 people & some are a bit smaller but still have a lot of flavors. I gotta go back for the red snapper.

Love the plants, love the food, love the restaurant. Stop reading this review and GO THERE. 

So, what's so great about this place?

1. Food is unique and not for a premium - you can get charged $14 for avo toast in the city yet my tamal was nearly the same price for a much uniquer tasting experience
2. Cute ambience / Plant deco 
4. Makes you want to try everything else on the menu

We came here for brunch (made reservations, a good idea) and sat at the chef's counter. It gets toasty (obviously) so if you're sensitive to the heat, maybe opt for the table option. 

There's plenty of lighting in this restaurant and also the plant decorations just make everything feel good. 

We ordered the scrambled egg and the tamal. Both were spectacular. 

What gives this place a five star is that you just want to come back to try other things on the menu.

I highly recommend this place, at least for brunch! Add it to your hit list ASAP!

The service is not commensurate with the price point. They have the least inspiring wine list and they don't even have wine glasses!! This is Peruvian food for those who have no idea what huancaina, lucuma or cuy are and don't care to learn what amazing treasures they can be. This place serves cooked ceviche.. like what are you smoking huevon.

Cocktails were very tasty.  And any restaurant that stocks Redbreast is worth your hard-earned cash. Their signature dish, lomo saltado (this restaurant calls it something else, but it's basically marinated steak and fries) is absolutely delicious, and easily feeds two people. Which is great, because it cost $72.
Food was delicious. Barely see any Berma restaurants in the states but this is one you must try.
Nice hipster place Interesting food and nice cocktails. I would go back to try some new things.

Although I love the beef tenderloin entree, the price has increased from $56 to $72 for the same portion size. It is delicious (and the extra rice they bring at the end is perfect) however I don't think it is appropriate to increase the price by $16.

I wish I could give it a 5 star rating because the food was phenomenal but unfortunately the service wasn't the same quality as the food. Our drinks took too long to arrive, then when we ordered a second round it turned out our first round had the wrong drinks. Our main courses were served while we still had appetizers unfinished. We felt like we had to rush through our dinner. And at the end I was charged a different table's bill. Overall a little disappointing for the price you pay.

This place kills it on the ambiance-o-meter: an architecturally stunning space, shrewdly placed bar (in the center of the room, with dining on the periphery), whimsical cocktails with names like Lana Del Rum (or something to that effect). 

Peruvian food this is not! The vegetables dishes are entirely ill-conceived: quinoa with bananas, cashews, tomatoes, avocado, and mayonnaise (why does no one EVER list this as an ingredient?) mushed together in a kitchen-sink recipe. Salty lentils with a runny egg. Over cooked chicken and mealy potatoes that run $40 a dish (the smoky flavor was the best part, as it tended to mask the dryness of the meat).

Come for the vibe, but head to pio pio for true Peruvian food.

Had an overall really excellent experience at Llama Inn. Great ambiance, very cool space. Attentive waiter. 
FOOD
Fluke Ceviche- I am not generally a ceviche fan and I really liked this. It's citrusy and acidic without being too much, and the plantains are an amazing addition. 
Shrimp Skewer- delicious, wish there was more of it!
Pork belly skewer- our favorite thing we ate. GET!! Delicious sauce. 
Chicken thigh skewer- nice and moist. Potato chip on top was a nice touch. 
Lentil salad- probably our least favorite thing, but that's not saying much. We still cleaned the plate. Who needs health food anyways?
Beef cheek- tender, delicious. Comes on top of tacu tacu which was potatoes and delicious. 
Bread pudding- good, not life changing.

I took two colleagues to Llama Inn last night (I have previously been 4 times before, that's how much I love this spot) and they adored the whole experience. The food was out of this world, such exciting flavors and creative dishes, but still extremely 'light'! Our server Tyler needs a big shout out, he was a pure joy from start to finish (he even gave me a hug at the end of our evening). Funny, informative and attentive, without being over bearing, just the perfect server, thank you Tyler.
One of my favorite places to eat and drink cocktails.  Really delicious each time, never disappointed.  Always bustling w/ lively guests.  Bartenders and staff are super friendly and attentive.  A+

Came here for brunch and had the beef tenderloin. It was oh-my-god good. If you like beef, plantains, and fries, this is the savory brunch meal of your dreams. What was the gravy/broth? I dunno, but...*drools.*

I can't even adequately describe it. But I will be back to order it again.

This place is ahhh mazing. My husband and I went for apps and drinks. Please please please try the quinoa, ceviche and the scallops to start. You will not regret it. The quinoa was so good we almost ordered it twice. Drinks are really good as well. I had the Llama cocktail (similar to a sangria). It's got a nice balance. Beautiful decor, open kitchen, high ceilings and bar is nicely placed. I absolutely recommend, nice date night, drinks night. Make a reservation ASAP.

How can you advertise as a Peruvian Restaurant if the food is not? No authenticity to this so called Peruvian restaurant. Not one Hispanic person is visible, the menu itself was far from Peruvian. Now, Ill pay anything for a good, authentic Peruvian meal, problem here was, couldn't find one! As a Latino male, my advise to the ownership is not to advertise as a Peruvian restaurant! There is NOTHING about your establishment that provides any scene of Hispanic heritage in any way shape or form! So if your looking a loud, tight bar to have a over priced, non authentic Peruvian meal, then this is for you. Now if your looking for a Peruvian restaurant with authentic food, and ambiance, then this is not the place for you!

I've lived in Williamsburg for the past 9 years and have been to most of the top restaurants in the neighborhood. Tonight my family went out for Mother's Day and had the best meal we've had around here in years. Try the beef cheeks, the octopus ceviche and spring for the branzino. Save some room for the lime pie. Great ambiance and amazing food!

WMM (Worth My Money) 0 out 0!!!

This place is the worst! This is a review not about the food and chef but simply the restaurant and management. 

I had a reservation booked almost a 5-6 weeks ago for a large party and for a very special occasion. 4 hours before my dinner they canceled my reservation and simply told me to go somewhere else. Didn't offer any assistance or help. How in the HELL am I supposed to find a reservation for a large party in New York on a Friday and coordinate everybody to go somewhere else in 4 hours. 

Simply, I will never try to go back and never recommend it to anyone. I hope management sees this review.

Overrated restaurant, service was very mediocre and the food is a joke: we were charged above $20 for bites and $70 for their so-called beef piece, which is actually a plate of french fries with 2 chunks of meat...

My first visit to Llama Inn was to join friends for a weekend brunch. This place has such an interesting atmosphere and food choices. We had reservations so we were seated right away but the restaurant wasn't too busy when we were there.

Overall food was great with rich flavors and good portions. 

I wished that the menu was a bit more elaborative to better explain what the dishes actually were.  Waitstaff were nice but weren't very attentive. We had to remind them for our drinks after food had already arrived and was a bit difficult to grab their attention for refills and etc. 

Despite the minor confusion, I would give Llama Inn another try in the near future to try their dinner menu.

To be considered a worth while restaurant experience you compete on three things:

1) Product
2) Service
3)Value 

Let's begin with product. The food was pretty good, we ordered the fluke ceviche, sweetbreads, beef hearts, beef cheeks (this was crazy good), and the beef empanada (be fore warned this is a special and not on the menu... if you know empanadas this dish was okay.. nothing special). All in all, the food was good. 

When you go out, part of it is to eat the food. Most of it is to have an awesome time. Restaurants are magic, and how you are made to feel is as important as how good the food tastes. How you're made to feel here is ok, nothing special, nothing terrible, but definitely not memorable.

We paid $210 (This also includes a bottle of Albarino $65), for a poor excuse for Peruvian food. Ambiance was phenomenal but when you factor in the value for product Llama in falls incredibly short. Would I recommend this place as a spot for quick drink and catch up with a friend, absolutely, but that's all. The food is fine. Not worth the price tag. And the service does not make up the difference. 

Bottom line.. you aren't missing much if you don't go. 


If you find yourself in Miami, for whatever reason, this is some bad ass Peruvian food for comparison: http://www.ceviche105.com/site/
Excellent dining experience, truly word-class.  Can't wait to go back!  We had a variety of appetizers and full course, but felt like there was plenty more on the menu I wish I'd eaten.

79 degrees outside and the restaurant had no air conditioning. (Several different excuses from several different employees but there is no excuse for this.) Many other patrons sat fanning themselves. Then they rearranged tables to put a large table for 6 literally 6 inches away from us.  Unbearable. The food was really excellent but not enough to make up for the physical discomfort and not enough to ever return.

Expensive for what you get. Cute ambience, slow service (took 1h to get my food, not kidding). We had the ceviche, the beef tenderloin and other tiny (and expensive ) things. Good but nothing special in them. They get super busy and the service can't keep up with the orders.

I just had dinner at Llama Inn and I find it very difficult to write a review:
Young and beautiful (noisy too...) crowd, definitely eye candy. The staff is perfectly nice and the food is good. That should mean 5 stars, right ?

WRONG!  The menu is ridiculously small, to the tune of your having to choose the only things that you don't actively dislike. The menu isn't the only small thing... so are the portions. Besides, apart from very very few offerings, you do not stand a chance of eating that food in Peru. It simply isn't Peruvian. 

Your dish comes... when it is ready, totally irrespective of when the others at your table are served. If your hot dish comes late, you would expect it to be hot or at least warm. WRONG! It arrived late and cold. You want to complain, but how can you when the waiter apologizes profusely before you have a chance to say anything, then brings the whole table an unsollicited free round of drinks? You can't.

Obviously, 99% of the patrons have no idea of what Peruvian cuisine looks and tastes like, so they don't mind.  All in all, not a bad evening, but certainly not worth $ 90 per person. The matches are cute; they still smoke in Peru.

Looks like reviews are hit or miss which I find so difficult to believe when our entire experience was exceptional. Came on a Tuesday evening based on a recommendation from a friend. I'm happy I finally made it a point to check out Llama Inn. 

The atmosphere is aesthetically comfortable and architectually pleasing.. even the plates and bowls the food is served on felt very culture appropriate for peruvian cuisine. 

The food was delicious! We had the two ceviches, each of the scewers and the beef cheek dish. For dessert we had the key lime pie and palo santo ice cream. My boyfriend and I finished every last bite off our plates. Came ready to eat and Llama inn served it. 

The service was was exceptional. I wish I could remember the gentlemens name who was our server. He was tall, blonde and had his hair pulled back into a bun. His was charistmatic, knowledgeable of the food, the drinks and was super helpful when it came to narrowing down some choices for our dinner.  He was very easy going and helped us conclude our evening with a personal cocktail favorite. 

Boyfriend I will be back and we will be telling all of our friends about Llama Inn.

Everything was so good that our night here flew right by us. We started off with a couple of drinks recommended by our friendly and passionate bartender. I had a glass of mezcal and my girlfriend had a delicious citriusy, drink with a kiwi garnish.

We started off with the baby artichoke. It was served in a creamy yet spicy sauce alongside spinach and beans. This dish set the tone for the well balanced items to follow. It seemed like each item had some of every flavor. I

Next, we had one of each of the antichuchos. I highly recommend doing that so you can try a greater variety of foods. I liked how the antichuchos were very different from each other.

For our main course, we shared the beef cheeks. These were some of the most tender pieces of beef I've ever tried. These tender and savory chunks of beef were compliment by bitter raw onions, earthy turnips, soft and hearty rice, crispy everything quinoa crackers, and a sauce similar to mole yet a little less sweet.

For dessert, we split a Paolo Santo ice cream. It was like a plant flavored ice cream with hints of eucalyptus, coconut, and smokinees.

This was one of the most flavor intensive meals that I've had. It was a pleasure trying so many new flavors and combinations.

The chef knows what he's doing. But the crap service and the overpriced menu killed this for me. The pacing of our meal was nonexistent. And as delicious as the lomo saltado is, it is essentially two small pieces of nicely cooked steak with a ton of French fries on top to make it look like a large meal. Tasty but no where near $72 worth of food. I felt suckered. How they get away charging that blows my mind.

Everything was so good and so worth it. I'm still drooling over the Palo Santo Icecream (oh my god) and the pork belly skewers. Will definitely be back soon. It was such a rich and satisfying dining experience.

REALLY AN UNEXPECTED DISAPPOINTMENT

We have been going to Llama Inn about once every other month since they opened and have always felt they were one of the best restaurants in Williamsburg, after tonight I believe they are a victim of their own success or just greedy.

It is a Saturday night and I can easily accept that restaurants get busy and can't really keep their reservations timely. For our 8:15 reservation, we got seated at 8:50. This was truly no problem and we had a great drink at the bar waiting. However after that delay and once we were seated we anticipated everything would go smoothly, unfortunately nothing did. It took the waiter another 25 minutes to take our order. He was gracious and said they were swamped. We order another round of drinks and some anticuchos, small appetizer dishes to have with the cocktails and ordered the rest of our meal at the same time. 20 minutes later the first entree showed up but none of the anticuchos did or the other first course. We asked Asa, a waiter who served us before did the order get screwed up and was told the grill was behind. 10 minutes later our first courses showed up and they were cold, not right. Asa sent over the manager who graciously comped the anticuchos, which was good because they were not meant to be eaten cold-think cold belly. I am out of space to convey the rest-it just went down hill from there. 2 stars for trying minus 3 for failure

My wife took me out to celebrate Father's Day. We decided to head over to Williamsburg without preconceived plans and we came across this place. Having no reservations, we sat at the bar. The mix drinks were excellent although served in glasses too small and at $15 a pop. 
The food looked good, so we decided to order some appetizers. we order the Shrimp Adobo, Beef Hearts and the Fluke Ceviche. The food was good but certainly not outstanding. The portions were minimal even for an appetizer. I mean the Shrimp Adobo was literally one shrimp and the beef hearts were a small skewer with three small pieces of meat.
from looking at the other dinner there was a plate I saw that caught my eyes. The plate looked good in presentation and in portion. This was the beef tenderloin stir fry or what a real Peruvian restaurant calls Lomo Salteado. To my astonishment this plate that at any other restaurant is the normal serving size for an entree is prized at $72 because it supposedly serves 4... Really!
 After finishing our drinks (4 drinks) one of them a beer and eating our appetizers we paid over $100 plus tip. 
We were still very hungry, so we left to a bar nearby where they have a Taco truck in their back yard and spent $38 on a real meal. No wonder the Latinos in the staff at this restaurant were looking at us like "what are you guys doing in this place" while we were there. We are Latinos too... lesson learned... stick to traditional Latin restaurants for authentic Latin food. 
I do not usually write reviews but I'm doing so to today because I felt an obligation to do so and save people from "getting robbed" at this place.

another one bites the dust...  my party of 4 were really looking forward to dining here but sadly, the food, drinks and service didn't hold up to our standards. it was like pulling teeth to get a pitcher of spicy mezcal margaritas... when they finally arrived everyone was disappointed. water down, tasteless, not good but ok... we order the fluke ceviche, salmon app and all the skewers, just delicious! flavorful, interesting, small but wonderful. the whole chicken was a special and highly recommended by our server for its size, complexity and enough to satisfy our size group. for one reason or another we have to relocate inside (it started raining) to be fair, the host staff did their best at that very moment and found us 4 seats at the bar( DIRECTLY IN FRONT OF THE HOT CHARCOAL GRILL) it was 95 degress last night... anyway, it's fine, we managed, and we're still in good spirits but after 15 minutes sitting at the kitchen bar we noticed no server moved our pitcher of tasteless margaritas non gave us water, etc. at this point the wait and kitchen staff are panicked and voila the chicken arrives! it's huge and we're excited but can we have water???? we're shy a plate. and can we order a few cold beers? we stop a running server to ask for what we needed and it took forever! no, not like 5-10mins... more like 20 mins. ok, we're still vibing, enjoying each other's company and laughing at how absurd the service is because it's a Monday night and it's raining and it's Monday night... once again we were able to express our discontent with yet another person and then we were moved to a normal table that could accommodate four people and a whole chicken for $62! they ran out of ALL BEER! the chicken was smoky, tender but so tasteless. not one spice or seasoning. it comes with three large bowls of different creamy mayonnaise dipping sauces, barf. anyway, the roof space is beautiful. lots of plants and they do a great job hiding the BQE highway for that i give 2 stars but that's really all i have nice to say. Peruvian food has spice, complexity, flavor...the more restaurants choose to white wash their menu, spices and vibes to accommodate the newly white gentrified williamsburg the more inclined I am to stay home and cook my own food. good luck guys!

Absolutely loved this place! Went before heading over a outdoor edm concert! Turned out to be great choice and totally prepped us into the mooood!

Corvina Ceviche: very fresh.
Skewers: beef heart and the scallops were absolutely amazing. 
Beef tenderloin main: huge portion! came with fries, avocado spread and scallion pancakes. And it gets better, at the end of the dish, they serve buttered slightly salted rice and put it into the stew sauce. Completely wowed us. Sooo good! 
Drinks and desserts were very good too. Definitely gonna visit again.
Portions are super small and expensive. I'm Peruvian and if you want better Peruvian food and better prices and portions, better go to Chimu.

The service was really bad. They did not describe the menu properly. The portion size was smaller than they said. The waiter placed the food in front of the wrong person. It was definitely not worth the price we paid. In then we had to go to another restaurant.
Food is good but ordered a chicha with no ice and this is what I got, restaurant policy PATHETIC
Of the 34 restaurants my girlfriend made me eat at on our last trip to New York, this was my favorite.

Wow.  Did the chef change?  The lomo saltado was so disappointing (a far cry from the glory days of opening). Meat was over cooked and grey.  Sat in a sloppy wet puddle of flavorless juice. The meat x tomato x onion ratio was all wrong. Four pieces of bite size meat, three cherry tomatoes and a few onion wedges at best. We payed for a plate of french fries - and not the hand cut fries you'd expect for 72 bucks. We sat pretty speechless during the meal. No staff checked in. Oh, and the rice came well after we were done.  Nice work guys.

Amazin' food.  Great service. This place had it all. The rooftop is great and it has a really relaxed and chill vibe. The scallops are the best thing on the menu. Make sure you ask about the specials as well as the things that are off the menu - for example, the pancakes.
Way better than I expected . Service is also amazing. We sat on the rooftop and it was really relaxing. Everything we ate was delicious!

Updated:
Went back. Loved the whole fish for two and tried the unusual, tasty orange wines. Also the mushroom appetizer. Unreal. This should be a Michelin star place. Anyway, you just earned your extra star from me, Llama Inn!

Review from 2017:
This is a fantastic date place and a great drinking place.

The price point is high but for the money you get 1) unique and sexy decor 2) fantastic service 3) a creative chef doing interesting and delicious things with Peruvian cuisine.

The pork belly and scallop skewers were obscenely good. With a cocktail, this would be the perfect first date.  Or let's be real, the perfect penultimate apps/drinks before sex.

The quinoa salad falls squarely under the "creative chef" category, with banana, bacon, and cashew giving this cold, crunchy grain (well, quinoa is a seed) salad a distinctly South American flavor that is at once tropical, savory and sweet.

We split the tenderloin tacos as the main entree. This is where my personal taste did not mesh well with this kitchen. A very salty, rich dish without enough brightness (e.g. cilantro, salsa, lime, SOMETHING) to counterbalance french fries, smothering savory sauce, savory onions, and (delicious) starchy pancakes. If you like to have many cocktails with dinner, this is the dish for you. Sop up that alcohol!

Let's be fair. The tenderloin itself, once unearthed from the massive pile of fries, was *exquisite*. My uncle--nearing 80 years old and totally confused by the menu here and the vibe of the restaurant (we came to Llama Inn because Bamontes is closed on Tuesdays!)--LOVED the meat. And he's one picky, cranky lifelong New Yawkah.  As a nice touch, they came around and added perfectly made white rice to our platter to soak up the sauce as we started to whittle down the meat and fries.  If you're hungry as Funk, order this dish.  You'll leave satisfied.

The meat was very well paired with a nice by-the-glass Cab Franc.

Next time I'll definitely go with fish--either share the Branzino, or do the Rock Shrimp. As it is I chose this rockstar Chef's "power chord" and was a bit overwhelmed.  I'm a pussy!

Nevertheless, this place gets a solid 4 and a half stars for service, location, ambiance, cuisine... loses 1/2 star for price point (a bit too high for what it was) and the overpowering salty/savory of the tenderloin which had not enough veggies, greens, or something as a counterbalance (even the guacamole was just gilding the lily, offering fatty richness to be smothered upon richness).  

I will be back and look forward to writing a 5-Star review the next time around.

Ah-mazing service! Service alone makes this spot worth a visit or 2 or 20! I mean we didn't have reservations and still got a table within 20 min and trust me it was busy. We over stayed an hour after they closed but they didn't rush us. They even let us use the restroom after we left and came back.

Drinks were exceptional hands down. We didn't eat dinner but the small plates especially the scallop is to DIE for. I'm usually not so passionate about my reviews but look, given that this is in Williamsburg, I really had low expectations because well it's Williamsburg (let me explain, it's too rich and bougie for my blood lol). This place blew me away. 

Decor and ambiance also earn this place a 5 star. Love the greenery!

Will definitely come back. Need more places like this!
Sat outside upstairs on a perfect summer evening. This was my first time here and it didn't disappoint. Everything we tried was unique and flavorful. I will be back to try the large format beef dish.

Omg this was so delicious. We had the bronzino fish for 2 people and it was so filling and amazing. Came with roasted Brussels sprout and rice as sides, as well as a bomb sauce to pour on top. It tasted a little bit like Thai food, shrug lol. Had the shrimp and scallops appetizer dishes too. They were small but incredible as well. I highly highly recommend this place!!

You know how the person of your dreams is always right in front of your face, but you tend to ignore it because you're always looking for something that doesn't exist, that's the Llama Inn. Live right near it, and have avoided going to it for years in fear that it wouldn't live up to expectation. I was horrendously wrong. This place is out of this world. I might book a flight to Peru soon just to try the food there.
Had a few cocktails with pisco in them just to keep the authenticity of my Peruvian night in check, and they were phenomenal. Ordered the quinoa and artichokes based on the waiters recommendation.
The artichokes were good but forgettable. The quinoa was great, with banana and bacon, the texture and flavor of it was beyond interesting and tasty. But I don't know if I'd order them again only because of one reason: THE BEEF STIR FRY. 
You could go to the llama inn and order only this and be full. Comes with scallion pancake, rice, guacamole, a Peruvian sauce, with beef onions and peppers topped with French fries. Prepared do it yourself style, you can eat scallion pancake tacos! If you know something better than scallion pancake tacos, you're a liar. 
Don't be a fool and go here whenever you can.
Super cute inside. Friendly & attentive service. Most of the food was good but everything was really small for the price.

We had a great meal at Llama Inn last night! 

The service was superb the whole night. Our party size changed at the last minute and they went out of their way to accommodate us, the manager even coming over a couple of times to check everything was ok!

The vibe is laid back but polished, so it seems very casual, and sharing type plates are the order of the day, but the attention to detail is superb.

We enjoyed the ceviched fluke. The pork belly skewers were delicious but perhaps packing a bit too much chilli punch, and that's from a chilli addict! The scallop skewers were amazing, as was the lamb belly, with apricot perfectly cutting through the incredibly rich meat!

The stand out without a doubt is the Whole Bronzino, baked in a banana leaf and served with unbelievably good crispy Brussels sprouts (I would buy them by the bag if they offered them). The fish was perfectly cooked, moist, and packed with flavor.

Exceptional food presented in a casual friendly way, it was my first experience of Peruvian cuisine and it certainly won't be the last.

The prices are high, our bill for 4 came to $400, but it was a stand out food experience for me!

Hopefully we will be back many times!

My cousin-in-law had been asking us for quite some time to try Llama Inn. We finally went and I left feeling...unsatisfied. It's not that it was bad by any means. It's just when it comes to Peruvian food, it's typically better from an authentic hole in the wall establishment. When you pay a fortune for a small plate, it's hard not to compare what you would get from other local Peruvian places that are spot on. The price tag on the lomo unfortunately isn't worth it. While delicious, it wasn't worth the 6 cubes of filet. The atmosphere is nice and upscale, which clearly is what the restaurant is about. Upscale and with a twist while touching on Peruvian roots. I wouldn't come again but was worth trying.

Twice made a reservation here. Both times showed up and couldn't be seated. 

Good news is a place like this cant survive in williamsburg. So, I guess we will wait until they're out of business next year and somewhere with better service replaces them.

four stars just because i think the food is slightly overpriced, and drinks are expensive but quality and service we're amazing. very GF friendly, i think there were only 3 dishes i could not have. i was in a party of 4 we started with the beats and goat cheese as an appetizer, it was flavorful and had nice greens and gooseberries added a nice touch. the star of the night was the whole branzino. OMG it was cooked to perfection loaded with acidic peppers and herbs, also came with delicious coconut rice and brussel sprouts. the dish felt more thai than peruvian but it was dang tasty!!!
Food and staff were wonderful. Not the usual taste combos. Was a little noisy and it was hard to hear others is my only issue, but that means more coziness.

This doesn't seem like typical Peruvian cuisine to me but rather a modern take on Peruvian food.  The execution was very good. I came here in a group of 5 while not being very hungry and got:

1. Chicken thigh skewers
2. Beef heart skewers
3. Beet salad
4. Asparagus
5. Pork shoulder (main)
6. Lamb belly (main)

All the dishes were loaded with flavor and very well balanced though if we were hungry, we would need to get at least a couple more dishes. The portion size on the two mains were a tad on the small side (especially for the price) and I think they were just sitting on the window for a while because they came to our table luke warm but other than that, we had no complaints cuz all the dishes were delicious.  My favorites were the beet salad and the lamb belly - I would go back just for those. 

The cocktails were pretty good too. I had the Chimpin' Aint Easy - a mezcal based drink which had just the right amount of smokiness and paired well with the food.

Hate to be the alpaca in a room full of llamas, but the Llama Inn was a solid 3 stars. ()

My Russian boyfriend took me here last night and we were both so excited to check out an 8.8 on The Infatuation.

The positives:

Super chill vibes, verdant decor, cool lighting. Fantastic service. Note that nearly all seating is barstool.

The negatives:
While certainly different and inventive, we just didn't love the food. Keep in mind we were only two, so we couldn't get the large plates they're famous for. We got the sea bream ceviche, slippery shrimp, chicken and scallop skewers, and Chilean sea bass. All was covered in thick cream sauce which totally took over the flavor. Finally, the paltry dessert menu was merely three mediocre options. I opted for Ben nd Jerry's cherry Garcia at the end of the night, as well as a little nightcap to top it all off. But truly, we ended up going to Cvs for popcorn where I stuffed my face with Skinny Pop after spending $160 fat bucks on dinner!
