It's ok though, the company everything. Even a visit from our lovely friend.

Oh,,, plus - we took a 28 dollar cab right home and my Russian boyfriend fell asleep in my lap!!

Tata for now...

In NYC, you never really know if a restaurant is great or just has a good PR team. Llama Inn is absolutely worth the trip to Williamsburg! The space is decorated with artful Peruvian touches setting the mood for magic. We sat at the bar for a date night. Although the portions are on the smaller side, everything was made to perfection. We had the shrimp, which was only one piece, but it was perfectly spiced. The ceviche was also good with banana chips making it a playful dish. The asparagus was topped with a homemade cheese. I've never had better asparagus anywhere! We also had the red snapper and pork shoulder as entrees! I'll definitely be back. Get the Touch of Evil cocktail and splurge on the lime pie. Finding a restaurant that really goes the extra mile is so rare these days.
Expect extremely slow service. Not once did they apologize until after I asked why we had been waiting 45min for a chicken sandwich. Will not come back.

Everything we ate at Llama Inn was terrific. New tastes and not a single disappointing dish. The 5-star service was friendly and informative. The room and vibe were great. But the prices are too high, in my opinion, by 25%.  We choked at the bill, given what we'd eaten and how weak the drinks were.  If budget is no object, book the Llama Inn!

The only good thing about this place is location and rooftop. The ambiance is pretty and I love the atmosphere. Everything else is over priced and the food isn't that good. The drinks are really good but for the prices I rather pay that in the city not Brooklyn so it's not worth it. The food portions are really small and when they say it's shareable it's not. The quinoa is actually really good even though in general I don't like it, they made it really tasty. The fish branzino is also very good and tasty. The sharables aren't really good but it was worth trying. Wouldn't go again unless I wanted the rooftop or the ambiance.

The food is great but can you be rushed through your meal any faster? This is my third time here, and it just felt like they are trying to rotate you in and out, no matter what you order. Our waiter cut us off mid question in order to get on with his night - rude. The quality has gone down hill and I'm very disappointed.

Llama Inn is an instagrammable brunch spot with good drinks a lot of creative dishes. The rooftop is gorgeous - the plant game is strong and feels like a secluded little garden even though it's right by the highway overpass.

Unfortunately, the service was horrifically slow and a little overpriced. We were there for brunch at 1pm on a Saturday and the restaurant appeared to be rather empty, but our food took almost an hour to be prepared. We were huuuuuungry. 

For food, we got the pork shoulder sandwich and the tamal with fried egg. Both were good (and also very filling and heavy) but the tamal only came with two shrimps and came with shells on. I also tried the $9 juice, and it was served in a pretty glass with a leaf garnish, but definitely not worth the cost.

Might be worth a shot, but just be prepared for a wait and a hefty bill.

V v good. Ceviche, Snapper, and Squash were all 

Another good place in the hood. Very nice decor. Service was good, and everything came out quickly.

Everything I've had here has been excellent. The small plates are all beautifully presented and the flavors are delicious. Their cocktails are creative and tasty, too. One of my favorite restaurants in New York.

The vegan options on the menu were limited, but they had a delicious vegan special with beets and ginger poached pears. The drinks were especially good. Noise volume is a little high, but otherwise liked the vibe.

We came in a group of eight. The ambiance and decor is pretty good. And the pisco sour had to be the best part of the night. However, as far as service it was a nightmare.  We were told which foods could be custimzied to be vegettarian and to our surprise half way through the appetizer; the fish was mixed in the sauce.  The waiter barely apologized and did nothing to salvage the night.

Thanks for a memorable night !

Incredible food! Only thing is that the owner (or the guy who was running the floor... I think his name was Jason?) that night kept touching me and my friend on our backs. Several times through the night. He didn't touch the man who was dining with us--just my back and my girl friend's back. It made us really uncomfortable but we didn't want to ruin our meal, so we didn't say anything about it while it was happening. We had a great meal, but it was unfortunate that it kept being interrupted by unwanted touches. Next time, keep your paws to yourself please!

I've been to Llama Inn many, many times.  The food is decent but the service is a complete nightmare EVERY SINGLE TIME.
We booked a reservation a few weeks prior and the day of the reservation I received a call from an unpleasant manager canceling the reservation.  The day before we received a text confirming the reservation?!  This isn't the first time I've had this problem.  So don't bet on having a reservation.
I've had it with the attitude from management and hosts.  The food isn't that great.

LOVED Llama Inn. My two girlfriends and I went for dinner, and while it's definitely a pricier meal ($245 for the three of us inclusive of tax/tip) it was worth it. The restaurant is really cute, loved the wood and greenery - plants are hanging down from the ceiling/windows. Restaurant was dark but it seemed to fit the overall vibe. 

We got the sea bream tiradito which I loooooved, one pork belly skewer to share (one bite each!) and the quinoa salad to start. We liked the quinoa, but agreed we could have skipped that and each gotten our own pork belly skewer instead. We got the beef tenderloin for our main and that was a perfect amount for 3, and also insanely good. Basically rolled out of the restaurant but worth every bite. 

Cocktails were also good, and free dessert didn't hurt :) will definitely be back at Llama Inn, maybe after my next paycheck.

Great cocktails, with subtle flavors.  Wish I could have had one of each, but I would not have lived to write this.  Of the ones I tried, my favorite was La Chunga.  Beer selection is limited but eclectic.  Had already eaten, so could only sample the appetizers.  Like the cocktails, they combine a lot of interesting flavors.  The rest of the food menu looked worthy of repeat visits.  A bit pricey but not outrageous, especially considering the effort that goes into every item on the menu.  Only complaint is that it is quite noisy at peak times, so limber up your vocal cords beforehand.

Trendy decor + plant life. Remarkable and original cuisine  - cocktails, tapas, entrées and desserts. I can vouch for the Llama del rey and Cumbia cocktails, the pork belly, beef heart, quinoa salad, whole Bronzino, chorizo and the pork shoulder. And, all those desserts were heaven.

WOW - what a meal. It's pricey but definitely worth it. The beef tenderloin stir fry was fantastic - it's a lot of food though so if you probably only need 1 appetizer (we had fluke ceviche which was SUPER tasty) because you don't want to miss out on dessert!

Service was great, took the time to explain dishes and helped us decide on our meal.

The only minor thing was we sat at the bar since we didn't have a reservation and we arrived at 5:30 when they opened and probably could have been seated at a table with enough time for them to turn it over.

Went there for my birthday, so that day I specifically wanted to treat myself with a good dinner, good food, good service.

The table I reserved was ready, so we were able to sit right away. 
Our waitress welcomed us with a genuine smile on her face, she offered us water and gave us some time to read the menu. 
After she came ove and started to explain us the menu. 
She was very professional mentioning us the most popular dishes with the distinctive ingredients. But she did even a better job when she mentioned us what she thinks are her favorite dishes of the menu, and we followed her advice about the Fluke Ceviche which I personally think was the best Ceviche I have had since been living in NYC ( 7 years), perfect balance and pleasant texture with the add of crispy plantains. 
Delicate flavor which opens up and warm up your mouth even though the citrus works as a contrast. 

Then we had pork belly skewers which were so rich in flavor, buttery tender meat, and then we had the scallops skewers, which were very soft, even if I personally would have preferred a lighter sauce, just not to cover the fish flavor. 
We continued with an amazing quinoa pistachio salad which I found phenomenal, and I'm happy I followed the waitress advice about it .
We ended up with a whole Branzino, perfectly seasoned, perfectly cooked, very flavory meat with the perfect texture, with a side of white rice and super tasty Brussels sprouts. 

They offered us  2 desserts: a rich lemon pie, and an amazing Palo Santo ice-cream, which I particularly loved. 
The flavor was right on point, nice light foamy/creaminess, but what I loved was the cold-warm feeling the chef created between the temperature and the " warm" earthy, smoky flavor of the Palo Santo. 

They also offered a round of drink.
We had the Llama del Rey which was fruity but I personally think it lacks of " charisma", I found it pretty flat. 
The Incas sunset was very good, and the hint of spiciness just added an extra layer of flavor which I really liked. 

During the whole time of our dinner we never had our glasses empty. Waiters and manager were constantly refilling our water. 
They always made sure we were completely satisfied. 
I saw beautiful smiles on their face, and the whole environment was welcoming and friendly, with a smooth service and great teamwork. Great job guys 

It was an impeccable experience, the beauty of the decor, the great staff, the great food, the manager who was beyond amazing, and the Chef definitely knows what he is doing 
Our new favorite restaurant

This place is spectacular - pricey, but spectacular. 

I came here on a Wednesday with my partner and we sat at the chefs bar - I was cold so it was perfect but if you get warm easily I would steer clear of this option as we were right in front of the skewer grill. The food is to die for, the ambiance is great, and the cocktails are delicious.

To drink we got two different shaken cocktails (mine had brandy, ginger, lemon & lime) and they were both delicious. 

To eat we got one pork belly skewer and one scallop skewer - again, both delicious. The scallop came with a mild cheese sauce and the pork with a Asian-y glaze.

As our main we split the main steak dish (it comes with probably 6-8 pieces of steak, a mound of fries, a side of avocado spread and crema and some scallion pancakes). It was honestly slightly too much food for the two of us but we managed to eat all of the meat. Once you are part way through/almost done, they come by with some white rice to soak up the leftover sauce. I wish I knew this so I wouldn't have eaten as much as I did!

Overall it was a great experience. They have a coat check and hooks are the bar seats if you were curious.

Don't get me wrong, the food here is incredible. The complexity of the chef's palette is what I must applaud. However, the service did not justify the quality of the food.

First impressions, we were seated 30minutes after our reservation time (given that we came 5 minutes earlier), it was unacceptable. Yes I wouldn't mind waiting by the bar for 10minutes, but 30? Also did I mention our dinner reservation was at 10:15pm? I just really hope that the restaurant will get more organized with their reservations and take into account the time it takes to set the tables as well.

Another bad impression was that we didn't know the portions and wanted to order more food after our first set of orders, but was unaware that the kitchen closes at 11. Our waitress said that our hostess shouldn't informed us, its not a good look to take blame on others like that. 

We were in a bad mood, but eventually they realize that we were dissatisfied and take our second order and also gave us the beef tenderloin on the house. It was a good ending to the night actually, because we were very full and satisfied. I'm giving this a 3 stars because I was very unhappy with the service.

Came here on a busy Friday night. The place was hopping.  You feel like you are in the middle of everything that is happening.  We skipped drinks since we had them at another location and we went straight for the food.

Appetizers  - these were REALLY SMALL!  The photos online made it look like it was a bit more food but the waiter told us the appetizers were a bite sized.

chicken thigh - good
pork belly - very good but before I could fully appreciate it, I was done!

mains
duck sausage - this was very tasty and filling.  
trout - the trout tasted like salmon - very weird.  It was good but again not that much food.  Get this if you want a light meal

Overall I was not blown away by the food.  I had very high expectations and the place was packed.  The food was good but I wouldn't go out of my way to come here.  Overall good experience and friendly wait staff.

This place redefines 'nyc sucker seating'.  I know sometimes it fills up quickly, and sometimes it doesn't...like on a Wednesday.  Why do hosts/managers so often put you right next to another table when more than half the restaurant is empty?  Food is hit or miss.  If you have to physically move the tables every time people sit down, the tables are TOO CLOSE.  It just makes the restaurant look greedy and completely detracts from the atmosphere.  It's not like it's a tiny space that requires such space-station compactness...it's pretty big in there.  If you're gonna eat here, eat at the bar on a weekday...and if you have to pick between brunch and dinner on the w, pick brunch.  Dinner menu is more expensive but not necessarily better tasting than brunch.

Nice, spacious brunch spot tucked in a street corner with a cool, cozy, leafy rooftop. Made reservations, and got there right when they opened. It was empty when I arrived but quickly filled up and was completely full but the time we finished brunch and were heading out. 

My friend and I split the beef tenderloin stir fry (cheesy fries with beef and delicious toppings), and the crispy pork shoulder sandwich with veggie chips (choose the veggie chips!). We also split a pitcher of the llama del rey, which was enough to keep us cool on a July morning and get us lightly buzzed. 

Everything was delicious and service was amazing. All the servers were super knowledgeable about the menu items and very attentive. 

I definitely want to come back and try more of their items. It's not meant to be tapas style, but everything looks great so I'd bring a friend or two to order multiple items and share.

Simply incredible. I can't wait to see what the place is that these talented people cook up next. We were sent by an awesome guy working at The Williamsburg Hotel bar named Francisco. Once he found out we loved Peruvian food, he told us we could not leave New York the next day without at least trying it. We were strapped for time and eating later, so we had 3 appetizers and each tried a cocktail. Everything was incredible. We both still regret that we didn't just cancel the late dinner plans and stay there to feast. Ceviche scallops and anticuchos. The ceviche and anticuchos were simply the best we had ever had. And we have tried maaaaany. My girlfriend (Peruvian) said that it was even better than anything she had had during her many visits to Peru. The scallops were incredible too. What a treat. On our next trip, this place will be our first stop, no doubt. Thanks Francisco!

Llama me tell you. The food and drinks here are spectacular.

Our friends who brought us had previously been here with a Peruvian couple. That couple had assured them these tastes represent true fine Peruvian dining.

So for four of us...scallop skewers and pork belly skewers. The best pork belly I've ever eaten. Quinoa with bacon, avocado and more--outrageously tasty with incredible textures and complex flavors. Sunchoke warm plate-fine but not as amazing as everything else.

Save room for the rice...which comes late with the steak main, to soak up final juices. Steak is first top loaded with frites. And then the rice as sponge. Yum.

Cocktails like you don't typically get. Very hipsta' atmosphere...hey it is Brooklyn. Fantastic service.

My husband is hard to please and he was SO PLEASED. We look forward to the opening of Llama San in my old Village neighborhood.

Our favorite restaurant of 2018. Thank you Llama Inn.

This place is so cool! Recommended by a friend for cool dinner spots in Brooklyn/Williamsburg. There are a few different seating options online that were a little confusing without knowing the layout. They ended up having to move us from window counter to a table, but that was probably what we would have preferred anyway. Chef's counter did look pretty cool getting to watch them make the food.  

The menu is super trendy with lots of interesting things to try. It's shared plates so we relied heavily on our waiter to make recommendations, and he did a great job of that. It sounds awful, but definitely try the quinoa banana thing. Wild combo but delicious! Nothing we had was bad. The cocktails were really good as well. I tried one on draft and one shaken - both were excellent. All in all I would recommend trying a little bit of everything and relying on your server to lead you down the right path!

Came here for my husbands birthday and was blown away! We can't stop talking about the great food, service and drinks! We started with cocktails at the bar and although I can't recall the names, all were delicious and creative! 
We were nervous at first that we would be restricted by the size of the main dishes - notoriously large enough to feed 3 (we were only 2). We started with the chicken skewer which was moist, flavorful and a great start to be meal but the star was the branzino!! Served with Brussels sprouts, Peruvian corn/white rice and coconut curry ... it was a feast and worth reserving our appetites for the main dish! Husband already wants to go back and undoubtedly, we will but next time will try the steak and bring a bigger party along :)

New Peruvian restaurant in Williamsburg, where being a native is just trendy. Unique Nouveau Scrumptious Peruvian inspired dishes, an explosion of flavor and good taste.
A must.

A fun vibe and a bar big enough to make this an elite last minute "I want to go somewhere not boring" place. 

Draft cocktails are on point and paired with a ceviche would make for a nice little (expensive) solo bar snack. The beef tenderloin is a delicious large format meal, though for the price you'd expect more meat, but the salty, spicy, acidic bite is one of Williamsburg's finest.

One of my FAVORITE restaurants! I've been twice, and each time was an absolute treat. The bronzino is an absolute showstopper MUST ORDER. The lime pie is also SUBLIME for people who love desserts. Could not recommend this place more, everything I've eaten here is divine.
Made reservation for 9:30. Did not get seated until 10:30. Staff was not even apologetic.

We always enjoyed going to Llama in the past. The food has always been "Very Good" and "Plated" Excellent (sometimes) too small a portion. Never the less has been a good experience. 
However our New Years Eve was entirely a complete disaster!!
  First we were never told that the regular menu was not being offered that evening, (either by e-Mail or on there own WEB-SITE).
  Talking to the manager (both) they assured me it was. We checked again sitting waiting for service. (NOT in either place).
  Fixed price menu's were handed to us (two regular - one Vegetarian) only Three (3) items and One (1) dessert. The problem here with this (Menu) was no place on the  menu was there any "Pre-Price" dollar amount printed..? NO PLACE NOT ANYWHERE
 At the bottom of the menu (Pre-Fixed) was "in very small print" with wine pairing $65.00. Sooo we were to understand that it would be $65. per plate !! WRONG and we never thought to ask. (Again NOT on WEB or e-Mail) "Wine Glasses are Small 4oz. flat at best" ONLY filled Once with each very small course.  
  Our finial bill ( Only One (1) Chi Cha Morada was extra) charge was $525.00!! 
  This "New Years Eve"  / event  at Llama was poorly organized / setup and miss informing at best. 
   And YES we paid the "Bill / Tab"   PS. Won't be going back there anytime soon or at all .

First, a haiku:

An ode to Peru!
Must get: Quinoa side; Skewers.
Cocktails yummy, too.

Now, for those of you who have more time on your hands.

Outstanding food and nice service. I went to Llama Inn for an early dinner reservation for three people, and it seemed that the staff was confused about where we would sit, and sat us at a table set for 10. Since I was there celebrating my birthday, I would have picked another place if I'd anticipated a group dining experience when I wasn't expecting one. Another group joined the table about a half hour into our meal. 

However the food was delicious! The quinoa with banana was tasty and unique. Must try. The drinks were delicious, including the milky tequila orgeat cocktail as well as the wine cocktail with frozen grapes. The skewers were great. I think we had better anticuchos in Peru and at other restaurants, but overall the skewers were pretty tasty. The scallop and the pork belly were standouts. Also, beautiful decor, which I failed to capture!

Came here for my boyfriend's birthday and to try Peruvian! I got the La Chunga cocktail which was very good and he got a whiskey sour. There aren't many options for vegetarians but the waiter was very knowledgeable about the menu & knew how to modify dishes to meet different dietary concerns. I got the sweet potato & goat cheese dish (no veal jus) it was absolutely delicious and gone too soon. For dessert we got the lime pie after seeing other tables order it and it was also wonderful even as someone who doesn't usually prefer citrus desserts. It was a great experience but if you're vegetarian you might want a snack beforehand!

Llama Inn is the champion of interesting food and a fun dining experience in Brooklyn. It has become quite popular and reservations are challenging to secure and the wait times have soared to a solid hour on Saturday nights (but the wait is still significantly less than the 4 hours Lilia is willing to offer you around the corner for a table for two). 

The plants and vegetation that is artfully and skillfully decorated throughout the restaurant creates a dynamic vibe that makes you feel like you're dining outside of a city. The layout of the venue with the bar in the menu gives off the illusion that the space is bigger than it really is. 

There are too many items on the menu that are must orders! And another handful of items that I wish I had the room to try. Must order: scallops, sunchokes, and pork shoulder. Lime Pie if you have time for desert! 

The tartar sauce applied to the scallops was a little over the top but it was absolutely delicious. And who would've thought pairing sunchokes with pumpkin seeds would make for such a delightful combo?!

The lime pie definitely takes the cake ("pie") in terms of dishes that hit the spot. The burnt meringue rivals a baked Alaska. 

The bar tenders and servers are super nice and generous with their pours as well!

Happy with my first visit. Service was good, food good, drink good, & ambiance nice.

Got the beef tenderloin stir fry which was good, especially the beef. The fries, egg, beef, sauces, and veggies all went well together. As for the banana, which was buried beneath everything, it could have been left out or on the side. The sweet & salty combo wasn't working for this savory dish.

To wash it down, I got the Llama Side, a non-alcoholic drink. I ordered it without ginger. It was good, a bit too much lime, but good!

A friend from out of town wanted Peruvian food and I had heard good things about his place so we went for brunch. Positives: the atmosphere is very trendy and welcoming, service was good and there were refills on the coffee. Negatives: the flavor profile of the food was not really to my liking - I whole heartily admit that I'm not an expert on Peruvian food but I found everything we ordered to be quite greasy and flavorless compared to the other Peruvian places I've been to in the city. Would not recommend unless you're looking for a place for a purely esthetically pleasing brunch.

Pisco Sour: 5 stars
Pork Belly: 4 stars (flavor is great but need more of it!)
Beef cheek: 5 stars

This place is great. I can see why they fill up on wends. Im here on a Tuesday and its the perfect amount of busy.

THIS IS NOT A PERUVIAN RESTAURANT!

Couldn't quite figure out what it was until one of the waiters/bussers said it was a fusion with Japanese. And then it made a little more sense. But then another waiter said it was a fusion with American. So it seems like the staff doesn't know what it is either.

Pros:
The place is beautiful 
Staff is very attentive
Food comes out quickly
Nice food presentation

Cons:
PORTIONS ARE SMALL
Food doesn't taste that good
Expensive for the quality
Tables are a little too close to each other along the wall.
No Happy Hour

The food more specifically:
Skewers are TINY!!!!- DEFINITELY for 1 person
The Skewers are also not consistent. A neighboring table got a slightly bigger portion. The Pork Belly was good but a little spicy. The Scallop was good, but you are left wanting more.

As for entrees, my mom had the Duck Sausage and she didn't care for it. The portion was decent, but she hated the cilantro rice, which had a strong cirtrus/acidic taste. I had the Beef Cheeks, which were saucy and not that good. Also had a strong acid taste. I finished the food because it was expensive, otherwise I would have eaten less. Mom didn't finish her meal and I had to prepare her something to eat once we got home. Kinda defeats the purpose of going out to eat. And little painful after you drop $80 on dinner. 

We had one rude busser, otherwise the staff was friendly. I asked him if the tiny plate on the table was the dinner plate and he replied, "I don't understand the question". I asked him 2 more times and he replied the same way but with lots of attitude. He gave me that look like it was my first time in a restaurant and I couldn't speak English. I spoke to the manager and he apologized, but that's it. Another manager would have taken something off of the bill or given a free dessert, something!

Overall, this place is not worth the money. I wish we would have gone to Chimu down the street.
Way too expensive. Lomo saltado literally 9 pieces of (really) good meat but come on... Small plates are ridiculous small.ufff

The food is absolutely delicious and the restaurant offers a nice evening ambiance. Unfortunately my experience with the service was terrible. Our waiter, Victor M., was very pushy in trying to convince us to order more food, which we found very odd. He recommended a bottle of wine, which our party disagreed on due to the very night price point. When the bill came, we noticed the wine was about $30 dollars more than the bottle we chose. The waiter aggressively argued that we were wrong, but thankfully he changed it...but with attitude. We were so disappointed in his service, so we decided not to give him a great tip, due to the aggressive argument, being very pushy, and the excessive long wait for our dishes. Victor stopped me from leaving the restaurant to complain about the Tip.  I spoke to the manager, who was lovely and assured me they will look into the situation. I took photos of my receipts incase he try's to add a higher tip, which the manager also assured me he will look into.

If this place was solely evaluated on their lime pie, I wouldn't have enough stars! The rest of the food is great too, but the portions are a bit too small in some instances, tapas style or not. You MUST get their lime pie though, it's insanely good. It's so tasty we've popped in just to have the pie with a glass of wine or coffee.

I've been to Llama Inn twice for brunch and twice for dinner, and love it for both meals. The food, drinks, and ambiance here are all 5/5 stars, no question. Docking a star for the service though, which has been inconsistent. The service for our first dinner, which was at the bar, was incredible (shoutout to Spencer, who gave such great recommendations and was amazing!). For my next two visits, the service was unremarkable, but fine. But I came here for brunch with a group of five last weekend, and our waitress was just... bad. She would literally walk away from our table when we were speaking to her. We would try to flag her down, and she would rush away without making eye contact (while doing nothing, she didn't have another table's drinks/food in her hands). My friend asked if they had any non-dairy milk, and she just said "whole milk." She really just seemed to possess no sense of urgency, even as we (by we, I mean me, if that has not been made clear through this review) grew increasingly frustrated with her. 

Also, on a bizarre note, they have no black pepper here, because apparently their kitchen doesn't cook with it (one of my friends asked for salt and pepper)?! Which seems crazy, but the dishes I've had have all been very interesting and flavorful, so I guess they don't need it... 

Anyway, on to my the good parts of Llama Inn (the substantial majority)! This restaurant is so, so beautiful, especially when it's sunny out. Gets ton of light, and there's lots of thriving plant life. I've also heard there's a rooftop patio, which I've never been able to take advantage of (always either too hot or too cold when I've eaten here), but am excited to try this summer. 

The mixed drinks here are amazing, even the non-alcoholic ones! We got the Llama Side juice at brunch, which was pineapple, passion fruit, ginger, and chicha morada. SO good. I finished mine before any of the food had even come out. At dinner, I always get the Llama Del Rey, which is one of my favorite cocktails in the city. I can drink a pitcher of those on my own, honestly (although for the sake of my friends and family, I will refrain). 

The best way to do dinner for two is with the fluke ceviche, a couple skewers (love the scallop and pork belly the most), the quinoa, and splitting a main dish. The ceviche is a must order, just the perfect combo of tangy, sweet, acidic, and refreshing, with such fresh fish. And the quinoa is such a sleeper hit -- might actually be my favorite thing on the menu?! It's mixed with banana, avocado, bacon, cashews, and crema. Just such an awesome mix of contrasting flavors and textures. You need it. If you're coming with the group, you can also get the beef tenderloin stir fry, which is basically a giant pile of beef and french fries served with crepes. It's definitely good, but the crepes are a little too greasy for me, and I actually prefer the smaller version of the dish that they serve at brunch. 

I've had two brunch experiences here, one where the food was just fine, and one that was incredible (the last time I came here, despite the service). Since we had such a big group and the dishes are a little smaller here, we were able to try a pretty big chunk of their menu. We got the ceviche, the swiss chard and mushroom empanada, the avocado toast, the kale salad, fried rice omelette, beef tenderloin, fried chicken sandwich, the burger, and the french toast (yes, we eat a lot). The highlights are really the beef tenderloin, french toast, ceviche (although I think the dinner version of the ceviche is better, this one is still pretty great), burger, and fried chicken sandwich. Everything else was still very good though! The only item I wouldn't order again is the fried rice omelette... rice inside an omelette is not my favorite texture/flavor combination.

Honestly though, it is hard to go wrong here, even when you get a terrible waitress. The unique, well prepared food and drinks really speak for themself. Can't wait to come back many, many times.
really good food and service, went on a weeknight so that may have helped. highly recommend the fluke ceviche, sweet potato dish, and the whole fish. only thing I would pass on is the potato skewer.

I came here for brunch two weeks ago, and looking at these food images my mouth is watering all over again and I wish I could have this meal again.

Make sure to get a reservation if you're coming on a weekend! They certainly fill up quickly, and they have you sit at the bar to have your entire party arrive before seating you.

The three of us got 3 entrees to share...tapas style. It was a great way try try a bit of everything (portions are an ok size. We could have probably gotten another dish too)

Beef tenderloin: amazing. Highly recommend, the sauce on it is so flavorful and the fries add a nice balance to the beef and eggs. 

Tacu tacu: We ate ALL OF IT. The only thing I'd say here was that it only had one piece of plantain??? So weird, of all the things to skimp out on...

French toast: the toast had a nice crunch to it but was very fluffy on the inside. It was really nice to have a sweet item with our meal.
Nice ambiance but a bit stuffy environment. Favorite aspect was the palo santo scented restrooms. All the food was nice & fancy but nothing authentic

This place makes me wish I lived in Brooklyn! Went here for brunch with a friend, and we ordered the tacu tacu and omelette with Chinese sausage. The tacu tacu was PHENOMENAL and the omelette was delicious too. The iced coffee was so good I wanted a second glass but decided against it since it would have been my third glass of iced coffee that morning. Highly recommend their brunch menu! Will definitely be back.
really excellent Peruvian food and cocktails. A fun and different stop in the NYC restaurant scene worth trying for new ideas and delicious comforts food. You must get the beef stir fry!
no reservation no table, doesn't matter if the place is empty ... host is very rude pretty much ignored us for 15 min before telling us "no"

Llama Inn is one of my favorite restaurants in NYC. The atmosphere is great and the food is out of this world. The Parmesan crusted scallops were unlike anything I'd had before. My friend was visiting from upstate and still talks about how good Llama Inn was. My only regret is that it's a little hard to reach from Manhattan but you won't regret going

OH MY GOD. 
Everything was magical. 
The venue is really cute and well decorated, and the food is extraordinary. 
The scallop and the beef tenderloin steer fry were to die for, and the key lime pie is also worth mentioning. 
I highly recommend!

Starting off by saying I've got some credibility in experiencing great food and even better service - I've got no problems with most of the hyped up restaurants in NYC that live up to their reputations- Olmstead, Four Horsemen, Roberta's, Metta, Lilia, Maison Premier, every Andrew Tarlow restaurant on the planet - love them all. 

I'm also not a complainer at restaurants at all unless it's bad. 

That said, I do not understand the hype here and I just have to air my grievances and we went months ago... to warn my fellow good citizens not to waste your money...

Soooo - My friend and I were SHOCKED at how rude the service was (we sat at the bar). We're not too precious at all we don't mind non smiley people but this was .. different. We were ignored for so very long every step of the way. It was excruciating waiting at those dreadful barstools to order a drink, to ask for food menus, to ask for drink menus, to ask for anything at all. 

I had wondered if there was something I did to this man in a past life. Seriously what the actual .... was going on. 

Fine we'll put up with it I guess if the food was as good as the hype. But sadly it wasn't.  Overly salted and I LOVE salt. We ordered clams that came in a thick creamy sauce with no shells you had to fish them out of the sauce. Everything was so small and I LOVE small portions. Too smalll 

Girl bye never coming back.

More likea 2.5 star. Based on information available online, we were expecting it to be a much better dining experience. A quick rundown of the food: 

Ceviche: Average and not as flavorful as should be expected
Bunch of skewers: Again, nothing out of the ordinary. Which is unfortunate. 
Trout: Tasty and probably the best of the dishes
Beets: Ordinary and can be cooked at home easily. Nothing complex about it and should be taken off the menu. 
Key Lime Pie: Excellent 
Drinks: Solid but not outstanding 
Ambiance: Tropical and relaxed
Service: Poor. Our waiter was pushy, unprofessional and seemed to be off his game and distracted. Pushing dishes that we didn't want is one aspect which can be let slide, however snatching a glass from my hands no less with a little of my cocktail still remaining (while I wasn't looking) was downright unprofessional. 

All in all, the food and the service don't call for a second visit to this place.

I've been 2 times. it was bad both times. The staff was kind and attentive but the food was horrendous and incorrect. The manager came out and gave us raw fish after we had already finished our dessert -- not sure why?? Not worth it.

Cool  spot with open kitchen , nice interior, loads of plants . 
Menu though is a little bit difficult to understand..
 Nice and cozy.

Really love the vibe at this place. The food is solid  get the ceviche and the duck if they still have it!  We were told that the duck was a special by the bartender. Also, grab a spot at the bar. You're sure to get treated well by the bartenders.. we got a free shot of a pineapple flavoured drink.

Just ok, in my opinion. Peruvian food is so spectacular to begin with that they are already starting with much potential, but didn't think they did all that much for the food. Same cannot he said for the prices. $7-8 for a bite of anticucho is steep; but $70+ for a lomo saltado, which although good, consisted primarily of French fries is ridiculous. Cocktails were similarly overpriced and just ok taste wise. Service and ambience were good, but non of it made up for the price tag.

We arrive at 8pm on a Saturday without a reservation, the host was very attentive, he putted us on the waiting list for the bar (which we had no problem) and suggested us a place where we could have drinks while waiting. We had a message after 50min which was the aprox time he said it would take. At the bar we had drinks, Llama del Rey was delicious! And then we ordered our food. I ordered the Broccoli beaf hearth and the purple potatoes, rocoto ocopa, and my boyfriend ordered the Rock shrimp( which was like a paella style). Food was spectacular, delightful! I ordered a side of purple potatoes since I knew the plates were small... I just wasn't expecting them that small... and was not expecting that they would arrive at different times! Literally my boyfriend didn't get his plate until I finished!! How is this possible?! 
 He had to stare at me while I was eating my food, and then I got to stare at him while he was eating his Food! The bartender only checked on the kitchen when I was basically finishing my food, because WE HAD TO ASK and that's it, he didn't anything else... I was expecting a bit more from the service and be at least at t he same level of the quality of the food that we were paying for.

Beside the bustling Brooklyn Queens Expressway, just upon the desiccated outskirts of town, stands a bright turquoise loft-like building marked with its sign "Llama Inn" discreetly perched on the corner. Upon entering, I was greeted by the earthy, illuminated space lined with a farrago of tropical plants -- almost like a patio set under a roof. The bar-side seating, where I was led to sit, was surrounded by petite tables and small bar tables. As a design enthusiast, the eccentric décor was definitely a cherry on top of my eager anticipation for the food.

(Note: Because I went in February, during the winter months, the actual patio seating upstairs was closed off; however, photos I have seen of it insist that I visit this restaurant again when the heat greets us again.)

With experience in both American and Peruvian cuisines, Ramirez brings a delicious fusion of New York's innovative inspirations with Peruvian traditions and roots to the table. Llama Inn opened in 2015 and has since scored two stars from the New York Times as well as a Michelin Bib Gourmand -- a rising star.

/Brunch Menu/
Corvina Ceviche, Lime, Red Onion, Cilantro, Sweet Potato

The overlaying crunchy layer of nuts was juxtaposed with the chewy texture of the fish, a pleasant contrast to the palette.  Along with the sweet potatoes, the tangy mix of fresh onions and herbs sprinkled on top were a refreshing addition to the core flavors of the dish. These flavors were reminiscent of the classic Hawaiian poke dish with its salad-inspired seafood fusion, but with Peruvian undertones. This earthy appetizer was a incredible introduction to the Chef Erik Ramivez's Peruvian-inspired menu.

Avocado Toast, Maitake Mushroom, Roasted Jalapeño, Arugula

Beneath the layer of arugula laid a silky blanket of poached egg and avocado that coated the toast. With its remarkable seasoning and texture that so effortlessly breaks in your mouth, these unique maitake mushrooms were a wise choice to cast as the star of this gem. The accompanying salted chips offered a crunchy variation to contradict the chewy toast. Recommended to us by the servers, this dish certainly lives up to its compliments -- a perfect Peruvian twist to a traditional brunch item.

TL;DR: 
Price Range (per person): $25-30
Along with its unconventionally appetizing menu, Llama Inn's relaxed patio-like decor definitely enhances the experience and adds to the luscious food and refreshing cocktails they offer. Although not suited for anymore than a party of 2-3, Llama Inn is a perfect venue to visit -- be it a late afternoon cocktail or a lunch with a South American fusion flair you're craving -- to catch up and converse with a friend. (4/5)

Insider's Notes: 
Be sure to make a reservation if you wish to be seated at a traditional, "proper" table; after all, Llama Inn is in great demand. Especially for dinner services, seating options may be quite limiting, perhaps even nonexistent, without a booking.

Wow... what a great place!  
We came on recommendation and they didn't disappoint! 

Decor and vibe is super cool.... 

We had the beef stir fry, fried chicken sandwich and the tacu tacu ....YUM and all!!  3 home runs!  

A must if your in the area

we called around 7p on Saturday asking if they could accommodate us for 3 people. The hostess said they were fully booked but that we could come in and wait for a bar seat or for a canceled reservation. We came 15 minutes later and were told that the bar was now fully reserved and we could leave our phone number and they would call us when a spot opened up (over an hour they quoted). We left our number and went to have nearby but they never called us. We went and had a great meal elsewhere in the neighborhood.

I love Llama Inn. I'm not sure why, but it took me a while to go here. I had heard about it, I wanted to try it, but I never made a reservation. There were always other places that came above Llama Inn on my list. This, I regret. Llama Inn is an incredible restaurant and I am sad it took me 2 years to realize that. 

If you have visitors in town or you're just hungry for something different, this is the place to go. This menu does something special that not many popular restaurants in NY have done. It has a list of dishes that are familiar, but they are done in a unique way with more flavors than I can count. 

The service here is also exceptional. The staff is extremely knowledgeable about each dish. They won't turn away a crowd that says "whats good here", they will welcome you with open arms and give you an overwhelmingly large list of options with incredible detail on how each item is prepared.

Don't come here with one other person. Llama Inn is better suited for a group. You will want to order half the menu.  

We ordered: Fluke Civiche, Chicken Thigh, Scallop, Pork Belly, Quinoa, Broccoli with Beef heart, Branzino and Beef Tenderloin. Honest, I loved everything we ate, I can't think of a single dish that we thought, "never again". That being said, go with your gut, order everything that calls your name, and get ready for one of the most delicious meals in BK.

Easily the most overhyped experiences in my New York dining career. Pretentious LA-like architecture, ceviche drowned in a cloying sweet red berry sauce, an ill-thought out paella-like entre which buried fried calamari and soft, unfried mussels in rice, resulting in an unpleasant textural clusterf***....The pork belly amuse bouche was good and maybe the 80 dollar shared dishes are worth it, but overall I'd say anything in the middle of the menu is middling at best.

Great ambience and food, though the tables were a bit close to each other. It's tapas style, so Its a great gathering place if you're looking for a good dinner spot with good drinks with friends. 

We had the purple potato, beets, sweet potato, and branzino. I would definitely come back.

We came here for brunch and I got the French toast. It was tasty but pretty dry, so I don't recommend. All my other friends liked their food, and the place is adorable! I had to ask the waiter twice for water so the service wasnt amazing, but overall it's a solid brunch spot

Went to Llama Inn with a friend a few months ago.  We had a reservation and were seated promptly.

The space is medium-sized, dark, and intimate.  There are a lot of booths, as well as high top seating lining the windows.  Service was good.

I tried the following dishes:

Japanese Sea Bream Tiradito, Persimmon, Ginger, Huacatay (3.5/5): This was a good sea bream.  I really love sea bream (madai), so I order it whenever I see it on a menu.  It was pretty good, but not amazing.  The fish was good, but I tend to prefer a more Asian style sea bream.

Purple Potato, Rocoto Ocopa, Peanut, Fall Seeds (3/5): Decent potato dish.  However, it was not really very memorable.

Beets, Chicha Morada, Pear, Sunflower Miso (2.5/5): This dish was okay.  The beets were good, but I did not like the sunflower miso.  Overall, this dish didn't do it for me.

Sweet Potato, Goat Cheese, Chancaca, Andean Pesto (4/5): This was my favorite dish of the savory choices.  The sweet potato was really well-cooked and a nice consistency, and it went really well with the goat cheese.

Peruvian Chocolate, Banana, Algarrobina, Walnut (4/5): This was my favorite dish of the night.  The dessert was really interesting and contained a bunch of different textures.  The chocolate was not too sweet, and I liked the mix of ingredients.

I also had a few drinks, all of which were good.

I had a good experience at Llama Inn and would be open to trying it again.  However, very few dishes stood out to me as great.

If I could give more than 5 stars, I would. This place is truly truly special. I went last night for the first time and I already feel compelled to get my Yelp review up the next morning. Here's the breakdown:

Ambiance: The restaurant itself had great energy. It's not too big, not too small and with a really perfect ambiance. They have a cozy little rooftop above the restaurant where you can sit and have a drink before dinner, which is what we did, and it was a great way to start the night. For dinner, we set at the Chef's Counter, which puts you right on top of the open kitchen concept, and creates a really great dining experience. We got to watch them prep and cook the whole time and interacted with the chef's throughout. Big shoutout to SERGIO who was awesome and interacting with us the whole meal. He was an all star!

Food: Hands down, one of the best food experiences I've had in my life. Period. I lived in South America for 6 months and have a pretty good pulse for good South American food, and this place is the real deal. The menu is divided into some appetizers/ceviches, skewers, and then some larger plates. We got a bunch of different skewers (pork belly, scallops and shrimp) and each was amazingly delicious. You can watch them cook the skewers right in front of you over wooden coal which creates a beautiful smoke. The scallops and pork belly specifically were 2 of the best bites I've had. Both were beautifully cooked and seasoned, with incredible sauces and garnishes to accompany, which just created amazingly balanced and delicious bites. Really special stuff. The showstopper no doubt is the Lomo Saltado which is a traditional Peruvian beef stiry fry. I've had this dish many times before, and this one was no doubt the best I've ever had. It was also probably one of the top 5 dishes I've had anywhere in my life, across all cuisines. It's a beautiful medley of the most tender and beautiful tenderloin (it eats like beautiful chunks of filet mignon). Those tender, juicy, delicious pieces of meat were so delicious. They are accompanied by wonderful stir fry veggies (onions, tomatoes, scallions, etc), and then topped off with a bed of fries. All of that is soaked in mouthwatering brown gravy/sauce that is not too heavy, not too light, and just perfectly delicious. They serve it with scallion pancakes to make a wrap with it, as well as some spicy chilis, a delicious sauce to put in the wrap and some guacamole. Believe me when I tell you that when you put all of those ingredients into the scallion pancake, wrap that bad boy up, and take your first bite, you are purchasing a first class ticket to FLAVOR TOWN. All I could do was close my eyes and bask in the deliciousness that this place had created in this dish. Every bite was just this incredible balance of perfectly cooked meat, nice savory and acidic veggies, wonderful fries to soak up the sauce, a home-cooked scallion pancake, a little kick from the chilis and sauce, etc... I was in awe of what this place had created and still am. If it sounds like I am going on and on about 1 dish, it's because it really was that good. Oh, and once you are about halfway through the dish, they bring you out a side of white rice to throw into the dish and soak up all that sauce. What a dream. 

Everything else -- the service, the drinks, the vibes -- it was all great. Shout out to VICTOR as well, our server, who was an amazing guy and was super accommodating throughout. In a city with thousands of restaurants to choose from across every cuisine this world has to offer, it's rare that I am truly blown away by a restaurant, but this one took the cake. I am already planning my next trip back.

Thank you Llama Inn for such an incredible culinary experience!!!!!
As a Peruvian...mediocre at the very best. Now I know why I haven't seen a single Peruvian here.

The tastiest dishes were the skewers...scallop, pork belly, chicken thigh & shrimp (in that order). If I went back I would stick with those in multiple. Ceviche was watery & nothing exciting. Broccoli & beef heart dish was good but nothing I'd die for. Sea bass in dashi didn't really fit into the palate, and by that point we weren't that hungry. Cocktails yummy & service excellent.

I've eaten at a lot of amazing restaurants in New York but this is without a doubt one of the best. Every single thing we tried was outstanding. "Wow" and "oh my god" were commonly repeated phrases throughout the night over how delicious the food was. My boyfriend is from Peru, and also a foodie, and he thought it was outstanding. Often you'll find a restaurant with really cool vibes that lure you in but the food is ok, but this had both. Great environment/style/vibes and top notch food. We clapped for the chef and kitchen. Definitely coming back and soon.
Amazing food and drinks -- scallops, chicken, ceviche, purple potato, lamb neck were stand out stars. Cocktails were fantastic too. Call ahead and ask to sit at the bar to avoid a wait

This place is ridiculously overrated. Portions are laughable, so my boyfriend and I had to order 10 items to start feeling SLIGHTLY full. The only thing on this menu that is worth writing home about is the lamb dish, everything else is fine but not amazing and certainly not worth the heavy price tag. Between two people, we spent $240 and went to get a slice of pizza after.

Llama inn has a small brunch menu and it's expensive for its portion size, I would give them a four stars if their portions were bigger, cause we did have a really good beef tenderloin and everything else was pretty good too, just disappointingly small portion sizes.

It's Brooklyn baby! As we pulled up to the restaurant next to the highway I thought the place looked cute and interesting. The reviews were fairly solid and our friends had recommended the place. 

We sat at the bar and the atmosphere was pretty good. The bar was nice and the place was full (at first). We reviewed the menu and it was extremely limited. We started with the ceviche which was great but the rest of the food went downhill fast. We got the signature tenderloin which was 75% French fries and 25% meat. Highly disappointing for $75. Also, the beet salad was so over salted and just plain not good. 

This place is Manhattan pricing with Brooklyn service. As the place cleared out by 10 my wife waited 30 minutes for another glass of wine which was crazy as half the bar was empty. Don't bother to go out of your way to visit this place. Just not worth the trip.

This is such a cute spot . I loved their ceviche, drinks and lomo saltado. It's definitely a place to splurge , their plates are tapas style for the most part and then the entrees are to share . I would say , ask your server on what they recommend before giving the menu a go , it's a bit complicated .   The waiters are super helpful . They also have a rooftop, be sure to check it out . I went for my sisters birthday and a group of 5 of us spent $500 with tax and tip included , so be prepared to spend .

Definitely lives up to the hype. 
Deserving of its bib gourmand rating.
Elevated Peruvian in a overwhelmingly restaurantized, hipsterized, and gentrified part of Brooklyn(in a good way).

Visiting from Behind the Orange Curtain in SoCal for friend's wedding. Got rec from Eater NY. Made Friday night 8:30 pm reservations 2 weeks in advance. Nice setting w roof deck. 

Started w squash w corn and green onions-pretty damn good. Then had the tenderloin(essentially their version of a loma saltado) which was fantastic. Pricey at $74 but a lot of really good food. The steak was super tender, flavorful and cooked a perfect medium rare. Accompanied by veggies and fries on top and 6 awesome chive tortilla/pancakes and rice. Enough food for two. The couple next to us had the Branzino which looked awesome too.
Friendly and passionate waitstaff.

2 private cans in back. 
*AC kinda anemic on 90 degree 90% humidity July day( what a wimpy fucking coastal Californian I am)

There are so many great restaurants in Williamsburg and tbh I just thought everything on the menu was about $6 more expensive then it needed to be. For that reason, this restaurant feels like a place you really don't need to visit more than once. We got about 8 of the skewers (which are about 2-3 bites each--each order is only one skewer), the beef heart and broccoli (the beef heart is like a thick cut pastrami and very tender), the beets, and the lamb neck and the seafood & rice entree. I really recommend the lamb neck--super delicious-and the beet salad with the delicious miso (not too overwhelming--more like a smoky peanut butter). Some of the skewers are almost swimming in mayo which is a shame esp. the scallops. Also, the kitchen coursed our food out oddly. We had finished out entrees and were about ready to wrap things up when out broccoli suddenly came out. We had totally forgotten we had ordered it and would have probably liked to have it before our entrees but you know, whatever. They also didn't have any specials which I thought a bit odd given that caliber of restaurant. I can't speak to the cocktails because we were on the roof on a hot day so we were just drinking beers. Lovely staff and lovely ambiance and a must visit but you'll get the gist after one visit. Left satisfied but not really interested in anything more.

Amazing food, service and flavors. Drinks were great, the service was flawless and it was fun to sit at the chef's counter and follow the action in the kitchen. The food was incredible! Loved every single thing we ordered. Will definitely come back, hopefully soon!

I have been looking for coming to this restaurant for a while and last night I have a chance to step in. I notice that the restaurant seems to be booked all the time but I didn't have the reservation, just walked in. The host told me only seats available were on the bar which was I didn't mind. 

It was crowded on Friday night and took a while for my food to be served. Food is delicious every single dish. Service is good and friendly. There are rooftop seats that look very interesting, maybe I will try next time.

Ate here twice during my stay in Williamsburg - once for dinner and once for brunch. All the food a cocktails were outstanding. Service was great. We ran into a bit of an issue with the timing of our main course and the staff was very apologetic and got us some complimentary drinks and snacks while we waited. Only complaint is that they're menus are obscure and difficult to navigate for GF and DF diets and they struggled a bit to come up with alterations but the food we ended up ordering was great.
Probably the best Peruvian spot I've tasted thus far. I doubt anything would top this place. The ceviche is to die for. Customer service awesome, and ambiance was perfect.

Food here is amazing. I definitely recommend trying to sit at the bar around the windows and people-watch.
Stick to smaller plates and have more choices rather than getting one of the big plates.
Get any and all of the available ceviches. They're always the best thing on the menu!

We had a 9:00 reservation for two on a Saturday night. Even with  the reservation we weren't seated until about 10 minutes later 9:09.
It's definitely wise to make a reservation as many came in to ask for a seat even one at the bar but everything was full and there was a long waiting list.
For the most part I loved the ambience. The dim lighting and candles at the table really work because the long windows bring in loads of light from outside. There are house plants that line the tops of the wall and a few interesting art pieces. I love how the bar is at the center and that the seating forms somewhat of a U shape around it. The bartender was extremely friendly, he continued to check in with us as we were waiting to be seated.

Loud,
The restaurant is very noisy. It's not good for firsts dates, can't hear the person across from you. Music is loud but not loud enough for you to hear the words, only the bass and the beat.
The people around us were pretty loud so I had to keep repeating and asking to repeat.
On the service-
Our server Victor was not attentive and didn't even try. He never asked how our food was or if we needed anything. However,he managed to ask the table next to us constantly how everything was going. He made jokes and suggestions and asked whether or not they wanted dessert. He even went so far as wiping down their table after each dish was cleared in preparation for the new one. For us, he tossed the menu on the table and pointed to the desserts without making eye contact and never wiped the table. It also took him 7-10 minutes to get our check after asking for it.

On the food-
None of the food was my taste. A lot of it was new flavor combinations that I'm simply not used to and didn't enjoy but I recognize that everything was cooked well and displayed on the plate in an attractive manner. I don't want to comment on the food for that reason. My partner enjoyed his food and finished my plate for me.

The drinks have interesting names and very unique combinations, you should definitely try one or two! 

Side note:
Bathrooms are gender neutral

My overall review is 2.5. Overall decent restaurant it just doesn't match my tastebuds
Nice atmosphere and great drinks! The food was good, but not amazing. Def a nice spot to grab a drink.

Amazing! This is our second time at Llama Inn! The atmosphere/interior is so open and refreshing. I had a bloody Maria and the brunch omelet (same as last time) and it was just as good as I remember it!

Our waitress was lovely, attentive and ensured we had a great experience. If you need a solid spot to take family/friends in wburg - this is your place!

Overrated.

The food is good but so is the fare at a dozen other nearby restaurants, the decor is excellent too but so is decor of those other places. So why is it that this specific place is so popular? Is the food better - no. Even though it's good, is neither here nor there. Not exquisite enough to warrant coming back nor homely enough to bring back memories. With my wife we spend a little fortune on restaurants and know the culinary area very well - this place so absolutely forgettable.

My favorite dinner spot in Williamsburg. Always incredibly creative and delicious dishes and the cocktails are so good. Don't miss the quinoa with banana (trust me) or the pork belly and chicken thigh skewers. This is a perfect spot for a birthday celebration, date night or casual brunch. The inside is full of beautiful artwork and foliage and it makes you feel like you're in some South American oasis. If you're just visiting NYC I would say Llama Inn is a MUST!

Nice ambiance and tasty food options (ceviche, anticuchos, etc.) that are on par with genuine Peruvian flavors.  Solid cocktail options.  Service is good as well.  Had a great time with the family going there.  Would go back.

This is very rare, but I actually don't have the words to explain the explosion of flavors the food had last night at this restaurant. So much so that I'm still daydreaming of it the next day and wanting to relive it over and over. They took Peruvian food to a whole new level. I'm a huge foodie and this spot is a MUST TRY. First off the decor and vibe are great. Rooftop is adorable. We were seated at the bar which we were hesitant about but soon after did not care. Every appetizer, every sauce, every bite just got better & better. And our bartender/waitress gave us a shot which we were told to chase with a spoon full of the sauce from the charred octopus ceviche. OMG. It was an experience. A moment that will always stick out in the mind. 
Get a bunch of apps and the beef stir fry, their version of lomo soltado. It feeds 6 but the 2 of us pretty much devoured it. I never say this but it was orgasmic. 
And management was super friendly and attentive too. 
Great place in Williamsburg to eat and be happy.

Ugh, amazing! Ate myself into a food coma, racked up a bit of a bill, absolutely NO REGRETS!! My boyfriend and I walked in at around 9 on a Saturday night with no reservation. They were busy, but took our number and quoted about 45 min to an hour wait for seats at the bar. We went to grab drinks next door, and they texted us back to seat us in about 40 minutes. 

We ordered: 1) Charred octopus ceviche with crispy squid: oh my lord. I was unaware that ceviche could taste like this. Indescribably delicious, MUST get. 2) scallop skewer: super tender, delicate, perfectly cooked scallops with a delicious sauce and crispy fried capers. Soooooo good. 3) chicken thigh skewer: yummy, but nothing to write home about. 4) steak stir fry: I literally just sighed thinking about this. Super juicy and perfectly seasoned chunks of steak with charred scallions and other less noteworthy things in a very savory gravy, buried under a mountain of French fries and topped with some creamy sauce. They gave us extra sauce in a bottle on the side which was . Also guac. You're supposed to wrap the steak in these pancakes that come with it like tacos, but I found the pancakes were not adding a ton to my experience so I saved my stomach space for steak. 5) ordered a couple drinks off the Peruvian tiki cocktail menu, both were absolutely delicious and unique - unlike typical cocktails you might see elsewhere. 

So, we definitely ordered too much food for two people. If I were to do it again, I would have liked to have a third person there to help us with this amount of food. It ended up being a bit pricier than I was planning, but this was SO WORTH IT. Decor was beautiful, ambiance on point, amazing service. Would be a good date spot, but my boyfriend and I both fell asleep immediately after getting home so beware of too much steak if you're trying to get romantic

Came here for some bites at the rooftop space. 
Cute small rooftop I think only open in summer? 

Tried the skewers - pork, scallop, beef heart, all three are delicious, with unique and amazing seasoning. But I think they can even reduce half of the amount of sauce, a little too heavy on the flavor and overpowering the original flavor of the meat itself. 

Beef Heart + Kale salad - very good really like the texture/mixture of this dish (kale, broccoli, nuts, sliced beef heart, sauce) great flavor as well.

The food can be heavy. I suggest starting with the fish ceviches, there are usually 2 and both superb. The later dishes is where it can start to weigh you down. I love the large steak and the large fish. Most of the dishes are quite saucy, flavorful and bold. There are great cocktails and some cool wines on their eclectic list. The staff is fun and always on point. They give a little personality which I appreciate. Check out the upstairs if weather is nice. My friends are bonkers for the skewers. Prices in general are a little on high side. Beautiful unique decor

Impressive sounding dishes but lackluster in the execution - i.e., big pile of messes with flavors that fight not compliment each other.  Servers try their best to cheerfully up-sell but unfortunately even they know it's just overpriced garbage.  Hostess is clueless to boot...

We had an amazing, truly delicious one of a kind meal on the rooftop on Monday. The food and service was SO GOOD that we actually went back the next day to celebrate my mother's 80th birthday. Highly recommend their lomo saltado family style special, the bronzino with peanut sauce, and both ceviches (which are the 4 dishes we repeated on the 2nd night). We will definitely be back.

Nuevo Peruvian. The pork chop is a must try. It is the most tender and flavorful meats I have ever had in my life. We had the scallops which is on one skewer, bean salad and octopus ceviche was one of the other delightful highlights. I will be coming back.

Just left the restaurant and well I was underwhelmed. I guess, I was expecting something else?? I wouldn't go back as there's other places that aren't as pricey and more tastier. I did like the service and our server was super nice. She went above and beyond as I asked her about sitting on the rooftop. There was seating, but only the bar area. We declined.

Anyways, we decided to order the llama del Rey  and llamarita for drinks. The del Rey drink tasted like sangria but with a slightly different kick. My friend has the other drink. 

For the food we ordered the locro, fluke ceviche, mariscos, chicken thigh skewer, pork belly skewer, and scallop skewers. The skewers were great, but the locro which tasted like mashed squash soup was interesting. The fluke ceviche was good as I liked how everything was seasoned and the fish was good too. Otherwise, everything else was subpar. Yea, I wouldn't go back especially for the over priced entrees.

I would consider myself to have pretty high standards for NYC restaurants, and Llama Inn was by far one of the best restaurants I have eaten at. I literally reactivated my Yelp account to log in to write a review for how much I loved it!! Every single dish we ordered was seriously amazing - flavorful, colorful, unique, different than anything else I have ever tried... I cannot recommend this place enough for a fun get together with friends, a nice dinner date, or a trendy place for drinks (the plants and décor are so cute inside). Highly recommend the patty pan squash, beet salad, summer beans and stracciatella, the quinoa salad was amazing, and the beef tenderloin was one of the best dishes I've had in a while. Also the wait staff goes above and beyond and were so nice and helpful, and genuinely kind. It is 100% worth the trek from Manhattan to Williamsburg to try Llama Inn! 11/10!

I love this place so much my friends and I try to replicate the dishes. The restaurant is really beautiful with the big open windows. The locations is very unassuming. Good is always extremely depictions and amazing cocktails as well. 

Highlights:
Pork shoulder
Ceviche
Beet Salad
Quinoa Salad
Beef tenderloin

Heaven for your tastebuds. Don't waste another second.

Don't come here looking for a llama hotel and/or llama. And definitely don't come here without a reservation. Located in Williamsburg-North in Brooklyn, Llama Inn serves up some of the finest Peruvian cuisine I've ever tried. It's a little pricier here than your typical Peruvian fare, but definitely worth every bite and sip.

From their drink menu, I chose one of their Llama Classics called the Llamarita. Made with tequila and mezcal, it tasted of almond, avocado, and lime together and topped with a rim of cinnamon salt. At a price of $16, it was worth every penny and more.

From their food menu, the skewers are found within the second group of items from the top. We ordered three skewers (Scallop, Pork Belly, Purple Potato) and they were all so tasty.

One of my favorite dishes was the Rock Shrimp, Mussels, Clams, Calamari, Aji Panca, English Peas, Rice. Yup.. that's the name of one dish from Llama Inn's menu. They really spell it out for you. Anyhow, this dish was amazing and I highly recommend it. We also tried the Charred Octopus Ceviche, Togarashi, Avocado, Crispy Squid and loved it as well. Ordering on the first visit might be a little difficult, but our server took the time to explain the whole menu beforehand and she gave very detailed answers for any questions that we had.

As mentioned earlier, reservations are a must. Without one, you might be turned away. Go to their website at www.llamainnnyc.com and book an available time slot and seating arrangement. We were able to find one or two open slots for the next day. Would definitely come back here again!

We were really really poorly served by one of the guys with a kind of a long hair in a ponytail.I don't remember his name because but the service was absolutely terrible...


The whole atmosphere it's not service minded at all they don't smile they throw your drinks at the table without looking at your face when you say thank you they don't even look back it's a kind of place I would never return

another excellent meal. Can't beat the fish in banana leaf. Really appreciate the kitchen staying open longer to accommodate our groups need to keep eating.
2nd time and will be back again

Service and food were spectacular! We ordered the Pork Chop, Fluke Ceviche and a Quinoa Salad along with some skewers at the beginning. To drink the Llama del Rey and a chocolate dessert at the end that was great! 5 stars!

Great time here. Waiter was very helpful with Gluten friendly items. Even made a custom gluten free menu for me (which I uploaded).
Great dinner, great drinks, great ambiance. Will definitely be back.

Not like and Peruvian Restaurant I have ever been to, it was a unique and delicious cuisine!! Excellent food and drinks and the dessert we had was to die for. Service was very efficient and the environment was wonderful. An amazing experience!!

This place had great food, just a little pricey. The octopus ceviche was amazing, super fresh. I got the quinoa cashew bacon dish which looked very simple but the flavors were really complex. My friend had the paella which was also delicious and filling. It was a light meal for the expensive price, but we had great service and a wonderful experience.
So delicious. Dinner and now brunch. Live this place! Also, the dry aged ribeye burger is the best burger I've ever tasted.
It's as if they took a meatpacking restaurant and gave it Williamsburg chill flare. Will skip next time!

This place is incredible. Stylish decor, gorgeous bar. The share plates are unique and so delicious with such unique characteristics. Cocktail game is strong and the semillion wine went well with all of our courses. Oh and nice the fact it's open past 10pm.
I'm really a fan of the ambience here I'm glad that I came here with my friend and was able to enjoy the great experience. Definitely will come back again next time I highly recommend this business.

This place is spectacular! It's like a bite of Peru in good 'ole Williamsburg. You can get small bites, medium dishes, or a solid entree. No matter where you sit on the hunger spectrum, there is a spot for you. Sure, it certainly is a bit pricey, but the taste is well worth it. The combination of flavors and textures brought to the table leave your mouth wanting more. You'll wake up thinking about the dinner you just dreamed of, happy that it's a reality you can return to. Thank you for the food and service, Llama Inn-- I'll certainly be back.

This place was incredible! The skewers were amazing (as was the rock shrimp). Definitely on the pricier side, but overall enjoyed my experience and will be coming back. Thought the inside decor was nice as well!

People's expectations of food & service change as you move from one price point to another. While the food is good, Roxana's service left a lot to be desired.

When a diner answers that it's their first time at your restaurant, you should explain the menu - especially when your menu lacks headers of the various sections. 

When you offer pancakes to eat with the remaining fresh cheese from a dish, you should communicate that to your colleagues so they are not constantly trying to take the dish away before the pancakes arrive.

When you work in the restaurant industry, you should know there are two copies of the credit card receipt and not try to take mine, especially when I've already handed you a neatly paperclipped stack of the restaurant copies. Probably also polite to wait another minute while we finish up the last bites of dessert. 

Food was good but nothing mindblowing. Avoid the shrimp skewer - never had a dryer shrimp in my life.
The food and service were very good. We had a really great experience. However, my husband and I both got sick afterwards. We think it was the quinoa, but were not sure.

Probably my favorite Peruvian restaurant to go to. Not a single thing I haven't liked yet. Even tried things I don't usually eat and these guys killed it. The drinks as well. Love every drink on their menu. My favorite has to be the one with purple potato.

First Of all.  This is a real nice place.  Cool vibe   Got there a bit early and had a cocktail at the bar. I asked the bartender for a "signature " drink.  Not sure what she made but it was good.  I tried to pay.  But they don't Take cash?  Sorry I am old school.   Take my cash.  Anyway sat down. It was quite busy for a Tuesday.  I asked the waitress for some wine and dinner recommendations.  She went right to the most expensive stuff. Which I could have done myself.  Anyway we ordered a bunch of different things off the menu. The food was real good.  Super flavor.  The lime pie for desert was great.  The phone reception was non existent which kind of stinks. All in all. It was a good experience. If you plan on going make a reservation

The table I reserved was ready, so we were able to sit right away.  Stylish decor, gorgeous bar. We ordered the scrambled egg and the tamal. Both were spectacular.  The share plates are unique and so delicious with such unique characteristics. Draft cocktails are on point and paired with a ceviche would make for a nice little (expensive) solo bar snack.  The skewers were amazing (as was the rock shrimp). Fluke Ceviche- I am not generally a ceviche fan and I really liked this.

My boyfriend and I came to llama Inn on a Friday night. I made reservations a couple of weeks in advance to get a prime time slot. The restaurant was very crowded when we arrived. Thankfully we didn't need to wait very long for our table. We started with the ceviche, which was delicious. Then we shared three skewers. We had the pork belly, chicken thigh and beef heart. We enjoyed them all but especially the beef heart. It was delicious. For our main, we shared their version of lomo Saltado. It was amazing. The sauce was delicious, the meat was cooked well and we really enjoyed it. It was was topped with many fries. Once we ate through the fries and were almost finished with the dish, the server brought over white rice to absorb the rest of the sauce. I thought that was great idea because it would be a shame to waste the sauce! Overall, the food and cocktails were great here and I would love to return!

That lime pie is OMG!!! Seriously, that delicious, buttery graham cracker crust topped with perfectly blended lime filling & torched meringue. I usually don't like lime pie because it's too tart but the chef at Llama Inn definitely has found the right balance of sweetness & tartness in this creation. I'm not a big fan of meringue either because it tends to be too sticky & sweet for my taste but lord, this pie defies all odds.

Everything my friends & I ordered was deliciously savory. Brunch was calling our names on a lazy Saturday morning.

And seriously, get that damn lime pie!!!

Great atmosphere but misleading menu. I took my wife here for her birthday. I'm vegetarian but she eats meat. It was her night so I was willing to compromise and just order something that could be modified. The menu descriptions were non existent. My wife is Peruvian so she explained most of the ingredients to me. 

We asked the waitress which plates could be modified into vegetarian. She pointed at a few and I ordered the Quinoa plate (without the Bacon). Listed on the menu as "QUINOA, BANANA, AVOCADO, BACON, CASHEW". 

At no point in the menu it said that the dish would contain (be soaked in) balsamic vinaigrette. When the plate arrived I was taken by surprise. I honestly can't stand the taste or smell of vinegar (or balsamic vinaigrette). I didn't want to ruin my wife's night so I just politely told the waitress I didn't like the plate and that I didn't know it had balsamic vinaigrette. 

The situation became awkward and the waitress, while courteous, didn't admit the menu omission nor apologized for the misunderstanding. My wife tried to be courteous as well and offered to take it home, even though Quinoa doesn't sit well in her stomach. We couldn't come to terms to having a waitress pay for that plate or for the food to go to the trash. More importantly, it was my wife's birthday and I didn't want to make a scene or argue about anything. It sits now on our fridge awaiting to be thrown out.

In the future I will ask more questions (at another restaurant) I just wish the menu and servers were more clear with what the plates have.

The food was good but not amazing. The service was great but not excellent (nor outstanding).
