Best place in Williamsburg! Kate, Chad, and Asa are the beat servers ever! Very knowledgeable and attentive! Such a nice team working atmosphere. Food is phenomenal! Must try's are the fluke ceviche, scallop, chicken and pork belly skewers and the whole Branzino! Omg and you HAVE TO TRY THE KEY LIME PIE! Best we've ever had in life! Favorite place in Williamsburg! Kitchen staff/cooks are so focused and consistent. We eat here once a week, make every other week and everything is always awesome. Bar staff is so talented. Katelyn is our fave and so precise! And the manager Chai is so nice! Must try!

Llama Inn was my groups choice for our holiday meal. Two of our 4 have dined here before and raved about it. We arrived 5 min late after calling to let the hostess know. We were seated immediately. Our server greeted us quickly and was helpful ordering a bottle and explaining the menu format. After we ordered the food came out quickly and it was delicious. Truly an amazing meal. However, after our 2nd course the server came over and started asking if we wanted more food. We informed our server that we were fine to order desert and that is what we did. The server came over two or three more times to ask if we wanted anything else but it was actually a pressured ask which felt more like "when are you leaving". Then when we got the check the server came over withIn twenty seconds to take the bill, we were not ready. While the quick service was appreciated it was especially rushed and pressured. We were a 4 person table that was in and out under 1hr30 which is standard average table time for a 4 top. When we told the hostess we felt rushed she told us they were pressed for flipping tables, which is valid but not the customers problem. I have hostessed at many restaurants before and know that 1hr30 for a 4 top is beyond good timing especially in New York on a Friday night. For 5 star food the service was rude and pressured. Might not return for the service alone.

I had llama inn saved in my "want to go" on google maps for a long time. Finally made it for an early Sunday dinner in December with hubby. The decor and vibe is a 100, great style, laid back but clearly meticulously planned. Lots of plants which quite frankly will always get you a high score in my book. We didn't drink because we had a late-night Saturday and can't bounce back like we used to but the cocktails looked delicious. We had a non-alcoholic drink, no clue what it was called but it was some sort of deep purple tea situation. 

As for the menu, I'm pretty disappointed to say I wasn't blown away by the food like I thought I would  be. There's a chance I set too high expectations, but it's New York where competition is steep so that's the price you pay. We had the octopus ceviche, every one of the skewers, and the paella-like entree. All were good, the octopus ceviche was my favorite of the order, but nothing was a major stand out or stuck out as something I needed to have again.

I'd probably go back for a cocktail and an app if in the neighborhood because I liked the ambiance so much but won't be making the trip back for dinner.
Don't come for an event haha the NyE menu was expensive as expected but got nothing for our money. Don't come
This cuisine is delightful! The wait staff was attentive and accommodated my allergy with ease. I will most definitely be coming back.

The cutest gem in Brooklyn!! I took my boyfriend here for his birthday and he was so content with the service, food and ambiance. I got the grilled octopus and it was literally cooked perfectly and my boyfriend got the rock shrimp dish and it was very delicious. The waiters were also very friendly and accommodating. I can't wait to come back in the day time and the summer time to be on the rooftop. My new favorite in BK!

The brunch wars are REAL! And when you are hungry you really can't play around in uncharted territory. The meal and space must be a proven area.... then there is Llama Inn. This would be our second time coming here, the first when they opened up a couple of years ago. To our surprise a couple of items we loved were not on the current menu. This is not necessarily a bad thing as it means they keep the menu innovative and fresh. 

The Tacu Tacu is delicious and their spicy ceviche was nothing short of fantastic. What really stood out for me was the LLama Side drink, which was amazingly tart and tangy. We also destroyed the rice pudding dessert, which speaks on how good it was.

The service was really on point, as our waitress was highly diligent, attentive and meticulous in making sure we were accommodated. It was a fun place to be in, the staff permeate the chill vibes, and all seemed to be having fun.

I Love that Llama Inn flipped on its head the perspective on what Peruvian food is. Taking those classic Peruvian ingredients and innovating the hell out of the menu. It is risky and bold move, but it works!! This is starting to make it's way into my classic book of brunch places to eat. =)

The food here is incredibly delicious. Everything has a unique taste and is well prepared. The only unfortunate thing is that the servings are very small for what you're paying. I wouldn't go if you're expecting to be full after.

Very cool atmosphere and good drinks however, this is absolutely not the restaurant to go to if you have a shellfish allergy. I have an allergy and scoped out the menu in advance and planned my visit accordingly. However, once our waitress was alerted to my allergy her face dropped and informed me that only two items (a quinoa share plate and a squash share plate) were options for me to eat. Every other item had cross contamination or contained shellfish ingredients not listed on the menu! I've never heard of a restaurant having "secret" ingredients that are major allergens (for example, their highly popular beef tenderloin stir fry contains oyster sauce which is unlisted). They were unwilling to substitute any items (which wouldn't have been that much of a bummer except the girl at the table next to us had an onion allergy and they accommodated her). Our waitress disengaged with us the rest of the night. A highly anticipated visit left us seriously underwhelmed (and hungry) considering the reputation this place has. I really wish they would list the allergens on the menu or have a footnote on its website to alert people with this extremely common allergy.

We took our daughters recommendation (Brooklyn resident) and had dinner at this unique "Peruvian"restaurant. We only had 1 night in New York and so we had high expectations-and we  were not disappointed!

We had a reservation (which is recommended) but arrived early and  they seated us immediately in a nice corner table. 

We had  the sweetest waitress, Kathryn S, who gave  us the lowdown on their unusual menu. This direction was super helpful and gave us a plan!

We chose to  start with the Quinoa With Banana, Avocado, Bacon, And Cashew which was crunchy and creamy at the same time?!  Very complex and satisfying. 

Next we had all or "around the world" of their antichulpos which are various meets and vegetables on skewers. My favorite  was the purple potato. My husband liked the pork belly. They are fairly small skewers so we were happy we tasted all of them!

For our main course we had the octopus (best I've ever had!) and the braised short  ribs also very good. 

Finished  with their key lime pie. 

Our only disappointment was our bottle of wine came  half way through our meal. (Not our servers fault-the bar was slow). 

Even considering this is NY with so many choices...
a perfect choice  indeed!

Not worth your money or your time! I was extremely disappointed by my dinner at the Llama Inn. There were three main reasons for this horrible experience. The first was the service. Our waitress aggressively up-sold us during the meal. We finished ordering and she was spitefully dramatic about the small amount of food we ordered. Given her appall with our order we decided to get two more dishes. We did not finish (or hardly eat) either of these additional plates. Large waste of money, which we anticipated, and the waitress ill-advised us on for her personal benefit. The second reason was the lack of flexibility with a limited menu selection. This restaurant does not have good enough food or revolutionary culinary techniques that warrant dishes that cannot be altered for their customers. I had even called and alerted the host of any restrictions. They assured me over the phone that we would be fine. They were incorrect and someone in my party was only able to eat one thing (a salad) on the entire menu (and she only avoids dairy and meat). The third reason was the fact that at our 7:30 (Monday night) reservation, they had sold out of their signature dish, which we had come to try. I will not be back and I recommend steering clear of this pompous, over-priced, let-down of a restaurant. New York has plenty of great places. Go anywhere else!
one of the best brunches I've had in New York- get it all!! Amazing cocktails and great service. Not the kind of food I eat normally but will now crave regularly. A must for any avocado lover!!

Amazing experience! The menu gives very little detail about the dish. Just the key ingredients so each dish was such a surprise when it came out. The waiter was very knowledgable and gave great recommendations. We had the chicken thigh skewer, ceviche and the winter squash with goat cheese.

I've come twice, the first time I would have never reviewed the place as it would have been far too harsh due to the amount of sodium they attempt to kill one with their salty but oh so delicious pricy carne asada. The second time I ask for less salt to which the kitchen aid (idk what their title is or why they had to interject) came to ask why and explain where salt was used and why............ They put salt in the sauce, on the meat and on the potatoes. I was baffled at all this salt and questioned, to myself the chef actually has the title of chef? I asked for no salt on the potatoes as apparently the sauce is premade and cannot be corrected and it seemed as if it would blasphemous to say none on the meat. Overall with less salt my heart raced less and my tummy was beyond pleased. Overall this place is far too expensive and only worth a venture if you have the funds and you're able to speak up to ask for food to be made in a way it won't end you. The drinks are phenomenal and I definitely will return on days I have paid off my bills. However for almost 80$ going to a butcher with sustainable meats is less expensive.....

Not sure this is a Peruvian restaurant, it feels more like it's an American restaurant trying to pass as Peruvian (I know, very confusing) 

Their food is not that good and portions are horribly small for all of the money you pay per dish. Drinks are ok, nothing crazy. Service is horrible, don't waste your time going unless you have a reservation. They won't sit you even if there are tables available. First time I went, made the mistake of not making a reservation and waited for two hours even though there were at least 4 tables empty, the hostess refused to sit us- what I call, a waste of revenue. We could've easily had 2 drinks each and eat in that time. After the long wait, we decided to leave and go to an actual Peruvian restaurant 5 minutes from there- Chimu Restaurant (go there instead if you're looking for good Peruvian food)

We, of course, had to come back because had to understand why the hype about this place, and this time I made a reservation! What a disappointment, couldn't believe I paid so much for so little and no quality and still horrible service.

Probably my favorite brunch spot in Williamsburg. They are a little pricier but the food is well made, well seasoned, and plated nicely. Their drinks are great too.  Aesthetically this place is one of the nicer looking ones. Definitely try the ceviche, sooooo good.

This place is absolutely AMAZING! Great staff, very restful and warm to everyone. 
Their menu has a different style of what we are use to for brunch but very clean, healthy, and fulfilling.

5 stars for your beef tenderloin + fries dish - YUM AMAZING.... maybe the best food ive had in my lifetime. hands down. 

however, giving you negative stars for your service. i am not picky when it comes to service but when I am paying 14 dollars for a glass of wine please do not take it away when the glass is still 1/4 full. also when your dishwasher is broken please do not take away the silverware that was already on our table (to give to another table) and bring us serving spoons instead. also do not try to cover up the fact that your dishwasher was broken by telling us that "the chef wants these dishes [ceviche and quinoa] to be eaten with serving spoons" -- when we have eaten here many times before and have never been denied forks for ceviche.

when the service is horrendous all night please double check that our bill is correct before dropping it at our table. lastly, please do not make me beg for something on our bill to be comp'd after i have already had to approach the manager three times to tell her that something went wrong with the service. the manager should have offered to comp something on our bill after the first 3 mistakes went down, not after the 10th!

either drop your prices or get your act together llama ! we love you!

After my hopeful first visit to Llama Inn, I will not be back. 4 ladies and I went for an international women's day brunch - we arrived promptly at 11am, both when they opened and at the precise time of our reservation. We were seated immediately since the place was still empty. The service, however, was some of the worst I've had in years. We were patient with the drink order since the drinks are mainly cocktails, which are good, but then when it was time to order the issues started to arise... first, a vegetarian was told that she couldn't get the breakfast sandwich without the meat patty. It's 2020 and you're in Brooklyn, be prepared for vegetarians and respectful - it's not like she asked for a shredded meat to be individually pulled from a dish, it was a patty. Then with the two sandwiches either salad or fries were offered - not a big deal until they arrived and the only sauce options were mayo of siracha - both work fine, until the bill arrives with individual charges for each sauce and an up charge for the fries that wasn't mentioned. It should be mentioned that although we all had a 2nd cocktail, we were repeatedly asked if we were done - it's a Sunday brunch that we're enjoying, not a dine and dash. All this to say, beware. You'll pay for a delicious meal in a fun environment, but there service will be poor and you'll spend $60 each on brunch.
Food was really good but had the beef tenderloin stir fry for $73 and it consisted of 7 small chunks of meat and some French fries on top.. Totally Overpriced

This is my favorite restaurant in NYC, but it's pricey, so a special occasion situation, not a casual weeknight dinner. The beef tenderloin is phenomenal and huge (and there is a... surprise at the end, so save some room!). The skewer appetizers are small, but very rich and flavorful. Cocktails are perfectly balanced, and the one with avocado doesn't... taste like avocado? It just has a slightly creamy feel. It's amazing. I would eat here all the time if I could. Also, I don't know why people are saying they've had bad service. I've only ever had excellent service, from bartenders, waiters, hosts, and bussers!

Llama Inn is a trendy space with a cool vibe. We sat at a window counter, facing the street with large windows adorned by hanging plants and candlelight.


The food is superb; we shared the tenderloin plate between the two of us and it was plenty (could easily stretch to 3 or even 4 if you're getting apps). The meat was tender and soaked in a delicious marinade.

We also tried the scallop skewer, which was very tasty. To complement the meal, I ordered a smokey mezcal cocktail that was mixed to perfection.

Prices are definitely not shy, but the food is high quality and well-prepared. The ambience is cozy and the service was friendly.

Definitely would recommend this spot to anyone in the area.

Love this place! We've been to Llama San too, which is great, but we keep coming back here. Incredible food, the fish sandwich is a home run. Great cocktails too and a very well thought out wine list with a lot of natural wines to choose from. We drank a skin contact Torrontes from Argentina which is incredible! Sad we haven't been able to go but it'll be our first stop once fun gs are moving again!
Thrilled you are now doing delivery/pick up but an you please stay open later? COVID-19 doesn't mean we are suddenly eating dinner hours earlier.

Im Live Yelping this review right now.  There is a reason fancy restaurants shouldn't do take out / delivery unless they are going to send you your meal in courses by bike or hand you your app while you wait outside.  Why do I say that?  Well it's because I'm standing outside of Llama Inn waiting to pick up my food.  It's been (checks watch) an hour.  I ordered food (checks sundial) two hours ago.  That food was not cheap.  The lady at the window was little to no help and obviously overwhelmed.  This is when an open kitchen concept is not such a good idea.  Why?  Well we can see how many people you have at the restaurant and the answer is....drum roll...three.  Three people.  There was a restaurant worth of people waiting outside and three people working.  No offense to them.  I'm sure they were trying their hardest.  But three?!?!?  So needless to say, a bunch of angry people waiting for expensive food outside in the rain.  Not a good combo

Great spot for dinner and drinks! Food was really delicious- especially the scallop skewer and sea bass ceviche! Outdoor seating was well done with plenty of space between tables. Temperatures were checked on arrival. Really enjoyed dinner out in the neighborhood!

I had an extremely negative experience this morning attempting to visit this restaurant. Upon arriving and checking in, and then waiting for the seater to arrange the table, I was asked to have my temperature taken. The lady administering the test told me that my temperature was 100 and that I needed to wait and cool down. I told her I was baking in the sun and that might be difficult. She told me "it doesn't matter, that doesn't affect it." Besides the fact that she was arrogant, she was incorrect. Infrared thermometers measure surface temperature and are absolutely affected by sitting in the sun. I asked if I could "cool down" inside where it was actually cool. She ignored me and said, "I'm just doing my job" again in a curt fashion, turned around and simply walked away. I was left standing on the sidewalk feeling belittled and embarrassed. We left.

Tatianna was the sweetest and super helpful! The food was incredible and uniquely presented. Tatianna was so welcoming and made our experience comfortable literally adored her. Will be coming back when in the area!

We've been to Llama Inn many times before and tonight was the first time we went back since the whole pandemic happened. I can say this is the safest I've felt while outdoor dining because of covid. The tables are very far apart and they give you a paper bag to keep your mask clean while you put it away. Everything else was as good as usual: great service, delicious food and amazing cocktails! The scallop anticucho is my personal favorite and I always order it, great way to start the dinner. We then shared a bok choy salad and some squash with corn dish, delicious. The fluke tiradiro is also one of my favorites, if you wanna go more Peruvian traditional get the ceviche. For cocktails Llamarita was our favorite that night. Llama Inn is one of our favorites place in Williamsburg and we are so happy they are open right now!

Be very aware that their booking system makes it very difficult figuring out how to book a table on the rooftop. I waited 2 weeks for a reservation and showed up and then it was not on the rooftop. I decided not to use the reservation and even though the management promised to to charge my credit card for a no show fee, THEY DID. So 50$ for absolutely nothing!

It's unreal that during a time that restaurants are operating at limited capacity some don't have the sense of good customer service. Last night, my girlfriend and I got to the restaurant at 8 without a reservation. The hostess tells us there is "nothing available until 915". We say, "great, sounds like a plan." She takes our number in case something opens up before that. We come back at 915 and she appears surprised that we are back. When she realizes what happened, she says she is going to do her best to get us in now, but when it's clear that it's not possible, she calls on the manager.
The manager comes out to talk to us and tells us that he's sorry but there's no tables available at the moment and to make a reservation next time. 
Asked him why the hostess would tell us hostess 915. He said, "she never told you you had a reservation," trying to make it seem that it was our fault. He also passive-aggressively criticized us for not making reservation plans earlier for our anniversary, which was just out of line.

The manager didn't even try to remedy the situation- instead he was abrupt and rude.
I'm not upset at the mistake obviously made on their part, I'm pissed at the way the manager handled the situation. 

Llama Inn, it's ok to make a mistake, but you should own it when you do. It's easy to take care of it, just don't be a dick about it. 

Sincerely, 
Previous Llama Inn fan
Amazing food and service. This food here actually has flavor and is original. I can't believe I just found it. Highly recommended.

5 stars for the food. Maybe a bit steep to have on a normal basis but thought it was well worth in terms of quality. Perfect amount for three people, with just some left over. Dressing on the salad was so good, we wish they bottled it up and sold it. Lots of nice contrasting texture in the ceviche. Sauce here was a citrusy concoction super refreshing, again wish it was bottled and sold. Skewers were amazing, beef heart was cooked well and pork belly was melt in your mouth. Get these. I wish I could have these all the time. The beef in the stir fry was also cooked perfectly, very tender chunks, in addition to the pile of fries was slices omg onions, cherry tomatoes, and lots of scallions. Love all the accompaniments too. And they gave us a tiny pot of rice for the end to sop up the sauce. The rice alone was so good. It had really subtle seasoning already and some fat added to it I think, not sure but I wish I had room for more. Key lime pie was a great way to round out the meal. Refreshingly tart balanced out by the sweetness of the meringue. 

Also random but love the plates and bowls they have.

The Good:
Food was incredible. Big bold flavors. Chef is clearly an innovator and a risk taker.
Skewers - Pork 10 (best bite all meal), Scallop 9, Beef 8.5, Chicken 8.5
Ceviche - Tilefish and Salmon. Incredibly delicate sauces with some great ancillary ingredients e.g calamari. 9.5 for both.
Whole chicken - always appreciate someone that can lead with this on a menu. Very smokey, perfectly crispy and tender. 9.5
Beef tenderloin/lomo saltado - beef couldve been a bit more tender. Great sauce with a nice kick. 9

The Bad:
Waited 20 minutes post reservation time for a 930pm. It happens. But the bad...waiter told us 5 minutes upon us sitting down that the kitchen was closing, to put all orders in right away. Make us wait 20 minutes...then rush us out!? We never felt that we could settle in to our dinner for 6. This was a celebration of what was a strange summer for all. 

Great food made up for the bad service. Would come back when indoor dining is back up.

10/10. Wow. Wow. Wow. I came here for brunch on a Sunday after nabbing a reservation through Resy. We arrived and went to the open window where we got our temperatures taken and was quickly escorted to our table. I looked at the menu and there was so many delicious and yummy looking dishes that I wasn't sure which one to get. We settled on getting the crab avocado appetizer, the beef tenderloin dish and the sausage dish. We also got 2 ice coffees.

First of all, the crab avocado dish was SO good. The crab was extremely fresh and had a bit of the sea flavor. It was not overwhelming at all and was very light and refreshing. 

The beef tenderloin dish is one of their most famous dishes and I can tell why. The french fries, the banana or plantain along with the tender beef tenderloin was magnificent. The flavors really complemented each other and each bite was exciting and delicious.

I had a piece of the sausage dish and it was just as yummy. Although I did enjoy my dish a lot more :)

The coffee had a bitter/sour taste to it which is interesting- maybe that's how Peruvian coffees are like? Regardless, it was a good ice coffee.

I can't wait to come back here- it's definitely going to be one of my go to spots!

What an unpleasant experience. I live in the building across the street and this used to be my favorite spot to grab dinner but never in my life have I been so disappointed by the management or the level of service and treatment at this establishment tonight. 

We were treated so passive-aggressively throughout our dinner, and when we mentioned that we had ordered the main meat dish several times, were finally approached by the manager who said that the kitchen was closed and that they didn't even ring our order. After joking about throwing in a complimentary desert for our troubles and not receiving our full order, he replied in a hostile manner that since we asked we are not receiving it. This treatment is not acceptable by any standard, and I have never felt so belittled at a restaurant in my life. I am a loyal customer at Llama inn and I never expected that this is how they repay their customers for THEIR mistakes.

Finally, when we wanted to clear the air and speak to the matter with the manager, he only responded with scoffing and mockery and such petty behavior. 

Wouldn't recommend. The service is slow, and mean, and I'm never coming back again. Thanks for ruining my favorite neighborhood restaurant!

We were greeted by a seemingly lovely manager who was nothing but nice and welcoming. I actually turned to my friends and said "Wow, he is so nice." Little did I know we we would be treated so passive aggressively by the end of our dinner. We were seated outdoor on the roof and a friend was using her vape, when we were told by the waitress that we were not allowed to smoke, we immediately stopped. Right after that they flipped the switch and were completely hostile even tho we were LITERALLY nothing but respectful and kind. We ordered the beef entree but received the appetizer beef skewers instead. Fine. Could have been a miscommunication. When we mentioned this to the waitress she informed us that the kitchen was closed, and that we hadn't placed the order for the beef entree, proceeding to say that she will call the manager. The manager, who I initially thought was very welcoming and kind, approached the table. When we mentioned that we ordered the beef, he reiterated that it might have been a miscommunication. My friend jokingly asked if we can get a free desert, he said, verbatim "I was going to give you a free desert but since you mentioned it I won't do it anymore" and walked away rudely and dismissively. We couldn't tell if he was serious or not. He was serious. For someone who was giving us nice banter and conversation at the beginning of the night, it's strange that a light hearted joke like that would trigger him so much. At the end of the night, I asked to speak with him to express my dismay at the service and his dismissive behavior. Instead of an apology, he was extremely petty and full on blamed US for their mistakes. No accountability, no responsibility, and no respect. It's not that hard to say sorry guys!!!!!

So i booked through Resy for a reservation for 2 ppl and then ended up canceling and making a new reservation for 3 at 30 min past the original time. I only booked because I saw their feature in Eater Ny for rooftop restaurants open right now during COVID and all I wanted for my birthday was one nice brunch with my fiancé and future SIL.There was some sort of mix up, probably on the end of RESY where the restaurant had my reservation as the canceled time but for 3 and I was deemed 30 min late despite showing up 5 min before my reservation time. Despite showing the manager the confirmed reservation I had, which I confirmed via text the day before, he was not willing to budge. My issue isn't with the mix up. My issue is with the attitude I got from the get go. As soon as I said my name, the manager was very rude and was not willing to be empathetic at all. He offered that we wait 30 min for a table or he could let us eat but we would need to be done in 1 hour. I begrudgingly accepted, simply because I thought maybe the anticuchos will be worth it. Big FYI: I chose this restaurant because as a Peruvian-American, I had really been missing my mother's food and cannot travel to home to see my family due to COVID. We did not get a table on the rooftop. We did not get a table even in the sunlight. We got a table in the very back on the sidewalk right next to the service entrance. And as soon as we sat down and I saw that very limited menu without anticuchos (btw called the day before to confirm if they would have them available for brunch - nobody answered), I just felt so defeated and left. Happy birthday to me!

We celebrated a belated birthday up on the roof after making a reservation. And basically sampled the menu. Highly recommend the summer squash and any of the appetizer skewers. We did do the shared main dish which we had separate plates of course. Staff is excellent! They provide a paper bag for your mask and hand sanitizer. Temperature checks are given at the door before you're seated. Rooftop is gorgeous!
Branzino and scallops are amazing!! Very good service! Shout out to brad, thank you for making my friends' birthdays special.

Came here for an anniversary dinner and everything was excellent! From the service to the drinks, down to the food. Llama Inn has a decent outdoor seating and even provided paper bags for our face masks, plus they take your temperature before sitting. My boyfriend and I appreciated the efficiency and cleanliness. Tbh, it was so good we forget to take pictures of our cocktails and food. Definitely will be returning!
One of the best meals I've had in NYC: in competition with 4 Charles, JeJu Noodle Bar, and Carbone. Absolutely fantastic and have already booked my reservation back. Thanks!

Hole in the wall gem! 
It is literally in the middle of nowhere on a corner and there's no other restaurants or shops next to it. Drove by plenty of times but never thought of coming here because the vibe is a bit weird since you're eating right underneath a highway where there's cars flying on top and next to you while you eat. Indoor dining looks really nice though but not opened due to covid. Menu is also limited due to covid but everything on it was pretty good.

Skewers 
The scallop, chicken and pork belly skewers literally melts in your mouth. Do yourself a favor and get your own order and then some more. Don't share these lol

Vegetables
Summer squash with cheese and corn was super tasty with the sauce. Waiter's favorite & recommended it. Approved by me :P

Salmon ceviche ... not big on raw salmon but my friend really enjoyed this dish.

Beef tenderloin stir fry came out overcooked and it is not worth the $76. This dish is WAY overpriced.  Presentation was cute though, guacamole came out in a little pot and scallion crepes in a little skillet/plate. Wouldn't get it again.. Don't get it.

Drinks - Cocktails were pretty pricey at $17 
Don't get the llammarita, it was really creamy / heavy for a drink. Tried to force myself to finish it since it was expensive but I couldn't do it.
El Chapo was recommended by our waiter and was the exact opposite of the llammarita. It was very light and refreshing but it kinda also tasted like straight up tequila lol

Great food but it wasn't worth $300ish for two people. I would like to come back to try their brunch though.

There's a reason the Llama family has stood the test of time. Mind-blowing, creative and thoughtful cuisine and great service. I can't say there's much like this in the NYC dining seen, and that's saying something. It's hard to get me to Brooklyn, so my willingness to venture here is also saying something. Llama Inn has made the necessary, COVID-related adjustments and is operating with impressive efficiency. A phenomenal outdoor dining option if you're in the neighborhood, but it's worth the schlep even if you're not!

We came here at around 8:15pm on a Saturday night. Unfortunately, we were not seated at one of the coveted rooftop garden tables, but rather on the sidewalk next to the highway. Okay, not the best start, but once I got over my envy of the diners up above, I reminded myself that we came to Llama Inn for the food and not to be performative and trendy. 

COVID measures: First, they give you paper bags to put your masks in while you're ingesting whatever it is you have in front of you. They'll ask you to put your mask on whenever you're speak with your server, but otherwise feel free to keep it off. I will say that it is quite windy next to the highway, so make sure that your mask bag doesn't fly away! Tables are spaced far enough apart -- everything feels very safe in that regard. 

The updated drink menu isn't on the Llama Inn website, but I can report that all of the drinks we tried were fantastic. Of what's online I can say I got the Llama Del Ray (complex, unique, punch-style, delicious and deadly) and my bf got the Touch of Evil (I don't drink Mezcal/Tequila but it was his favorite drink of the night). I'd also recommend checking out the wine list if you're into organic/biodynamic wine. Many unique options, lots of complexity there.

The food, as we had hoped, is the shining star here (as it should be). The menu is small plates-style, so it's recommended that all is shared. And you should take this route, because it will allow you to try more of the menu -- I assure you, you will want to do this. We were perhaps overly ambitious as far as number of plates ordered, but ultimately content with our strategy. The Llama folks are big into their ceviches, so make a special note to try at least one (they have three on the menu and I'd recommend two, they ain't like any ceviches you'd tried before). Eats, below: 

Skewers (one of each):
Beef Heart, Aji Panca, Rocoto Salsa: A-
Chicken Thigh, Fermented Soy Bean, Aji Verde, Potato Chip: A+
Pork Belly, Char Siu, Pickled Chilis, Spicy Majo: A+
The pork belly and chicken thigh were the winners here. The beef heart wasn't bad, just not quite as exceptional as the other two. Beautiful, colorful presentation. Bright and fresh. Incredibly flavorful. Good things come in small packages!

Bok Choy, Grapes, Sunflower Seeds, Huacatay Caesar: A+
This was a take on a Caesar salad and so delicious. Probably the largest plate we ordered, as it turned out, but it's very light. Still a rich, complex flavor profile and good texture going on too. 

Heirloom Tomatoes, Honeymoon, Qapchi, Sourdough: A-
Fresh, seasonal, tasty. Not mind-blowing but still very good.

Summer Squash Lorco, Queso Fresco, Candied Cancha: A+
The heaviest dish we ordered and well worth it. Rich and got us excited for fall.  

Fluke Tiradito, Aguaymanto, Poppy Seeds, Huacatay, Nasturtium: A+
I've said "fresh" a lot but it's the best adjective in many cases. Light, fluffy pieces of fish, beautiful presentation, flavorful and varied.  

Tilefish Ceviche, Aji Amarillo, Sweet Potato, Crispy Squid: A+
The funkiest (in a good way), most elaborate dish we received. I wouldn't think to pair "crispy squid" (a dressed up fried calamari) with a light ceviche, but it worked. Super creative, bold flavors as we had come to text, a nice transitional dish. More gorgeous presentation, great variety in texture.

I'd been to Llama Inn before (pre-pandemic), and was curious to go back in COVID times. I agree with previous reviews commending COVID safety. I received a text in advance of the reservation reminding me of the protocols, ensuring no one in my party had symptoms or was under quarantine restrictions, etc. Our temperatures were checked upon arrival, and we were seated at a table on their gorgeous rooftop with ample room in between us and other guests. Only thing I might add, which I've seen a few other restaurants do, is that they request the names of those in our party should they need to do contact tracing. Although maybe they feel like they can check that box by having the phone number/name of the reservation holder? Anyway, this was my second occasion dining out during the pandemic and I felt considerably more comfortable this time around. 

The food was incredible- just as I'd remembered. I will gripe a bit about the price - cocktails are around $18 on average, and $8 for an anticucho,  not to mention $76 for their take on lomo saltado, is a bit much. That having been said, I recognize that they're trying to elevate Peruvian food, and that includes "elevating" prices. This just keeps me from coming back more frequently, as the price of a meal here quickly adds up. 

Staff also let us stay at our table past the designated 1.5 hour period. I admittedly didn't realize there was a time limit until we were getting up to leave (nearly 2.5 hours later), when I saw that the menu included a note in fine print requesting guests stay no longer than 1.5 hours. Our mistake for not seeing this, but it was kind of Llama Inn to not force us out earlier on. 

All in all, a really nice time here and I look forward to coming back.
Service, food and space are 10/10. Get the steak if you're a meat eater. It was unreal!

Not that I tried all of their menu but it was just mediocre experience. Loved their bok choy salad
, their popular menu Beef tenderloin was very salty. One other thing about their service.. I know there's limited seating bc of Covid and all but the server came every 5 minute to see if we're leaving since 10 minutes after the food came.

Came here with some friends to catch up! Bok Choy salad, beef tenderloin, crab and avocado causa and the touch of evil cocktails were all delicious. The place itself is very cute and the playlist is perfect for a Sunday or really any day with friends. Nothing totally memorable that I would crave again on a random day but a great place to eat if you're in the area

My girlfriend loves Peruvian food so I took her here for a surprise date. We both really enjoyed the flavors of all the dishes and the seafood was incredibly fresh. We ordered the scallop appetizers, heirloom tomato dish, and salmon ceviche. The ceviche was definitely their best-done dish and anyone who goes here should at least order that. The only reason they don't get a 5/5 was because the service was definitely lacking. They sat us more than a full hour after our reservation and when we would try to inquire about our table the host was generally fairly rude. In addition, the serving portions were quite small considering the price. If you see in the picture, the scallop appetizer was like the size of my pinky finger and cost $8. We enjoyed the taste but definitely weren't satisfied or nearly full by the time we left.

Really glad this place is operating during COVID. They still have to work on time management so that those who come on time for reservation don't wait for too long. That said, certainly one of the best Peruvian meals. Must try is their Beef Stir Fry. Go hungry and bring company since the portions are huge. Decent cocktails to go with

To the Chef and Kitchen: your food has my heart.
I was blown away with the tang, sweetness and crunch.
Everything was beautifully presented and dish after dish, we were just amazed.

See you soon.

My favorite restaurant in Brooklyn (maybe all of NYC!).

Highly recommend making a reservation for the rooftop garden-such relaxing ambiance, you would never know you're basically on top of the BQE!

You know it's a good dining experience when you finish eating your main and realize you've barely touched your drink. The stirfried beef is the star (definitely share with 2-4 people) but don't sleep on the ceviche. I am not a sweets person but highly recommend you save room for the lime pie dessert.

I never would have though I'd love Peruvian food but it's my favorite thanks to Llama Inn!

This place sucks and is over priced and served me a bowl of shells with no seafood in them . I told the waiter he didn't give a shit and I won't be coming back . I've been in the restaurant business for over 37 years . Adios Muchachos . I hope you go out of business .

Love, love, love Llama Inn. Excellent location. Lomo Saltado is one of their most recommended menu items, I love it, and I think you really should try it too. Wonderful friendly staff. I highly recommend you try Llama Inn and I'm glad I found it.

Came here for dinner with a friend because neither of us have tried Peruvian food before. We ordered the chicken thigh and pork belly anticuchos as an appetizer and the beef tenderloin stir fry to share as our main. We also ordered the llama del Rey and Touch of Evil cocktails.

The highlight of the meal was definitely the skewers. Both the chicken thigh and the pork belly was cooked to perfection and the other ingredients on the skewers complimented the meat very well. Personally I preferred the chicken to the pork, but my friend was the opposite. 

The beef tenderloin was definitely very creative. It was a take on the normal lomo saltado, except it included many asian influences, such as using scallion pancakes (which were amazing, could probably just eat those by themselves). Beef was tender, and the dish was pretty good overall except maybe a tad bit salty imo, and I wish the beef to fries ratio was slightly higher. After we finished the majority of it, they brought out a bowl of rice to soak up all the sauce with, which was a nice touch. 

For the drinks, I preferred the Touch of Evil cocktail slightly over the other, but my friend said both were made very well and he knows a lot more about drinks than I do.

Overall, I would give this place 4.5 stars, but that's not an option on here.
how do you not have a working phone for customers to call. how can you send a $30 half chicken with no sides or sauce. answer your phone i have spent $1000s of dollars at your restaurant.
Great food! Loved the scallion pancakes and the lomo dish! The artwork is a great touch to the restaurant as well!Beef Tenderloin is a great dish! Highly recommend.

Overall pretty good food, great for sharing a bunch of small plates and trying a bunch of different things. The food is unique and pretty good.

I liked the skewers, came with a lot of variety and each one is flavored a bit differently. The salad was also surprisingly good as well.

I'd pass on the scallops though. That dish didn't end up tasting all that great, especially mushy risotto like sauce it came in.

Video Review here: https://youtu.be/uJ39GmFYFC0

(Disclaimer: The love in this food literally made me cry)

So, if I could give Llama Inn a 10 star rating, I would. My experience here, is absolutely unforgettable. One of my mottos that I live by as a food vlogger, is that I'm always lookin' for the love in the food, and at Llama Inn, I found love in the food, the service, the decor, etc. 
I went here for the second time this past summer (2020). I already knew from my first visit that this was true, authentic Peruvian Food, but they somehow, on this second visit, blew my mind even further. I made a reservation for just me. They sat me on their beautiful rooftop. The vibes are laid back, chill, bohemian, even. The server/bartender asked me what I wanted to drink and I asked if he could make me a Peruvian-inspired drink. He recommended the pisco sour, and girl, am I happy that he did. This limey, fluffy egg whites-topped drink was most refreshing and more importantly, tasty! The angostura bitters were sprinkled in the egg whites and it truly just added to the experience. 
For my first course, I had the scallop and the pork belly. I must say, the scallop was nothing less than perfect. Cooked beautifully with that creamy aji amarillo tarter sauce and salty, crispy capers that just made the entire bite a happy family. The pork belly was grilled for the kids, you hear me?! You tasted the perfect grill char. The rich fat of that pork belly made me feel like I had more money than I actually do! Perfect size starters. Not too big, not too small, but juuust right .
For the entree, I ordered the scallop aguadito (I know, more scallops, but SO worth it!) the scallops were served with the most warm, comforting romesco sauce on top of them, which really just warmed my heart! Also served with Swiss chard, rice, beans, and what seemed to be a salsa verde kinda sauce. Omg, this dish was prepared so wonderfully. Someone in the kitchen took their time to make this. Their first ingredient was love. I tasted it! 
For dessert, I had the lime pie, served on a graham cracker crust, covered in the most beautiful burnt meringue! This pie was to DIE for!!!! The most simple, yet, most well done crust. The lime pie itself was scrumptious! The perfect amount of tart from the lime, combined with the right amount of sweetness. 
Do yourself a favor and go to Llama Inn! A) You'll be supporting indie restaurants (and be sure to tip 20% or more) and B) You'll have a true food EXPERIENCE! Take my word for it! You will not regret going to this restaurant! It is one of my favorites in NYC!

TL;DR Final Verdict. Solid place to go for high quality food every once in a while. Food is very decadent and rich in flavor, and the service is top notch. A little pricey, but the experience was great. Now, let's break it down.

Atmosphere:
We made reservations for outside at 8:15PM Friday night, but called later in the week to move it to inside. They were happy to accommodate, and the inside of the restaurant is gorgeous! The outside section was full of heaters, and on a nice corner, but the inside is where you want to be. It's a little dark, and your table is lit by candlelight, and it's really just a nice environment. For this Llama Inn, you definitely get a 5/5!

Drinks:
The drink menu is full of unique cocktails and different wines and beers. I had gotten the Llama Del Rey cocktail, and honestly really enjoyed it. Basically, if you're looking for a red sangria, this is their version. Strong, but surprisingly refreshing. Could've had a few more if I wasn't driving. Highly recommend this cocktail. 5/5.

Appetizers:
For appetizers, we had gotten the beef heart and pork belly. The waiter was awesome, as we were skeptical ordering the beef heart, and said if we didn't like it he would take it off the bill. Well, we ended up loving it. Texture of a lamb chop, flavor of almost steak. Definitely would recommend it. The pork belly was the star of the show though, this is a must order. A little spicy, a little crunchy, what's not to like? Only problem was, they didn't explain it's only one skewer per order. It was described as though there would be two. While this is a basic miscommunication error (partly my fault also, not jut the restaurant), it would've been good to know. 4/5.

Vegetables:
We originally wanted the avocado and crab veggie dish, but they are limited quantity. The last one was sold just before we had gotten their, just my luck! Anyways, we ordered the potatoes, and they were great. Came in a cream sauce, definitely more then enough for two people. Nice side dish, but extremely rich! Cannot eat too much of it. 4.5/5.

Main Course:
Now for the star of the show, the whole reason we came. The beef tenderloin. At $76, it is pricey, but boy was it good. 7 pieces of what seemed to be filet mignon, covered in a mountain of french fries, and comes with sides as shown. The sides were scallion pancakes, guacamole, pickled peppers, and some sort of mild sauce. We made "tacos" for lack of a better term, and they were awesome. Only thing was, I wish their was a little more beef. That, and the fact that two of the pieces were very chewy is what brought this down to a 4/5.

Dessert:
Unfortunately, we really wanted the bread pudding, but it was 10PM so we had to get out of the restaurant. This isn't their fault at all, and I am not criticizing in anyway. If anything, I am praising them for saying that we had to leave instead of making that final sale. Next time, we'll be a bit earlier. N/A.

Bill:
The bill came out to be $167 for everything. This includes a 7% COVID Recovery Tax, as well as regular sales tax. I completely forgot about COVID Recovery Tax, so just keep that in mind. 

Overall:
The food was delicious, they took COVID precautions very seriously, and it was a pleasant atmosphere to spend almost 2 hours in. The food is very rich, so you cannot eat to much of it, but use those pickled peppers to your advantage to cut down on some of the fat. It'll be a once in a while spot for me, but I cannot wait to come back. If I could, I'd give it a 4.25, but because I cannot, my review will stay at a 4. See you soon, Llama Inn.

We made a reservation a week in advance and were turned away when we arrived. We were told they had made a mistake with another cancellation but the host didn't even TRY to fix it. After traveling in from Manhattan for dinner we were literally turned away at the door and no one even attempted to make it right. 

We even offered to come back later in the evening and it was just a "no". The icing on the cake was when they CHARGED us for missing our reservation. So disappointed in the mis-management. Notably in the past the same host here and at Llama San has been rude a difficult to deal with. 

The food is 4 stars from our past several times dining but it is really pricey and the experience upon arrival makes it not worth the price.

The good: 

The food and drinks here are amazing. Seriously some of the best food in New York City. They combine flavors that I never thought could work together. The drinks are great as well. Some stand-outs are the Quinoa as well as the Ceviche. Also, be sure to order their Pisco Sour cocktail. 

The decor and ambience of the restaurant is also great: it feels lively, modern and cozy all at the same time. 

The not-so-good:

They know they're good. With that knowledge comes a bit of arrogance. Their prices are really high even by New York City standards. I've gone here probably 10 times and I've had to deal with a manager who is not great in dealing with customers. There were a few times when I made a reservation and our table was not ready and we were forced to wait an hour and a half to eat. The manager did little to help and came off as rude. I understand there's a lot of pressure in being a manager or a successful restaurant but I can't help but think that their lack of good customer service makes this expensive outing slightly bitter.

We arrived a few minutes late for our 8pm reservation on 10/11. All was going well and we were seated about 8:10-8:15. We proceeded to order some drinks and appetizers. The waiter was nice and made some good drink and app recommendations. About 20min later, we ordered the chicken entree. The chicken took about 40minutes to come out. It was about 9:20 when it was placed on our table. My fiancé went inside to use the restroom and it was then that she was approached by the manager on duty the evening of 10/11/20 who told her that "they'd like to go home soon bc it was a slow night and theyd appreciate if we could wrap things up". It wasn't even 9:30pm. And we had just been served our entrees. The manager and a couple others were hovering around the bar and were heard laughing and saying "yeah it'd be nice to not be here all night".

My fiancé was upset. She felt disrespected and rightfully so. We're about to spend over $200 on dinner and they are rushing us and being rude while doing so.

I confronted the manager and told him there's no need to be disrespectful. I told him we've barely been here an hour and the food just came out. He yelled. He said he wanted us gone and tried to shut the door on me. I sat back down to finish our dinner. At roughly 9:38pm he yelled at us that he was calling the cops. He called the cops and lied by telling them "we refuse to pay our bill". At 9:40pm I called the cops too. At this point we felt we were being harassed. When the police arrived, I told him that we were in fact not trying to leave without paying and our party of 4 was still sitting at our table. He eventually told the cops he just wanted us gone. They asked us to leave. I tipped our waiter $40 and we left without finishing our meals.

Whoever this person was, should immediately be fired. To have someone like that represent your establishment is a disgrace. And a shame because the food at Llama Inn is really great. This was certainly not my first time here, but it will definitely be my last.

I came here last November and have fond memories of the Lomo Saltado coming out on a sizzling plate and generous portion sizes - well worth the $75. I decided to take a friend here on a special occasion and noticed the price of the dish was reduced to $38 and the server did call out the portion would be smaller, however, I was shocked to see the dish only come out with 4 bite size pieces of steak. Essentially you are now paying for  a pile of French fries and two scallion pancakes. If you want a refill on the guacamole or pancakes expect to pay another $6 for each. I probably will not come back after this experience.

Great food, extremely delicious. HOwEvErrr -- way too small for the price. Listen I know it's tapas. But you cannot tell me that one carrot cut into a million pieces is worth $15. Maybe $7... maybe. But like I said -- very delicious I just can't get behind the price for the portion. And the drink was sub-par. Solid 3.5-4 stars. 3 because the server also pressed us a bit on time even though we were fast.
This place did not disappoint. It was high end Peruvian like I've never experienced. Ordered the sunchoke, lomo saltado, and the ceviche. Can't wait to go back!

We sat at the chef's counter and I'll go ahead and say this was one of the best culinary experiences I've had thus far. 

Scallops: perfectly cooked. Literally butter the way they melt in your mouth (best I've ever had). Peruvian take on a mustard tarter. Add crispy capers... Order it. You won't regret it... 

Octo Salad: fresh. Perfect cook. Love that there was actually a lot of octopus plus a chill amount of Radicchio, so it actually felt like "salad."

Black cod: honestly, get it for the broth. Wanted to pick up the bowl and drink it. Cod was good, very crisp but honestly it was the broth that stole the show. 

Pig tail: did not want to order this and now I crave them on the daily. Think chicken wings, but more meat, crispier, and then even crispier.. with a soy base sauce. Step outside your comfort zone and do it. As our waiter explained, it's above the tail, not the actual tail. 

Bok Choy salad: so unique. The grapes must have been hand picked as they were only firm and crunchy. All of the flavors just came together. Nice crunch. Great way to finish the meal.

Michael (Mike) L... you're really good at your job. So entertaining. So helpful. Thank you for recommending the Pisco tasting. 

This was an incredible experience. True gem outside of the Manhattan bustle. Real sweat and passion goes into this food and I'm here for it. 

PS, all drinks were

This place is a real gem. Well laid out, beautiful space, welcoming staff, great drinks and, most importantly, amazing food. The sunchokes are a must (especially if you want to pretend to be healthy) and the lomo saltado was incredible - and this is coming from someone who doesn't usually care for french fries (judge your cousin). 

Sitting at the chef's counter was a treat in of itself, a gentle reminder of all the other great menu items I'll have to come back to try. 

RE COVID protocol, all staff are in masks at all times, guests are very well spaced out, place is kept spotless

The reservation...The hostess said they were completely booked for the night and said goodbye. As I walked towards my car, I checked online and found reservations after 9pm which she failed to mention.

Def not as good as precovid. For one, none of the entrees can be made gluten free and two dishes come out tiny tiny and also pretty salty yuck! I honestly was a bit disappointed with the food last night. Will not be back to this joint. Rather go ues Peru ceviche restaurant, mission ceviche.

I made reservations for brunch in their outdoor dining space about a month in advance. We arrived a few minutes before our 1pm reservation and they asked us to wait inside as our table was not ready yet. Someone was eating their dessert at our table and we ended up waiting roughly 20 minutes for our table. This was a minor annoyance. I understand a restaurant wanting to fit a table in before a reservation, but the point of making a reservation is so our table would be ready when we arrive. 

Our waiter was absolutely fantastic - he was friendly, personable, and a highlight of the meal. 

I had their Llama del Rey cocktail, with pisco, rum, wed wine, chicha morada, lime, grilled pineapple, and pink peppercorn. It tasted like a pisco sangria, which I loved. 

We split their Black Bass Ceviche and their Bok Choy salad as our appetizers. Both were absolutely delicious. The ceviche was fresh and light. The Bok Choy salad was really interesting. I've never had raw bok choy before, but I can see myself doing it more often now. 

For my main, I had their Tamal with Fried Egg and Aji Amarillo. Each bite was like a flavor explosion in my mouth! The tamal was moist and flavorful. 

X had the Beef Tenderloin and my sister had their Chicken Thigh Sandwich. Both were really, really good. I think next time I'd order the Chicken Thigh Sandwich because it was so tender and juicy. 

We finished the meal by splitting the Banana and Queso Helado Cake, which was just the right amount of sweet. 

Service was attentive and we never felt neglected while sitting outside.

If you haven't been here yet you are making a mistake. Everything from drinks to food to dessert is delicious. Favorite highlights are Fluke ceviche, Boc choy, and the beef dish. Everything is extremely flavorful and filling. We had 2 people and ordered 5 dishes and it was plenty. We sat outside in their "winter village" and Service was great. Will certainly return and can't wait for them to start up brunch again!

Lives up to the hype: delectable drinks & food. Highly recommend the bok choy salad - unique and flavorful. Sauce accompanying the scallops was also standout. 

Friendly service. Make a reservation in advance - saw several people being turned away BC restaurant was fully booked.
Llama inn never disappoints. Been multiple times and tried multiple dishes. Great service, food, ambiance and drinks.
Tasty Peruvian food! I really liked their cocktails to-go. Lots of different vibrant flavors and quality meats.

Had such an amazing time here. We made a reservation for a group of 7 on Sunday for brunch and they were super accommodating. We ordered everything tapas a style and basically just asked the waiter to bring out the favorites!

Out top choices were the tamal, the omelette, the camarones (shrimp), the sausage and egg sandwich, the ceviche and the beet and avocado causa!

Just get everything seriously it's so good. Also we had coffee and it was fantastic.

Celebrated my friend's birthday here last night, and def recommend. We were a group of 6, sat inside. It was small inside but the decor was super cute and love all the plants (outdoor area is where I wanna be seated next time we go back). We had small plates and shared tapas style which was great so we got to taste all the dishes! Friends loved all their cocktails especially the llama del ray. Honestly all the dishes were good! Was super pleased  got the bokchoy, scallops, asparagus, ceviche, octopus, sea bass, chicken, lomo, scallion pancakes. Everything was soooo good! Our server was excellent too! We had a great night, good vibes. Just beware, this place does charge a covid recovery charge 5% of the bill!

We had a next level dinning experience at Llama Inn. We arrived late to our reservation and rather than making us feel uncomfortable they made room for us even though they gave our table away. We started with Peruvian cocktail- the Pisco Sour was very good as was the Llama Del Ray with frozen grapes. We basically order one of everything on the menu. I absolutely loved the scollops ceviche, the pig tails and the lomo that was hands down the dish of the year. I also really enjoyed the Kale Salad. But Grilled Octopus was also excellent. The Quinoa flavored with a hint of banana was also good and unique. The service was good, the setting for table and the food was amazing - this is is most try place. The restaurant is festive and is a little loud. We sat by the open kitchen and with every order the soups chefs yell- yes sir.  Most was great retro tracks that were perfect for a old guy like me. Who doesn't like Elton John?

Bold flavors, great service, and casual cool atmosphere - would recommend for those looking for a unique meal in the Williamsburg area BUT you're better off looking elsewhere if you're on the hunt for good value. A meal for two will probably run you around $150-200 after tip/tax, and didn't feel particularly "worth it" from an ingredients/preparation POV. However, if a splurgey yet laidback meal is what you're specifically on the hunt for, Llama Inn is a good choice.

It was extremely easy to score a reservation day-of (Memorial Day dinner) as we were in the area and decided to search in Brooklyn for dinner on a whim. I had heard a lot of good things about Llama San, the Manhattan sister restaurant, so thought Llama Inn would be interesting to try.

For indoor dining, they require proof of either a negative Covid test or full vaccination, which was a nice precaution. The atmosphere/aesthetics of the restaurant are very beachy cute. Think pampas meets mid-century modern. Service was super friendly and eager to advise with menu selection.

My husband and I shared three small dishes, one entrée, and a dessert, which felt like a good amount. He also got a chicha morada, which was tasty but overpriced at $10 for a non-alcoholic drink (especially knowing how little I paid for chicha morada everywhere I went when I visited Peru since it's like their equivalent of OJ).

Verdict on the food? The small dishes were all very delicious. The flavors were all bold, bright, and punchy. We got the pig tails (crunchy and delicious), scallop ceviche (sweet and flavorful), and mussels escabeche (tasted like the most concentrated, room-temperature version of a cioppino). The pig tails were actually a generous portion, but the other two were quite pricey for their quantity. 

As for the main dish, we shared the lomo saltado - their signature dish. Volume-wise, it's definitely enough to share for two, but meat-wise, there's only enough pieces for one. The meat was well-cooked but overall the dish was underwhelming. Maybe it's because I'm Chinese, but stir-fried meat with soy sauce and onions, topped with a mountain of fries, didn't seem worth the $40-something price tag. Is it objectively tasty? Sure. But it wasn't elevated versus what you'd find on the streets of Peru for $5-10. I regret getting this dish because a couple more appetizers would've made for a more exciting substitute.

We also shared the banana ice cream cake for dessert. It was pretty good, but didn't love the frozen/hard cake texture - was a bit icy.

Overall, I still thought this was a delicious meal. On a value basis, I'm not thrilled, but I would recommend sharing several small plates among friends - again, only if you're in the mood for a splurgey yet casual meal.

TLDR: If don't look at the price tag and get the small plates only, you'll leave quite satisfied.

Broke this up into service, ambience and food.

Service:
Unfortunately I have a couple serious knocks against Llama inn re: service.

1. We had a reservation which we confirmed multiple times and still had to wait approx 25 mins for our table, during which time we sat at the bar and NEITHER of the 2 bartenders even acknowledged us in that time. Didn't even say "hi" or "be right with you" or "hey sorry it will be a few minutes we are very slammed/short staffed". NOTHING. Just treated us like we were invisible. I worked in the bar and night club business for YEARS and this is a cardinal SIN to me. Then after we sat down it was easily another 20 or so minutes until we even had a waitor approach and he just dropped off a glass of water and disappeared for a while before coming back to take our orders. Needless to say I was very close to walking out but I will say for what it's worth once we finally ordered, things started rolling smoothly.

2. Sometime between the time I booked in April, and may 19th.. they updated their covid policy to where you can not eat inside unless you have done a covid test within 48 hours or have proof of being vaxxed. Now my gf fortunately had her 2nd shot just the day before as did I, a few days before that. But we had NO notification of this policy upon making the res nor were we notified of needing proof of being vaxxed or tested within 48 hrs UNTILL THE DAY OF! Things very easily could have turned out very bad if it was inclement weather or very cold due to their lack of simple communication on new policy.

(Btw If this was some cheap neighborhood mom and pop spot I wouldn't be as picky about the service but we dropped almost $300(tip included) on dinner for 2... this is damn sure not what you expect when you're spending that amount)

Food:
This is where Llama Inn shines. Food was unreal from a culinary perspective. Every dish we had was more amazing than the next. So good! Flavors and combinations  were well curated and interesting. Like I never had chilled sweet potato mash in ceviche but it was spectacular. And the puree that came with the bass was so good I wanted to drink it like soup! 

Highly recommend: the bass, the soft Shelled crab, the octopus, and the crispy pig Tails. My compliments to the chef, big time.

The cocktails they had were awesome too!

Only knock on the food is portion size. Don't come here too hungry or you'll be spending hundreds of dollars.

Ambience:
Very simple yet tastefully decorated with nice plants. A classy/quaint vibe. Outdoor seating was very nice from what I saw walking in. Place was BUZZING... on a TUES NIGHT! I can only imagine what fri-sat must be like...
There is a rooftop as well though I didn't get to see it, I heard it was very nice and they have different cocktails up there. 

All in all I will maybe try it again, maybe they just had a bad day service wise. I wanted to give 5 stars because of the high quality of the food but I also wanted to give 2 stars for the very lack luster service experience. So I settled at 3 stars giving them the benefit of the doubt it will be better next time.

I love Llama Inn!! I booked a reservation for the rooftop for my girlfriend's birthday and we had an amazing meal. We sat at the bar and loved hanging with Kasha, the GM who happened to be tending bar that night. I could tell her and the rest of the staff loved the place and were having fun, and that good energy was contagious. We got the ceviche, scallops, duck hearts(incredible), soft shell crab, and picarones, all of which I would recommend. Thank you for a very special meal!!

Honestly unimpressed with the food. Came here for dinner , menu was completely different and they didn't have the classic dishes( cow heart) I had initially came here for. First dish was scallop tradito, although flavor was amazing portion was very small.  Probably 1 scallop sliced up into 4 small pieces. Next the mussels dish which didn't have much flavor.  Entree was the monkfish which was very greasy without much flavor. Portions are very small and variations to the plates were not possible as the server stated everything was pre-portioned out. Drinks were amazing and so was the ambiance and staff. Maybe brunch or different dinner menu would have made the experience better for me.

So I'm giving a totally fair critique here based on service and food. The food is good, I think it's overpriced for what it is but it's an experience for sure. So that's cool. Ordered a few different things for the table and while I stuck to the gluten free menu I did have the quinoa which was awesome and a decent serving. Also had the pork which was a rather small portion for $36 and a bit too salty for me 

*Felt everything was fairly salty but that's a hard thing to review when peoples tastebuds are so different. 

Our waiter was nice, the only thing that we had to speak up about was that he cleared drinks repeatedly that still had a fair amount in it. We ended up saying something but for $18 a piece that definitely should not be happening. When we said something, he obliged so that was good. It felt very rushed which I get is because of covid but dining is changing in general so we need to adapt. Only other thing that was super annoying ( I'm really sensitive to this!) was that it was SO HOT in the dining room. The nest thermometers were resting at 80 degrees. Not sure why that was but it just wasn't comfortable for me :(

Guys, my husband and I went to Peru, Lima - Barranco! This guys make a great afford to deliver the same expensive! Food is delicious and pisco Sour tastes authentic. Highly recommend it and would definitely come back here! No pictures sorry, a bit gloomy on the rooftop- but perfect for a dinner times

Clean, great service, beautiful decor. 
It's loud in there- I get that it's supposed to be "lively" but on a Tuesday night, I couldn't even hear my friend sitting next to me, or the waiter.  First we sat at the kitchen counter but the heat from the flame and the cooking peppers made it unbearable so we moved to the bar. 
Also, the bok choy dressing and the lomo saltado were too salty for me but otherwise I love the flavors and the menu.

Awesome experience, definitely coming again this place. We got to experience the rooftop, you are in Tulum but in Brooklyn. The food is amazing. Bathrooms are clean. It is sharing dishes. Mainly seafood. Cocktails are great. Would definitely come again

This restaurant was excellent! From the drinks to the food. The food has a very heavy nut and shellfish based menu so avoid if you have those allergies be careful to ask. Only drawback was the price of the dishes was not indicative of the size of the plates. I figure now that the restaurant is more of a tapas style where plates are to be shared and not for individual dining.

Absolutely awful service. Our waiter did not come to take our order for 15 minutes. Our first dish finally came 40 minutes after we were seated. After we finished the first course, our waiter brought out menus for dessert. We told her we were still waiting for our entrees and she apologized. Our entrees took another 40 minutes to arrive and then the waiter rushed us by coming to take our plates three times before we were finished. We would not have ordered dessert had we known it was not immediate but it took another 30 to 40 minutes to arrive. As we were waiting for dessert, the waiter rolled her eyes at us to the host; I would presume because we were taking a long time. At that point I told her that we would be happy to leave since I knew they needed the table back. She said the dessert would be ready shortly and brought the check. The remaining portion of the meal was tense. 

I was with people of color and am not sure what was going on but this was some of the most unpleasant service I've had.

I personally feel that staff can make or break a place, and here, it certainly makes it. Everyone here was beyond friendly and helpful. We sat at the upstairs bar at first, and the bartender was lovely. The cocktails were phenomenal- very interesting and unique.

Please note, you need to provide proof of vaccination to dine here, or else you can only eat outside, which is small compared to everything else.

The food was delicious. It's not inexpensive by any means, but you're for sure paying for the experience too, which is phenomenal. I would definitely go back on a sunny day to spend a weeks worth of pay on cocktails and ceviche lol

Oh man--I really really did not want to write this review, and in fact gave myself a few days to think it through to ensure I wasn't writing out of immediate anger and frustration. I've lived in NYC for years, in the immediate neighborhood (one block) from Llama inn for ten months, and been here through the entire pandemic, witnessing restaurants shutting down, struggling to open up, and eventually coming back to life. At every step, I have been a patient consumer, eaten in the snow, dined outside all winter, did anything I could to support small businesses, but the way my friend and I were treated on Friday night left such a poor taste in my mouth, I really couldn't find any way to write it off. 

We had made a reservation about a month in advance for the rooftop. Upon arriving, we were seated promptly at the bar, ordered a round of drinks (delicious), several apps, and a shared entree. Halfway through our first round, it began to drizzle and we saw several patrons ask to be moved. As we were under a partially covered awning, we asking for a couple napkins and decided to stick it out unless it got worse. We even joked about it with the bartender and ordered a second round. Around this time, the rain began to really pick up and the staff at the restaurant proactively began re-seating everyone around us. We asked if we could be reseated as well, and were told by a bar back that they were working on it. Pretty soon, the heavy rain turned into a torrential downpour and we were the only two people left on the roof--everyone around us reseated, and the staff scrambling to close the umbrellas and secure the rooftop furniture in the wind. At this point, we had waited about 25 minutes in the pouring rain and were almost completely drenched. The bar back suggested that since our entree had not come out yet, he'd be happy to close us out so we could leave. 

Upset about the situation, we quickly paid and made our way downstairs where we were cornered by a manager (or server in a floral shirt) who asked us why we were leaving--he had several plates in his hand and said "this is YOUR food" in an aggressive manner, when we reminded him that it's not even possible to sit upstairs in that weather, let alone eat a meal. Rather than apologizing or offering to re-seat us (or maybe offering a towel?), he made lots of excuses about the weather, not being able to foresee it, said we should have known what we were getting into since we made rooftop reservations. Again--just weirdly aggressive and unnecessary considering we were already leaving and didn't really make a hoopla about it. HE confronted US on our way down.

We proceeded to find two waiting chairs next to the bathroom and sat there ordering an uber and frantically trying to find dinner reservations ANYWHERE in the area late on a Friday. The entire hosting staff watched us doing this, but nobody said anything. As our Uber neared, we made our way to the front, closer to the exit, and noticed an entire empty counter with stool seating and candles next to the host stand. We felt further insulted that nobody even bothered to TRY and find a seat for us when all this space was available. Soon, the man in the floral shirt walked over AGAIN and this time he did apologize, but asked us why we didn't ask the hostess to re-seat us. I had to remind him that as a PAYING CUSTOMER WHO IS MID-MEAL, it's not my responsibility to wander around the restaurant and ask the staff to find me a new table. It's THEIR responsibility to help us out, especially since we were already eating and getting absolutely drenched. To add insult to the injury, on our way out into the storm, some woman tried to flag us down as a last resort, which just felt slimy when we had been sitting right under their noses, scrambling to find a reservation and a car for at least 15 minutes after we closed out on the roof. 

I don't know if the staff here has ever worked in a hospitality setting before because the entire ordeal was handled with such a lack of care that we felt humiliated and embarrassed, especially as other patrons watched us sitting in the entryway, drenched, while nobody made any effort to remedy our evening.

I don't know if the food is worth the disgusting treatment of customers, but I will never recommend Llama Inn to anybody, especially when there are hospitality-forward establishments in the area (Lilia, Amazzacafe, Fandi Mata).
We came here with a reservation. The food was great but pricey. Our favorite was the bok Choy salad. The asparagus only came with a few spears.
Amazing food. Excellent drinks and service. The outdoor seating was cute but close to the freeway above. Otherwise fabulous!

Everything on the menu is fantastic. The Lomo and the, get ready for this, Quinoa, Bacon, Cashew, Avocado and Banana dish were the highlights. Quality cocktails with a nice array of slight "different" choices.

My friend made a 9pm reservation, but the entire party arrived 30 mins late. Luckily they still seated us. Make sure you have your covid excelsior pass ready. They check it for indoor dining. 

I highly recommend the rock shrimps, clams, mussels, squids, ahji panca, rice, salad dish and the boy choy salad. The pork with fries were decent too.

Dearest Yelpers!

Had to go semi fancy this time and try some upscale Peruvian food at Llama Inn. For starters don't think you'll be able to sit inside unless you know the owners or you like to sit in a very uncomfortable miniature stool bar side. 

We made reservations a week in advanced and requested to sit indoors in one of the 5 booths they had but we're denied once we got there. Then we sat outside in what felt like a small wooden crate with grass in my ear. The bench was wood and they had a couple pillows but nothing I would touch.

Here's why they get the 3 stars. The food was exceptional. I grew up around Peruvian food and this did not disappoint. The drinks were delish and the waitress and server were really energetic enough to make me forget I was sitting in a crate on the street corner.

The desert left a lot to be desired but everything else was up to par. The price was definitely not worth the ambiance but like I mentioned the food was really good.

If you got the bucks I'd say 6 out of 10 recommend.

Came on time for our reservation and had to wait an astounding 35 minutes for our table because the patrons who had our table took forever to share a single dessert. Luckily the hostess sat us at the bar on the rooftop near our table and gave us free drinks as we waited. 

The pig tails and fluke ceviche was great but I think the ceviche was drowned in too much lime reduction. Like, swimming in it lol. But it was still good.
