The lomo saltado was amazing but I swear those fries were bought frozen and tasted exactly like McDonald's fries. It was still an enjoyable dish but overpriced for bagged frozen French fries... 

Took a star off because the seafood rice (arroz con mariscos) was so salty it was nearly inedible. And I'm Latina, I like salty food, that was just overboard. I picked out all the seafood and ate it and left most of the rice behind. 

Overall I enjoyed my experience because the hostess comped a lot of our drinks and our bartender was cute & friendly- but if they hadn't I think I would've given this place a different rating. Customer service matters :)

Ice Cream Sandwich - Not the delicious dessert advertised on reviews. Was awful with freezer frosting on it, that would take 45 mins to not crack a tooth

Pork Chop - Cold

Artichoke - Really Bland

Pig Tail - Best dish and then you realize you've paid 400+ dollars for pig tails

No Heart dish that evening - supplier issue. Would expect a restaurant that "changes their menu weekly for seasonality etc etc" to change the menu. 

Really overpriced & just really average food.

Excellent food service and vibe 
Interesting flavors and drinks , very low key but stellar

Loved this place and will be going back!! I would suggest making reservations- even on a Sunday they were busy. The way that you order is by picking a few plates then a larger plate to share. I do have to say they do a fantastic job explaining how to order. oh- COVID UPDATE: you do need to show your vaccine card to sit inside/ dine. We started off with drinks, pisco sour and their signature drink Llama del Rey. Then as starters we ordered the papas al a huancania, octopus ceviche, bok choy salad, and scallops. The ceviche was delicious but not a typica ceviche and small. The scallops were done perfectly but for my taste too much Parmesan. My favorite, the bok choy salad was so refreshing with the dressing and grapes. It was a delicious!! The papas were fantastic and the sauce was so creamy! Everything you could want in a typical papas dish. We ordered a big portion of the lomo saltado. It is different from what you would expect. It's a big dish of the steak, steak sauce, fries, and cheese sauce drizzled. The guacamole was delicious and perfectly made. I wish there was more! The sauce is so perfectly seasoned and the steak so well done. It comes with 4 scallion pancakes that you can make perfect tacos out of. Finally, we ordered the chocolate and Lucuma ice cream. It comes in a cute parchment bag that you can take out and it's basically an ice cream sandwich. We also ordered the piccarones- there are only three but they were PERFECTLY fried. Finally the last drink to end off was Como we Llama- it was okay. They did offer some drink digestives before dessert we didn't try. It's a dark place to eat they have indoor and outdoor dining. I loved the open kitchen! Great place to eat.

WARNING: Llama Inn does not take FOOD ALLERGIES/SAFETY seriously.

Here's the summary: 
Despite informing the restaurant several times of a severe dairy allergy, we were served food with cheese in a sauce while being assured several times there was no dairy in any of our dishes. 

Some contextual points:
- Llama Inn is VERY expensive (e.g. $44 beef stir fry), so you expect details like food safety to be more well taken care of.
- We had noted the food allergy when we made the reservation
- We informed our server several times and asked about each dish we ordered
- After our dishes were served, she came to our table and declared that ALL our food contained no dairy 

Specific issue:
The salad dressing, which we had been told has egg, but not dairy, contained cheese, something the manager confirmed when my wife started experiencing an allergic reaction and I asked for server the fourth time.

At least 3 things had to go wrong:
- The server wasn't well educated on the menu OR she made a mistake, and mistakes happen
- The server didn't consult with the kitchen to confirm the dishes, OR the kitchen save her the wrong information, neither of which are excusable
- The server didn't note our order/ticket OR the kitchen disregarded that notation OR the kitchen has no idea what they are serving, which means no one should feel safe eating at this restaurant

Credit where credit is due:
The manager did a great job with crisis management.  She ordered us a car to the hospital (and paid for it), which was very helpful given we were somewhat panicked, and then somehow got to the front door before us, with two bottles of water, and she walked us to the car. We really appreciated this.

(Additionally, she provided a work email address, and we reached to that address twice to try to get a better understanding of what happened--before I wrote this review--but never received a reply.)

Really delicious food, unusual & surprising flavor combinations. Really good cocktails, decent wine list. The only reason I'm not giving 5 stars is that it's a bit pricier than it needs to be. But it's a charming date-night spot.

I really really wanted to like this place. The presentation of the dishes were beautiful and instagram worthy. The restaurant was modern, clean, and classy. But the food was just alright. I've had better Peruvian food before. My favorite dish was the ceviche.
The beef tender stir fry was decent. Crispy pig tails, were so dry and salty. The most disappointing dish was the arroz con mariscos. It was so so SALTY. A table next to us sent their arroz con mariscos back to the kitchen, because of the saltiness. 
I personally would not return, the food was not worth its price.

Our first trip to Llama Inn remains one of the best restaurant experiences we've ever had in New York City, but it seems like things have changed for the worse over the last few months. We visited for our anniversary yesterday evening and unfortunately ended up pretty disappointed with our experience. Though the restaurant space is beautiful, the music was club-level loud, making it impossible to carry on a conversation. Service was really mediocre- our waitress spilled water on our table while pouring us water, and we had to ask three times for a napkin to clean it up. She disappeared altogether in the middle of dinner, and we had a tough time flagging down anyone else to take our order. Someone else ultimately closed out our check. While the cocktails were great, they had clearly been sitting at the bar for a while, because the ice in them had melted. And while most of the food we ordered was excellent, particularly the octopus ceviche, the much-hyped lomo saltado contained five tiny pieces of beef and burnt scallion pancakes, for $52. Especially for a special occasion, you really want your night to be incredible, and this was just...not it. It very much feels like a case of a restaurant starting incredibly strong and as they get busier and more popular, being unable to maintain the same excellent quality of food and service. I don't think we will be back.

I want to start off by saying I really wanted to like this place. I've heard a lot about it over the years, and as a 1st gen Peruvian, it means a lot to have a Brooklyn restaurant do right by the food I grew up eating. Llama Inn unfortunately didn't live up to their reputation. 

My family and I went for brunch to celebrate my sister's 21st birthday. We waited over an hour for our food and walked away disappointed and still hungry. I don't mind an overpriced establishment hiding behind a Michelin star, but the food has to be worth it. We had several of the brunch items: the tamal, the fluke ceviche, the quinoa appetizer, and the beef tenderloin - which is their take on the Peruvian staple lomo saltado. The ceviche was excellent but very small and hardly worth the price tag. The beef tenderloin was pretty good, but heavy on the soy sauce, and why banana instead of plantain? 

The restaurant was half full, so I'm not sure why the food took as long as it did. The servers barely checked in with us which soured the brunch most since we couldn't order many drinks while we waited. Llama Inn doesn't feel like a place for Peruvians

Pretentious and overpriced- the epitome of everything wrong with Williamsburg. The food is fusioned to the point of incomprehension. The components are very well cooked but some of the compositions are just not coherent. The 20 dollar cocktails are delicious but who needs it?

I was very impressed with Llama Inn. Not only does this restaurant have a lovely ambience, the staff are very friendly and accommodating.

Being vegetarian was certainly limiting, there was only one vegetarian option on the menu, however accommodations were made to two other dishes and the chef prepared some potato-based pancakes to accommodate as well.

The gems salad was probably my favorite, followed by the modified Quinoa dish.

For wines, the sparkling red natural wine was a MUST have, it was delicious!

Llama Inn is without a doubt one of the best Peruvian restaurants in New York. Everything from the ambience, to the quality of their dishes, drinks and service is outstanding. I try to come here at least once every three months or so as they change some of the items on their menu each season. 

My favorite drink is the Llama Del Rey (also love the creative name). I definitely recommend getting it if it's your first time here! Food wise, you can never go wrong with the ceviche (best ceviche in NYC!) and the Lomo saltado. 

Overall coming here is always a 10/10 experience! No wonder it's featured in the Michelin guide.

I made reservations for 2 for this restaurant on a Friday (10/08/21) at 4:25pm through the phone for 8:30pm. The person on the phone asked for my phone number and even asked if I wanted indoor or outdoor seating. I was confirmed for 8:30 over the phone. When we got there I said my name and they said I wasn't on their list. The two men at the door said we weren't on the list and had to make a reservation through this app called Rezi, which wasn't included on their page on Google nor over the phone. The two men were rude about saying our reservation doesn't work over the phone, but asked if we wanted to come back in an hour without even asking for our name or phone number. We had to suggest this, and when we did a random name came up for my girlfriend and they asked if her name was Mark... They called us 15 minutes later and asked if we wanted to sit at the bar so we said yes. We weren't satisfied so we ended up going to the Reunion around the corner with amazing food and great service.
Food is a bit underwhelming and pricy for the quality. I like the deco and environment tho!

The food was tasty. The service was pretty good. But the cost is obscene. I've had far better food for much less money. Biggest red flag should have been their outdoor area being sponsored by resy and Amex. Spent almost $200 for two people and left hungry. I got the potatoes and I kid you not, there were six small shrivels of cold potato. Ridiculous.

First Peruvian restaurant I've visited in a while and I loved it! I had a fabulous time - drinks, food, service,  vibe - all were great. We went on a Saturday night. I would recommend making reservations before going in. 

Of everything we had I absolutely loved the Lomo Saltado and the Lama Del Ray. Can't wait to visit again and try more!

Such a great place for Peruvian food!!! I still think about their bok choy dish, which is so unassuming but I'm so glad the waiter recommended it to us. Other dishes were just as amazing, loved small twists on everything. The quinoa has a banana center that paired well in flavor and texture. The ceviche are well done and so fresh. Their lomo saltado was interesting, as it was more of a taco style instead of the traditional bowl (also it serve two!). If anything, was surprised that I liked other dishes more than the lomo saltado, which is usually my go to order for Peruvian food, but it was still very good.

Conflicted. Been to Peru so I know what the food should taste like and I also know what a proper portion of food should look like for the price. This place misses on sooooo many levels not sure where to begin. My son lives in the area and we were visiting Brooklyn so he booked a reservation for a table of four. We ordered almost $300 worth of food and left hungry and personally unsatisfied. When a main course describes a seafood medley with shrimp and they charge almost $40 for a tiny bowl with a tablespoon of rice topped with 3 small shrimp that is simply ridiculous ! The surprise of the meal were the pig tails - almost like ox tails in a BBQ style - tasty but also a small portion. The ceviche was tasty but also a ridiculously tiny portion. Service was okay. Don't charge those steep prices and keep the vibe so casual and you might be able to pull this off IMHO. My recommendation: Save your money and eat elsewhere. Even Brooklyn hipsters deserve better! Small portions, high prices relative to what is served and generally a waste of $$$$. Strong pass on this one !

Highly recommend this place if youre into super acidic savory foods. The mussels had the perfect amount of "spice", "sweetness" and "saltiness" in a seafood dish. The fried potato filled with beef topped with egg was perfect comfort food on a rainy day and the sweet potato dish with ceviche had a beautiful lemony flavor with the natural sweetness of the potato. The michelada was just eh, wouldn't recommend it and having had micheladas from Mexico this isn't a "true" one but they do say it's peruvian based which I know is different. Definitely go if you're in the area.

I was struggling not to give this place one star. As someone from LA, we have fantastic Peruvian food for very reasonable prices. This place is crazy prices and food wasn't even good. My god - the lomo had frozen fries not even mixed with the lomo sauce. $150 for two people with no liquor and we were very unsatisfied in flavor and filling. So you know, we had the pig tails, ceviche and lomo. Hoping I can save one person from this place.

A friend and I randomly stopped by on a Sunday night without reservations and were seated ~30 mins outside which had a nice heater setup so we were fairly warm.

I will say I am far from a Peruvian culinary connoisseur however overal I felt everything was a tad overpriced and I am not sure I hype around this place.  We ordered octopus cervihe (best dish), crispy pig tails (pretty good) and lomo saltado (underwhelming and the amount of meat for given the price ~$45 was disappointing).

The service was great as were the drinks (llama del rey and wine selection) however I am not sure if I would go back.

Came here after a brewery crawl and this was a great end to the night. It's suggested to order several things as they are tapas. Between me and one other person, we shared 4 dishes. They have an interesting take on Peruvian and incorporate cheese almost seamlessly in their dishes. Not pictured: Lomo Saltado, which was yummy but heavy on the stomach.

Great spot for a fancy brunch! 
Came here last March, therefore menu may have changed since then. 
We got the lomo Saltado which was a beef tenderloin stir fry with French fries and a fried egg. This was my first time trying this Peruvian dish and I really liked it! The stir fry tastes like really good Chinese beef story fry on top of crispy French fries. 

We also got the red quinoa salad which came with a mix of things including banana. Reading from the ingredients, I wasn't sure if I was going to like this one but it came recommended from a friend. I ended up really liking it and I especially liked the crunch the red quinoa added to dish. 

We also got the tortilla de camarones which was essentially a shrimp egg omelet in a creamy, curry-like sauce. This was my friend's favorite and it was a good contrast to the other dishes we ordered. It was not very spicy but had a lot of flavor! 

The llama del Rey drink was also SO GOOD! Actually one of my favorite brunch drinks Ive had and it came with the sweetest grapes.
fave restaurant!! such an incredible menu overall with really unique and amazing cocktails.

This place is amazing. We had dinner last night, outside in 30 degree weather. Their outside accommodations are excellent. They have heaters and even blankets if you want. The waitress even offered my wife a cup of hot water with lemon. Everything we ordered was just delicious. We had the fluke ceviche, bock choy, mushrooms, mariscos, saltado. All dishes were out of this world. Highly recommend.

If you're looking For your next date spot, or somewhere to bring your parents llama in is perfect for all occasions. I've been here multiple times and I never get tired of their food, cocktails service or ambience. Five stars all around!!

The food was really good. The octopus and the other ceviche thing was good. Arroz con mariscos was really good. The drinks were good to. Also you can just get a pisco sour. 

Our main issue was there was no heaters. They said there were vents blowing but it was so cold. They need to add more heaters for sure.

This place and the staff are too buzzy being impressed with themselves that they forget they are in the service industry. Made reservations for 4 a month in advance, the entire party showed up a bit earlier hoping to have a drink at the bar, we were told with the biggest attitude that our table wasn't ready and we could not get a drink of wait inside. So we were forces outside on the coldest night of the year. Our table was right next to the door, and since they do not let anyone wait for their table inside the door was closing and opening all night, so we were freezing. When we expressed this, we were told that there is nothing that can be done and no other tables. The rest of the service was not any better, anything that we asked for the answer was "no", they don't have cranberry juice to make a cosmo, getting tea was an issue, and when we asked for coffee the answer was let me see if we have any left. what???? 
The food was good, the octopus was the stand out dish, some others were a bit weird. The menu did not describe the dishes well, and was hard to read. Also it seems like the menu changes often, so if you see a dish on yelp don't assume
It will be there when you go. 
There are plenty of other places with better food and definitely better service.

The food is definitely tasty but the hosts and the manager are not accommodating at all, to a point of being borderline rude. We came in 25 min before our reservations and wanted to sit by the bar and wait for our table meanwhile there were 5 empty tables that we could have sit at, instead we were told that these tables are awaiting reservations and due to COVID we couldn't sit at the bar even though there were other patrons sitting there. We were sent packing to a bar a cross the street and were told that someone will text us. When we did come back to the restaurant we were given a table right by the door where it was freezing and when we asked the manager to make it warmer we were told that it would be impossible because the other parts of the restaurant would be too hot. Though the food is tasty the dinner wasn't enjoyable at all because it was too cold.

This place was super amazing! Loved every bite of it! My favorite was the fried calamari and the calamari sandwich! It was a little messy but in a good way! The restaurant felt fancy and high end, but didn't feel out of place in casual wear! Definitely would love to go again! 
IG: @isaacb.rich

We visited with a total party of 4, and had an excellent time. At the recommendation of the servers, we ordered 5-6 dishes to share family-style, which ended up being more than enough, and there was no pressure to order a certain way, which we were extremely grateful for. The open space is very welcoming and the overall environment is still very much casual, despite what some might say. 

The food was both filling and exciting, with delicately balanced textures and flavors that have clearly been thought about in terms of both combination and presentation. The starters appear small, but the bok choy salad was more than enough and the scallops were also very much filling with the individual pieces and sauce. Both of these had great flavor combinations, with the balancing of the salad in terms of textures and moisture not being too much.

The crispy pig tail and chicken were also done well. Although the crispy pig tail was a bit dry (likely by design), it was still flavorful, and the combination of the chicken with the accompanying sauces and veggies made it an extremely pleasing experience. The mussels were also well worth the money with the eggs and sauce actually adding a great punch in flavor and creating an innovative mouth feel and considerable sense of fulfillment.

The main attraction is, of course, the beef stir fry, with tomatoes, scallions, sauce, fries, and avocados, peppers, and tortillas on the side to aid in the creation of whatever apparatus and combination of flavors you prefer. Their Lomo Saltado is renowned and there are numerous articles about its unique spin on the dish, and it was a clear highlight of the meal.

Overall, Llama Inn is definitely one of the best dining experiences that I've had in a while--the relative rarity of Peruvian cuisine certainly helps in its appeal, but it really is a great meal overall.

I rarely give 3 stars to an establishment but I must today. 

Let's start with the positive:
1. Beautiful restaurant with greenery and draped plants all around
2. Clean environment
Unfortunately, that's about it.

Here's the real deal:
1. Poor service. The food took so long to get to our table and no one checked in on us, no one assured us it would be okay. We had to ask a random server where our food was.
2. Expensive food with mediocre, tiny portions.
3. The food did not "wow" me (there is nothing that I would come back here for)

I assume if you are reading this, you are either considering going here or you have found yourself already there and you're panicking. Well, it's okay. If you are there, order the ceviche, it's really good. The quinoa was also pretty good, very different. I would suggest not to order the beef tenderloin stir - fry. I love a good lomo saltado but this was basically salt, it was extremely acidic and heavy on the soy sauce. I had to drink water in order to finish it. Maybe they just had a bad day and the chef was heavy handed? 

I'm always willing to give a place a second try, so maybe I'll try it again one day.

The drinks were amazing and unique but the food was subpar. I went for brunch with friends and no one was impressed with their food. We were so excited about this place and generally love Peruvian food but the brunch fell flat. One guest had an allergy to eggs and it eliminated nearly everything from the menu. He ate plain pasta and a plain steak- something we could have easily cooked at home. Maybe the dinner menu would be more exciting.

What a beautiful and amazing restaurant. We came here to celebrate my bday and it was amazing! We didn't have a reservation so we sat in the bar area. The service was impeccable. Everyone was so friendly and the staff made great recommendations for food and drinks. The bartender went out of his way to make me a drink they was not on the menu. Everything was amazing from start to finish including the apps, food, drinks and dessert. I highly recommend this restaurant.
It's delicious. The service is really good. It is expensive and you should probably dress a little on the nicer side. Oh and I forgot to take pictures because the food was too damn tasty to wait.

For the life of me I do not understand why this place is so highly rated and constantly packed. The restaurant is cute with all of the greenery and decor and my husband and I were really looking forward to trying this place out. For appetizers we ordered the salmon ceviche and beets with gouda, they were fine but like maybe two bites each. Moving on, for our mains we ordered the lomo saltado (a hefty $48) and expected delicious, flavorful and tender steak in this traditional Peruvian dish. What we received were four small CHEWY pieces of steak drowned in a sauce that was too acidic and salty which left us disappointed. Next we ordered the arroz con mariscos which was so SALTY we could barely eat it and in hindsight should have sent it back. Our waiter was nice but didn't check on us once to see if we were enjoying our food or needed anything. When we received our bill I asked him if he accidentally double charged us for a coke (priced at $6) and his response was..."No, it's just really expensive"...umm what!? Yeah, not returning.

Wow- took my sister here to celebrate her promotion and everything was perfect. You could tell the ingredients were all fresh, and there was a fancy flare on some Peruvian classics. It's not cheap, but it's worth the price you pay for clean fresh food.

I believe the menu changes frequently, and unfortunately I did not take a picture of it. We ordered the fluke crudo, beet salad, and lomo saltado. I don't even like beets, and me and my sister were fighting over the last one. Lomo saltado is a must, and the French fries on top were worth ordering as a side they were so crispy and flavorful. The crudo had a flavor I couldn't place, but it felt very familiar. After our meal we both decided we wouldn't have ordered differently; except there was so much on the menu we wanted to try we had to come back again. Maybe with more people so we could try more things and order the same ones again!

I find it hard to find a good pisco sour in NYC, but this one was delicious. I got the passion fruit and she got the chica morada. The egg white on top was perfectly whipped/blended in to the drink and the passion fruit tasted real unlike some overly sweetened syrupy drinks I've ordered at other restaurants. 

The only downfall was dessert, we were slightly disappointed in the chocolate ganache cake. It tasted more like a day old brownie, and we would have appreciated it being a bit warm or more cake like. The cream around it seemed homemade with potentially quinoa or another cereal and it was very unique and tasty. 

Our server was lovely, the food came out quickly, and the vibe of the restaurant was moody/hip. The kitchen is open, and the bar is in the center of the room so it feels like you are a part of the experience. Would be a great date spot!

We had a bunch of dishes here: pork chop, arroz con mariscos, fluke crudo, little oysters. All dishes suck in different ways, but the common theme is sugar on sauce on sugar on sauce on sugar. They even put a sugary milky cream on the oysters!
Stay away, very unfriendly staff and service. The staff will go out of their way to make your experience awful.

Made a quick trip to NY and am glad my friend snagged a res at this spot. A+ ambiance, cocktails, and food. 

Here's what we enjoyed:
- salmon ceviche: one of our favorites, I could drink the leche de tigre it is served with. 
- pigtails: this is an adventurous one. great flavor, but the bone is a little creepy.
- mushrooms: these were good, but nothing incredibly special. 
- lomo saltado: our other favorite, such a unique spin on a Peruvian classic
- arroz con mariscos: another highlight with a great depth of flavor

A little overpriced for the food. Everything is a little salty. Wait for long time for the food to be served. Nice environment. The kitchen bar seats are very hot because there is a grill in front of you.

I came here for my bday dinner. It's a beautiful and hip place with an open bar set-up and plenty of mood lighting. The server was friendly and recommended 4-5 dishes for me and my husband. We ordered 4. The food was quite impressive; we had the Maitake mushroom,  bass tacu tacu, arroz con mariscos and of course, the lomo Saltado. While most reviews highly favor the lomo saltado, I found the dish a little too heavy and greasy. Instead, I loved the arroz con mariscos and the maitake mushroom.  Dishes are tapa sizes. 

If I had known the lomo saltado was on the heavier side, I would have ordered 3 entrees, not 4. We also each had drinks- I had the mai tai which was pretty sweet but delicious and my husband had tequila on the rocks. Prepare to drop a Benjamin or two. Our bill came out to about $200, which was higher than expected but worth it.

Cozy set up outdoors replete w furry throws in trainstyle seating. 

The shrimp rice is amazingly luscious and jammed packed with flavor... only second to the pig tails we'd gladly slurp up the sweet & citrusy star anise marinade. The tails were interesting as they weren't so meaty but chewy, crispy, firm and so darn tasty. Honestly I would want nothing more than 25 of these suckers in a KFC bucket carpeted by a layer of white rice to soak up that porky soy sauce. 

The mash mushroom was also really yummy esp if you like/love mash. Super smooth, light and creamy at the same time. The salmon ceviche- we racked our minds on how that is basically un-fck-upable, like fried chicken. 

Llama inn is really really delicious and we will be back.

The llama Inn is one of those brunch places that is on every top brunches list you will find on Google. We came here for brunch today and walked away content vowing to  check out their dinner menu one day. 

Not a huge fan of the location, it's right under the BQE but the ambiance more than makes up for it. It has a tropical vibe with a bar in the middle of the restaurant surrounded by booths and tables. It has an open and airy atmosphere, filled with natural light and this was on an overcast day. I'd imagine it looks even better at night. 

The brunch menu was short and pricey. We didn't get any apps, went straight for the kill. We got the breakfast burrito with chips, fried rice with omelette and a steak dish with pasta. We had a toddler with us and were disappointed they had nothing for kids on the menu. We ended up getting an order of fries and a non alcoholic juice of sorts. 

Everything was great, the fried rice with omelette was sweet and spicy and it all came together beautifully. The breakfast burrito came highly recommended, it had eggs, poblano pepper and rice on the inside and was topped off with an aji verde sauce. The sweet potato chips on the side were delish. The steak and pasta was amazing too. The food has its roots in Peruvian cuisine and you see it in their decor too, but it's fusion rather than traditional. 

We got a drink which was their take on a sangria. I forget the name but it was delicious! We also got a dessert which was a deconstructed apple pie but eaten like you would eat nachos. It was delicate and decadent. The service is just lovely,the wait staff went out of their way to take care of us. Bring your date for a drink here or come here with friends, I know I'll come back for their dinner service here.
Food, drinks, service, ambiance, all 10/10. No hype here, just the good stuff. Total gem

Fantastic ambience inside makes for a perfect date night out.

We got here at 7:30PM and got seated immediately since reservations were made. We went with the quinoa, pork chops, crispy pigtails and the lomo saltado.

First was the quinoa. Came cold with quinoa, cashew, bacon and avocado. Great appetizer choice as it was a gif mixture of salt and sweet to whet your appetite.

Crispy pigtails came next. I've never eaten pigtails before and didn't know what to expect but was pleasantly surprised. Was indeed crispy with some meat on the tail. A bit on the saltier side and would've paired well with a bowl of rice.


Pork chops came with 2 meaty pieces. The pork was incredibly tender and whatever the sauce was, gave it a slight kick.

The star of the show, the lomo saltado. Giant dish of beef and fries in a sauce that definitely kicked. The fries were good but eventually got drenched in the sauce that had me dripping sweat. The beef was extremely tender but for a dish that was $52, only 4 pieces of beef was present. This comes with scallions, guac and rice. You're suppose to place some guac, rice, beef and fries onto the pancake for a DIY tortilla essentially. 

This place is worth a visit but as other reviews have stated, some things are overpriced and overly salty.
Delicious food and wonderful appetizers! We tried almost everything on the menu. The breakfast burrito was very yummy and I also enjoyed the quinoa. definitely recommend!

I didn't get any pics- it was too dark- but the food was good and so was my cocktail. The only issue was that the menu was not vegetarian friendly at all! 

We had the quinoa (without bacon) and I had the beets. Very tasty! I'm sure if they did a vegetarian protein dish it would be excellent!

Where should I start.. One word I can think of for this restaurant is "overpriced." when appetizer costs around 25? that's enough to say.. unless they have Michelin starred (and I have been to many many many Michelin started restaurants.. trust me...).

food - 4/5, food was surprisedly good. we ordered salmon ceviche, oyster mushroom and arroz con mariscos. really small portion. even waitress suggested to order 4-5 dishes for two.

drinks - 4/5, my husband ordered a glass of white wine and I ordered one cocktail (forgot the name). it was alright.

service - 1/5, we wanted to order more after our appetizers/main dishes, but our waitress NEVER stopped by to see if we were doing okay (we were sitting at the kitchen counter and restaurant wasn't even busy at that moment), waited to get a menu which we gave up.. waited to get another drinks which we gave up.. so yeah. service here was pretty bad when we pay $25 for appetizer kind of restaurant.

ambience - 3/5. totally brooklyn vibe.

overall.. not sure if I would like to return. just because they are so overpriced.. I saw a few couple walked out after checking the menu. so.. yeah

Made reservations for this spot a few days in advance for dinner with a friend. He'd been before and really enjoyed it so I was psyched to try it out. The place was busy, trendy, loud but in a good way. Our server was quick and attentive, and the whole general ambiance was cool and laidback. They also had a great playlist in the background.

We ended up ordering a couple delicious cocktails (the Llama Del Rey and El Chapo, I believe) and some great plates to share. My favorite was the very popular Lomo Saltado, which I would definitely recommend you try. 

Go here fam.

Llama inn is definitely a restaurant we will come back to. From the minute you arrive staff members are welcoming and very attentive.

Ambiance:
The vibes there were great, very diverse crowd with a fantastic music playlist.

Drinks:
We ordered two cocktails, llama del Rey and el chapo. El chapo was a very strong drink we ended up not even drinking whereas llama del Rey we loved. It was very similar to a sangria with the perfect balance.

Food:
We ordered so much food I'm not sure where to begin. For starters we tried both ceviches and it has been the best ceviches I've ever had. The salmon ceviche had a Asian flare to it where the fluke had a nicely balanced with sweet potatoes. If there's anything you order at llama in make sure it's both ceviche dishes.
Oyster mushrooms were a bomb of flavors, layers and layers of deliciousness. Another must order dish.
And finally, we ordered lomo saltado which by that point we were pretty stuffed. Nonetheless, we dug right in the minute the dish arrived the portion is perfect for two people, the lomo is perfectly seasoned the French fries were super crispy and had a sayer that really tied the entire dish together. The dish is accompanied by white rice, guacamole and scallion pancakes, it's meant to be eaten like a taco.

We didn't have any desserts didn't even ask for the menu that's how stuffed we were lol

Overall, the restaurant is a great choice. Can't wait to come by again and try the rest of the menu.

Llama San is like some fusion paradise sent from the gods, it's so good. So how is it that Llama Inn is so much worse? It's like dining with Tom Brady's out-of-shape younger brother who doesn't know what a touchdown is.

The food was fine, but nothing to write home about. My Papa Rellena had a burnt fried egg that ruined the overall taste. The Bok Choy salad was lovely, but had too much dressing. The Fried Rice Omelette was decent, as was the Steak, so if you have to get a proper brunch entree, get those instead. The Heirloom Cacao Hull tea (they were out of green tea, for some reason), is gross. Don't get it.

Where Llama Inn really lost me was our server. She was the most frowny, unhappy server I've encountered in a long time. It wasn't even busy when we were there (our resy was for 11:30am), yet she acted like she didn't want to be there, repeatedly forgot our requests for more water, and barely thanked us at the end of our meal. I know times are tough for service folk, but we were very pleasant to her, so why the 'tude?
I've been to Llama Inn twice now and both times it was truly incredible. The service is impeccable and the food is perfection. I couldn't recommend it enough!

Not bad for brunch! Would come back again. The ceviche and the mussels were great. Beef and spaghetti was delightful but a bit on the blander side. The outdoor seating was fine, but the rooftop of the shed magnified the lights so that there was a greenhouse effect.
Very expensive for bland dishes. Pretty, but most dishes taste the same and seems to lack the Peruvian flair they are advertising.

I have eaten at this restaurant a few times and was very happy up until tonight, but today was very so/so in general. Mostly my evening started out badly because they couldn't keep their reservation time and front staff was indifferent and borderline rude, just not very customer friendly. 

It started with the fact we had a reservation at a late time (9:30 pm) because that was all they had available and  then had to wait a further 45 minutes just for our table. I was ready to give up and go home but they got my credit card on file and it's $25 if you're a no show.

I get that they're busy and the person with our one table took forever to eat dessert apparently but with Llama Inn  the attitude at the front desk was just not very accommodating or friendly. Lots of folks came in and were seated before us because they were just two people and we were four. So that kind of makes sense. But it was already very late and who wants to eat dinner after 10 pm?  I mean come on, I was feeling *hangry*!!!

There were three different people at the front desk responsible for dealing with the reservations and we were the only ones waiting. Each time I went in it was someone different. The thing is, not one of them had the decency to give an update as to the wait. No one ever stuck their head outside to say, "Hey, we want to help but the table hasn't left yet or we're really sorry etc" We had to continually chase them. So clearly it makes you feel like they don't care about their customers.

After the fifth time of going inside to ask the status they finally offered us a tiny spot indoors as rooftop table we booked was still not available. Kids remind me how loud the indoors was and asked we continue to wait. Then I finally saw someone leave the rooftop. After another five minutes noone came so I went inside again. I said,"why didn't you come get us?" the line was growing steadily at that point) with several groups having pushed their way ahead of us. 

The front desk woman was clearly not attentive and made a comment asking if we were finally ready. Well of course we are you darned hostess!!! Then with her snarky tone she said she was coming to get us right then if I had only waited. 

At that point very tired we finally get seated. They were apologetic and after ten minutes they gave us two free drinks as knew I was annoyed. I mean I was hangry and just being a New Yorker. 

Waiter was awesome so I started to feel bad. I explain to my kids I think these snooty hipster places with 'we're too cool for you" attitude is all wrong! 

$19 for cocktails on the menu about gave me a heart attack!!!

I'll be brief on food but flavors were pretty good, just way too salty and not nearly as good as last time we went.

We had the quinoa, bok choy and pig tails. Branzino and tacos with scallion crepes.

Total cost of the above with two cocktails two non alcoholic drinks and tip = $300. Way overpriced.

Such an interesting spot! While originally a bit intimidated by the menu, everything was fabulous. None of the dishes tasted like anything we had ever had before. We had the quinoa salad, and the bok choy salad- both a hit! To drink I had the llama del ray- soooooo good!!

god damn, did i wait too long to attend a dinner at this place. however, i am sure i finally made the treck out here. i dropped about $120 on a meal here just for myself. im not a cheap date, but im a good one.

i emailed to get reservations because nothing was available online. im glad i did because on a random thurs night around 6, this place was bumpin and grinding. my biggest negative comment here is how hot it is here. there are so many windows and open space, but it was too warm for me. i was dying of sweat and heat. 

service was flawless and perfect. everyone that helped me paid attention and was incredibly alert. everything was timed perfectly, it was a true defintion of fine dining, in a more casual and laid back environment. i love the decor, plants, and notes of the peruvian influence that can be found throughout. youll even receive a peruvian post card with your check. yes, i framed mine.

i grabbed the fluke (it was actually red snapper) ceviche. this can not be shared. just eat it all on your own. its not your typical ceviche, but the traditional notes are there. it also has calamari in it too. i loved everything about this. the texture, to flavor and the colors. its truly beautiful. the broth had a perfect amount of spice.

drink? well, have i mentioned i love lana del rey? here we have the llama del rey.  it was a bit too much like a wine for me. i didnt hate it, but this is not something i would get again. it was made well and i got a nice buzz here. i love the play on words too.

now onto my entree... the bass tacu tacu oregeno and celary. i was a bit skeptical on how filling this would be, but i was pretty damn stuffed after eating this. i dont normally get bass, but the bass was so gentle. the beans were cooked perfectly. although small and mighty, but the celary on top was so nice. it was a pretty expensive dish, but i loved it.

always save room for dessert. and by dessert i mean the peruvian donuts. they come in a pair and are drowned in a cinnamon honey type of syrup. very good, but i wish there were some type of nut on them. theyre made out of sweet potatoe and butternut squash.

I used to love coming this place pre pandemic. I live nearby, so my partner and I loved this place for a nice dinner or brunch. 

HOWEVER prices have gone WAYYY up, & portion sizes have gotten so small it's a joke. They've also cut down the menu a lot, so your options are limited. 

I brought a friend to Llama Inn last week (after bragging to him about this place for months) and the size of the plates we received, compared to the price tag, was actually comical. $35 for the "shareable" chicken dish - which ended up being 3 skewers the length of my finger, served on a tiny dessert plate. We actually laughed out loud. 

The food was still yummy, but not the level of quality I remember from some months back. 

The vibes, music, ambiance, cocktails, and staff at Llama are still wonderful & oh so cool. 

But $68 for a plate of Lomo saltado?? Like really guys??? (Not even the most expensive item)

My wallet, better judgement, and self-respect will not allow me to return . However they likely won't miss my patronage as the place was still packed with people & prime-time reservations are nearly impossible to get. 

The curse of the popular new Williamsburg restaurant: they start out strong, get their exciting write-ups, get popular, and a few years later the quality tanks while prices soar. See also: Oxomoco.

I will say Llama Inn has a beautiful interior, full of plants and access to view their open kitchen. Each dish is meant to be shared among a group and for my group of 3, we all shared 4 dishes.

First thing, this place is not cheap. There's a relatively small menu so options are limited but each dish is super unique and our server was kind enough to give a description of each dish so we knew what to choose. Though expensive, I will say all dishes were really great! The ceviche with calamari was definitely the best dish, so I would strongly recommend it. Our Bronzino dish was pretty expensive ($62) and unfortunately had a few pieces of bone in it still, though we were warned there might still be a few in the fish. 

Overall drinks are on the more expensive side ($20), and though they were good, I wasn't too impressed.
This place is phenomenal. I recall first experiencing their food at smorgasborg several years ago and their restaurant is somehow even better!

I'll start out by saying the food was delicious. The service was fine as well, although our server was borderline too pushy with the up-selling. 

My biggest issue is that this restaurant is WAY WAY WAY overpriced. For example, we ordered the Lomo Saltado. Now for $59 you would expect more than 3 chunks of meat. But that's all there was, 3 chunks of meat and a whole bunch of french fries. I'm not exaggerating when I say that it was basically a $59 plate of fries. 

Another example is the price of coffee. A simple cup of drip coffee, without anything in it, was $8. Yes, that's correct, $8 for a cup of regular black drip coffee.  I don't care if it was the rarest coffee in the world and they hand picked it and roasted it themselves.  That is outrageous. We never would have ordered coffee had we known that it was the cost of an appetizer at some restaurants.  

Again, everything we ate was delicious. But the restaurant really needs to reevaluate their pricing. Until then, eat somewhere else.

I've been to Llama Inn's sister restaurant, Llama San, before and was super eager to try out Llama Inn. I've heard before Inn is a lot more Peruvian than San is, but unconfirmed. The interior of the restaurant was less Japanese-inspired than Llama San was I think. The food was quite delicious! One of my friends had a moment every time she had a bite of each of the dishes. My only complaint would be that our reservation was at 730, but told us we had to be out by 8:45 :c wasn't enough time to have ordered their larger dishes!

Good food, nothing to go crazy for but everything we ordered was tasty although it was in need of more salt. Learn to season your food folks. Ceviches were the highlight (delicious), the bok choy was pretty good although nothing exotic (why even use bok choy...?), the pork chop was fine, the steak was fine. Everything well executed. 

The problem was the prices and the portions. The ceviche was probably 2oz (certainly no more than 3) of fish for $25. The bok choy salad was maybe 10 pieces of greens. The pork chop was maybe 7oz on a good day ($39). The steak I don't even remember what it cost, $60?  Maybe 6 oz, and they give you four scallion pancakes, enough rice for 2 bites and a tablespoon of avocado. Split this between 3 people was laughable. 

In order to get a decent meal you would need to order per person one ceviche, a salad, and I would suggest two mains. You're now around $100 pp with no drinks. 

I understand the cost of food and running a restaurant has skyrocketed, I totally get that. But people cannot afford this, it's completely unsustainable and unsatisfying.

Wow, just wow! I've been having a bad streak with eating out and was starting to become jaded with the quality of food in NYC, but Llama Inn really helped course correct me.

The food, the drinks, the people, the ambience, the overall experience was just fantastic!

I dined here with just one other friend and snagged a table at the 'chef's counter' (which I highly recommend!). You really get a front row view into the kitchen's operations which made for a really cool dining experience. You can tell a lot of thought had been put into the design of the restaurant - despite being only a few feet away from the chefs, I did not feel a heat wave from the kitchen.

I started with the Llama Del Rey cocktail which was strong.... but delicious! 

The food menu is seasonal and changes frequently. We got the salmon ceviche to start which was fresh, bright and had a surprising spicy kick to it (but good).

Next was the Chicken Thigh Skewers. Get this and thank me later. The thighs were cooked over a Japanese charcoal grill so had this incredible smoky aroma to it but was still incredibly juicy. The crispy potatoe slices on the top add extra texture to this already incredible dish.

We opted for the Branzino as our main. Our waiter suggested we order a side of the scallion pancakes and use this to make 'tacos' with the fish. This should be recommended to anyone who orders the fish. So so tasty. The pancakes were fluffy with some nice char to it. Branzino was just perfect. Well seasoned and cooked perfectly too. I believe there were some nori(?) on the outside of the fish which added an amazing umami taste. Be warned though, despite having most of it's bones removed, there are still some left, so be careful when eating.

We had a chocolate cake for desert. This was onto of some of the best ice cream I've ever had as well as baked quinoa (?!? I didn't even know you could do this) which added this incredible crunch to the desert).

TL/DR - this is now one of my favorite restaurants in Brooklyn. Everything is tasty. Ask your waiter for recommendations and run with it, you won't be disappointed.

Food is whatever. 

Hit or miss for a Peruvian place. 

The pricing is outrageous. They charge Michelin-star prices for food that is not as good as the best street food in Peru, China, or Queens. 

There are far better options for Peruvian in Queens and Brooklyn that won't break the budget. Try KANTU on Metropolitan Avenue. Been there dozens of times. Kantu charge $20 for Lomo Saltado entree ($14 for lunch special). How is this restaurant sharing $78 for two people? It's robbery Fusion or not. 

This restaurant is a rip off. Will not go again.

Best best Peruvian food in nyc ! Is really hard to find authentic food sometimes, this place is beyond amazing. The service, the space, drinks & desserts are 100%. Can't wait to go back again very soon !!!!!!!

Nice atmosphere but the menu is completely over priced and plates miniscule.  Food is good but nothing amazing and for sure not worth the price point.  It's at least $120 per person with a couple of drinks. 
Definitely would never go back.

Was looking forward to a nice experience, and expected just that by the kind greetings at the door and friendly staff! Unfortunately when we were there they seemed to be having a major issue with the A/C because it was unbearably hot and humid inside. I was looking forward to the great food but couldn't stay longer than a drink because of the temperature. I can't imagine having to do all of the hard work and people please that the staff has pushing though all while having to work in an insanely hot and humid environment. 

But Andrew at the door was great and the drink that I had made by Eduardo was amazing so be sure to tip well, especially since they are being made to work in for this heat!

Not sure why this place isn't a full 5 stars. 4 of us had a unanimously unbelievable dinner on a Monday. We ordered almost everything on the menu. 

ALL the ceviches
Pig tails are a MUST
Lomo saltado is killer
Bok choy ruled 
Parsnip gelato ??! Yes. 
Wine and cocktail selection was a delight. 

There are a lot of weird cranky people who don't know what they're talking about - or how to have some respect for service industry folks.

I've been living in east williamsburg for a year with people consistently telling me to go here. We were a party of 5 seated outdoors. I think if we were inside that may have improved our experience as the ambiance and service quality seemed very different. Our dinner took around 3 hours because of how slow the service was. 

Nevertheless, while on the steeper side, the menu here is really nice. We enjoyed the drinks and ordered the quinoa, mushrooms, 2 ceviches, and the seafood paella dish. The ceviche and mushrooms were standouts while the quinoa we could have passed on and the paella fell a bit flat on flavor. Oh, and the fries are amazing!

A date and I stopped in to the Llama Inn for a late dinner this past Monday and it did not disappoint.  We sat on the rooftop, and all though it was a hot and muggy, New York summer night, the atmosphere, ambience and music more than made up for it.  The food was fantastic, standouts being the Bok Choy and Pig Tails.  The Bok Choy was truly one of my favorite dishes I've had in a long time, perfectly combining sweet and savory flavors with an outstanding texture.  The cocktails were also great, and across the board everything exceeded expectations.  The true highlight of the night however, was the music selection upstairs.  I believe music plays a large part in the atmosphere of a dining experience, and their playlist consisted of top tier neoclassical hip hop and R&B, perfectly completing the evening. Elite spot all around, highly recommend.

I've been to Llama Inn for brunch a few times, but this was my first time for dinner. Parking was very easy. We were about 15min early for our reservation but the hosts sat us immediately. 

They do great cocktails and even better eats. The menu is always changing which makes every trip different! The service was wonderful, very attentive staff ready to clear empty plates and glasses. Our server was super knowledgeable when we had questions about preparation, as well.

Will always come back here and can't recommend it enough to friends and family.

Honestly haven't had that much Peruvian food, but if this is a good sample then sign me up! The ceviche had a delicious sauce and fresh seafood. I really liked their bok choy salad, very refreshing and good mix of ingredients. Their seared fish was good but maybe slightly overcooked, but the sauce made it still delicious. 

Overall I like the casual and hip vibe, they have a lot of plant decor mixed with upbeat music.

This place looks amazing and comfortable, a perfect environment for a lovely date night. The food, however, is aesthetically unique but nothing too special in terms of flavors. The portions are mostly on the small side for the price of the dishes. The bass was very bland, even with the special sauce that accompanied the dish. The scallop and the fluke were different, with a blend of citrus, tanginess, and sweetness, but not really that delicious. Overall, our experience was a decent one and the staff were incredibly friendly, whereas the service was also on point and quick. However, just be aware that if you order the same dishes we did, chances are you may need something extra or you will end up leaving a bit hungry still. 

Thank you for reading and good luck!

I really wanted to love this place because I love Llama San but god the service left so much to be desired. I got there early and checked in for my 7:30 table and waited at the bar for my other 2 friends to arrive. When Everyone was there by 7:31 we went to check in again with the full party and were told there were only seats left at the communal table even though I had a regular table reservation for upstairs and had checked in early and was sitting in direct eye sight of the host. Then the host said "let me see what I can do to try to pull some strings to get you what you want" and we got seated upstairs essentially at another communal table (inches away from the party next to us at one giant table" and I had to sit essentially in a plant. The giant plant covered up my entire table and my face the entire meal. I asked if my server if he can move the pot over even just a few inches so I could use my table when the food came and he said no. Thank god halfway through my meal one of server trainees took pity on me and moved the pot over himself (thank you kind sir for being the only one who cared!).

Now the food. As others have mentioned it's good, but nothing on par with llama San and portions are small for the price. My favorite item of the night was probably the bok choy salad. The lomo saltado wasn't bad, but for $82 I'd say there are way better versions of this for cheaper (my personal favorite lomo saltado in NYC is at Popular!). 

The rest of the dishes were all ok, but nothing to rave home about. The one good thing though was the cocktails - I enjoyed the two that I got and my friends enjoyed theirs as well. 

If you're in the neighborhood it's a cute restaurant to try but not worth the trek out here just for this.

Before this restaurant all I knew about Peruvian cuisine was their chicken. And wow my eyes and palate was popped up to appreciate this whole different experience. From different kind of ceviches to braised meat, the drinks and in this case , also a superb service! My tastebuds were entertained and awakened with every bite, curtesy of Chef Natalie, I learned. The presentation was also high class. 
Drinks were excellent too including the classic Pisco Sour which is made with fresh egg whites, as you'll see the bartender breaks them eggs constantly. No artificial mix. Great wine selection and locally breweries and distilleries. 
Come hungry! You'd love it
Amazing! We will come back!

Listen. I'm a longtime New Yorker. I eat out a lot, and I'm used to the deal. It's expensive, it can be objectively pretentious, and servers may treat you in a manner to which the uninitiated are wholly unaccustomed (and is sometimes in fact rude by any standard).

That's kind of de rigeur here, especially at the spot-of-the-moment, where there's typically some form of negotiation/Faustian bargain between the restaurant's need to maintain a trendy reputation (often its lifeblood) and one's own need for cuisine and humanity. The point is, the food is great in this city, and we're all willing to put up with some nonsense to have experiences of which others may merely daydream.

But Llama Inn isn't the spot-of-the-moment anymore, and it hasn't been for ages. I've had many great dinners here over the years - with parents, friends, dates, everyone. But it *has* been *years*. It still has great food - certain dishes I have begged people to go try - but somewhere in Covid they caught an attitude that they just can't back up.

I and others have had kind of ridiculous experiences here lately, and you'll see similar things referenced in other reviews.

Essentially, if you think you've got a reservation... no you don't! You'll reserve a table outside but they'll close it without warning, then have no contingency for indoor seating. (A bit troubling for the few people still Covid-conscious, as was true in one case recently.) They'll offer you two seats at the bar for three people and when that clearly won't work, if you really press them, they'll put you at a communal table. They'll give you, and then very much enforce, an actual time limit at whatever table you do get.

To be totally fair, the kitchen still does great work, and the wait staff are still lovely; it seems to be more of a policy and hosting problem, and it is a *problem*. They've chosen to forego even the baseline of accommodation, and it's a shame. It makes me think again before going back, even when it's some of my favorite food in the neighborhood.

And look, this is New York! There's a near-infinite palette of of amazing restaurants to try, and more new trendy (for a reason, even!) ones every day. Ones that operate with the same (somewhat weird, but generally accepted) norms we all know. So although I'd like to continue recommending Llama Inn to friends and strangers alike - from here and elsewhere - I just can't. I'd do a lot for great food, but nothing's worth dysfunction.

We sat at the kitchen bar that was very unique, it was very cool to watch the kitchen operations. We ordered the red snapper ceviche and the fluke ceviche - both were very different and worth getting both! 

We also ordered the chicken thigh which come on skewers - great for sharing. 

The wine list was a bit eccentric for my taste but the cocktails looked amazing. 

All & all a great experience, would definitely want to try the arroz or steak dish next time!

Expectations met? Menu wasn't great at the moment. Got the staples recommended. Lots of unique flavors but served a bit oddly. Left full but not satisfied. Wouldn't go again unless for a special/new menu. Liked the rope artwork though!

5 stars for the service.  Seriously, top notch guys, and other restaurants really should send their people to train here, Lilia especially-- this is how service is done.

Great drink menu, lots of options for all alcohol lovers.  

Every ceviche is wonderful. Lomo saltado can probably feed 3 people-- it's pretty massive -- and with 1-3 small plates, you'll be pretty stuffed.

Great outdoor and indoor space.  Well thought out, good decor and vibes.
Rooftop bar is what's up. Sit in Pauline's section at the bar. She's cool and funny and makes amazing cocktails. The food is delicious as well!

We were looking for a romantic-feel restaurant and Llama didn't disappoint! Candle lit, greenery, dim lights, and just an overall cozy and intimate feel. We were seated within 15 minutes, even though we didn't have a reservation. 

Now the food: we ordered the Lomo saltado and it was AMAZING! The fries were nice and crispy, the steak was cooked perfectly (medium), the white rice was seasoned so well, and the jalapeños and guacamole was fresh IG. Absolutely delicious. 

The waitress was amazing, not pushy and helpful. I will definitely return!

Wildly disappointing and I'm surprised at the high ratings. The pork chop and the chicken skewers were tender and juicy but severely under seasoned. The restaurant smelled of smoke from the open kitchen yet the meats had little to no char flavor.

The ceviche portion was super small with only a couple pieces of fish and nothing extraordinary.

The worst was the lomo saltado as it was one of the more expensive items on the menu i think at $82, (the prices have changed from the previous menus I've seen). The fries were extremely salty and most of the dish was comprised of fries.

My partner wanted to eat out in BK for a Friday dinner and made a reservations here. We haven't had Peruvian food in a while so, we were both excited. However, I soon learned that this restaurant under the bridge was just not my vibe. 

Vibe: 2.5/5

I am a simple hole in the wall girl with old navy jeans. You walk in are blinded by everyone presenting their brand preferences from Prada to Gucci and date night looks. It was pretty loud honestly, definitely a time to sit next to your partner than across. It was not my vibe but, a good date night location for the younger crowd. I noticed a lot of people on tech there.

Food: 3/5

We order 6 dishes and one of them had to be their "family size" branzino so we wouldn't starve. We ordered two ceviches, salmon and red snapper, ($20+ each) that you could count the seven pieces on your plate. We got the pigs tails, which was my favorite, is like eating chicken feet. You have alot of fat and little meat. Finally, we got the branzino and seafood rice ( arroz con mariscos) which I won't say wasn't moist and delicious but was $72. Finally, we ended with a chocolate cake which was nice because it was multi-textured due the brittle, dry chocolate cake, and creamy ice cream below. We weren't suprised by the bill just hungry.

Service: 3/5

I think we must gone during a very busy day since our experience was so different. We sat down fine but, as the service started the service to our table was just disappointing. Like I had to flag down a waiter just to refill our water pitcher and that took over 15 mins. They were great at explaining the food especially since I am lactose intolerant and pointed items I could eat.

All in all, I won't be going back. I spent too much money to be hungry. But, happy to say I went once as I head to Queens for my ceviche fix.

I got here a bit before my friends. I sat at the bar and the bartender was extremely friendly! I got their gin strawberry drink that was quite strong and delicious. We shared the fluke ceviche, the octopus (which was kind of strange and I wouldn't recommend if you don't like olives), the bok Choy which was like a Cesar salad and I would recommend and the Lomo Saltado. The Lomo Saltado was amazing!! The scallion pancakes were delicious and it came with fluffy white rice, guac and sauces. The steak and French fries were delicious! I would definitely recommend!

Stopped here on a whim from a list of places provided by our Airbnb host. They sat us right away in the cute outdoor seating. The meal was delicious, especially the lomo saltado. Service was great too!

I brought a group of friends who were visiting from another county to this restaurant and it was a nightmare. Our waitress was lovely but everyone else we encountered was plain rude. We mentioned the ceviche was a little salty and the manager sent another plate of the same dish that we didn't ask for with a passive aggressive comment. And for that one comment we made, we were punished with progressively saltier and saltier dishes that came after. Our last dish, Lomo Saltado, was way too salty and it was inedible. I was so embarrassed by this whole experience and it ruined our mood for the night.

Don't come! Is overpriced and marketed as a "family style" but the plates are small and salty. The arroz con mariscos has no rice and their drinks are awful. I am not sure why people come here (bad taste maybe) but I came once and it was a bad experience overall

I love this restaurant for many reasons. First of all, the aesthetic is chic, high energy, and food and drink focused. Second of all, if you can, ask to be seated at one of Rachel's tables- she is the best server in the house! So knowledgeable, warm, and friendly!!!! And finally, the food. Do not sleep on the bok choy- legit you guys, if you don't order this, you're not living. The Lomo saltado is their signature dish and to good reason- order this. We also tried the hake ceviche which was bursting with layers of flavors and textures.

this place is fire. I genuinely do not understand why the reviews for this place are only a four-star. Possibly people trying to look for a six stars instead of five and missing. Food is delicious. Cocktails are terrific. Service is also excellent. Great place for a date.
i came here yesterday for brunch and honestly it lived up to the hype. great food and ambiance - will be thinking about that bok choy salad for awhile!!

Loved everything! The ambiance is what drew me here but the food was what completely won me over. Had the fluke ceviche, arroz con mariscos and lomo saltado to eat. Probably too much food for two people but it was wonderful mix of items. The ceviche broth was insanely good, the arroz con mariscos so well prepared and the flavors and preparation on the lomo saltado was just perfection. We had a few cocktails- the llama del ray and el chapo which were unique and incredible. Great spot- will be back!

One word, PHENOMENAL!!!!!!!!!!! 
This is most definitely a must go. Prices are justifiable for the high quality foods. Advice: get ALL ceviches on the menu. Sorry for no pictures I couldn't contain myself :-)
The bok Chou salad is out of this world. Ceviche is good and steak thing with fries is delicious. Also recommend the whole fish and chicken kabobs.
Phenomenal dinner! I loved the lomo dish, it was the main attraction. I thought the flavors were very authentic and thoughtful.
Can't speak highly enough about this spot.  Pure class.  Food is something that you will never stop craving.  Great wine selection too.

Ambience is really nice, relaxing and energetic at the same time. Service was good too. The drinks were pretty good, especially the one with mezcal in it. In terms of food, the bok choy salad is extraordinary. Get it!!!! We also had the fried rice omelette which was pretty good too.

Before getting to heart of the Llama, let me first commend the wait staff and environment. The staff was friendly and knowledgeable. And the interior is all around fantastic. Now to the food...

The chief certainly has a vision but he needs an eye exam stat. Fine ingredients were mashed together in a confusing and conflicting manner. For instance, the octopus was served over a banana purée, mixed with a purple sauce(?) and topped with nuts. It taste like banana flavored yogurt. I truly have no idea where the octopus was. The fluke ceviche was blah. And the quinoa, served cold, was sourced from a freezer bag, I presume. 

Finally, the $89 main - steak, fries, rice and scallion pancakes - was abhorrent. I know South American steaks are heavily salted but Jesus don't shove my face into the Salton Sea. And the tenderness natural in a filet was nowhere to be found. Chewiness replaced it. Overcooked to boot. 

I once heard a description of Michael Bay films as special effects masquerading as plot. I would say Llama confuses novel with good. 

Our waiter at one point called a dish controversial and steered us away. I tried it anyway. It wasn't controversial. It was sad.

We had a great time and an amazing meal in Llama Inn. However two of four people got their main course while we were still eating appetizers. Two other people got the main course 15 min later so ours was already cold.
Also, I don't think the quality, portions, service matches the prices. But I would definitely go again!

Split the bill wrong

Had shells of shrimp in the food

Terrible value for what you are getting

One of the best restaurants I have ever been to! We were able to walk in, but generally they recommend making reservations 2 weeks in advance. Fun yet relaxing atmosphere. Delicious, interesting and flavor full dishes. The waiters were all very knowledgeable about the dishes origination too. 

Highly recommend the ceviche, pig tail, and llama del rey cocktail.

Went to Llama Inn with friends for Saturday dinner. Everyone had a wonderful time at this beautiful space with excellent, tasty dishes.

Quality: An extremely enjoyable meal in a lovely setting. The weakest point was the cocktails, I was just not crazy about their iteration of the Pisco Sour or their specialty drink Llama Del Rey. The food however hit the spot. The Fluke Ceviche is a stand-out, while the Salmon Ceviche, a bit more Asian inspired, is also quite good. The Chicken Thigh is served on skewers with a beautiful purple chips laid on top. Incredible and should not be skipped. The Arroz Con Mariscos, was flavorful and fresh. And the Lomo Saltado is the star of the show, tender steak and all the fixings to create scallion pancake steak tacos.
Quantity: Family-style dining, even with lighter food items it is a lot.
Value: $17-$20 for Cocktails. $26 for the Fluke Ceviche. $25 for the Salmon Ceviche. $24 for the Chicken Thigh. $36 for the Arroz Con Mariscos. $82 for the Lomo Saltado.
Ambiance: Llama Inn is a chic Peruvian restaurant in Williamsburg. It has tall windows surrounding the space, making it attractive and welcoming. They have a well designed outdoor patio, and then plenty of seating inside. The bar is at the center, with tables and booths along the windows. The kitchen is wide open, giving full view of the flames. A few unique art pieces decorate the space and instrumental music played in the background.
Crowd: We were able to slip in without a reservation, but it is highly recommended.
Service: Our waitress was fantastic and attentive.
Parking: Decent parking options in the area.

I came here with a friend after reading a lot of good reviews and since it having a Michelin Bib, I would be expecting great things. We made a reservation on a weekday for dinner. Reservations are made through Resy, and we made it earlier in the week.

The ambience was definitely lowkey. It was a good atmosphere. The service was average. It was busy around the restaurant, but there was a good amount of time between us seating with the menu, ordering drinks, and ordering our entrees. 

Our server explained the menu and suggested since it was us two dining; she recommended the Lomo Saltado and 3 smaller tapa dishes. 

We ended up ordering the Fluke Ceviche, Bok Choy Salad, and the  Mushroom/Potato dish as our share-ables. We also ordered the Lomo Saltado, which is a popular traditional Peruvian dish consisting of stir fried beef, fries, and rice. 

We enjoyed the fluke ceviche. It had a good amount of acidity and flavorful with every bite. I thought it was an outstanding dish. Unfortunately this was probably the best dish of the night for us. The Bok Choy Salad was an interesting take on integrating asian vegetables as a salad. I thought it was an unique and interesting dish. The mixed mushroom came after our main course (Lomo Saltado) due to an error in the kitchen. The mushroom I believe was a stir-fried king oyster(?) mushroom, was a solid dish with great umami flavor.

The Lomo Saltado (our main course) was a complete letdown. I seldom let the price of a certain dish deter me from having a great meal. But sadly, this dish priced at $82, which comes with french fries. tri-tip steaks drenched in sauce, rice, guacamole, and scallion pancakes, felt like loaded fries dish from Chili's. The steak was drenched in sauce, which made it very salty to eat. It was also very chewy and hard to enjoy. This dish could've been shared with 4 people, but definitely still not worth it. There was nothing special nor memorable about this overpriced dish at all.

Overall: The smaller dishes were delicious, but the service could have been better. I was disappointed that the Lomo Saltado did not deliver to its caliber as it should have.

Let me make this clear - flavor wise this is a 5-star brunch.  My table ordered the fluke ceviche which came with crispy calamari, soft hominy corn, toasted corn and sweet potato in leche de tigre. Textures were great on this one and the flavor was delicious. We were offered a "pickleback" shot with our leftover leche de tigre. I wish we knew how much it would cost ahead of time because these were $17 each. The lomo salteado was enough for 2 people but was delicious as well. They didn't ask how we wanted the steak cooked but it came to our table perfectly tender with a crispy crust. The home-made a
Sausage was DELICIOUS. I'd go back because the food was great and the decor was the best I've seen in a long time but the prices were a little steep. We had a cocktail and some coffee with our meal and the bill was $178 before tip.

Food:  
The food was exceptional. We got two pre-fixe menus and added an extra appetizer which was a lot for two people. All the flavors meshed well together. We also got two cocktails and a bottle of wine. Drinks are well crafted too. 

Atmosphere:
Tables were very close together, so you can definitely hear people next to you. Darkly lit in an open space. 

Service:
They were very helpful and attentive. Our waitress made suggestions on which wines would fit our interests. Went in on a Sunday night and there was a lot of space.

The octopus, ceviche and desserts were really really good. I like the atmosphere and the openness of the restaurant. I would advise against the more expensive dishes. The $82 steak taco and french fry entree was very good but not worth the price.

Ambiance was cute, dim, and a little artsy. Service here was great, and our server was especially attentive to a food allergy notice. Similar to what some other reviewers said, don't skip the chicken thigh app...probably the highlight of the night. Lomo Saltado was good, although the fries on top were a little too soggy and spicy for my taste.

First, this review mostly focuses on food. The ambiance was great and it is a nice environment to grab drinks and has a extensive and amazing drink menu. If your intent is to only grab drinks, I would recommend this place in a heartbeat. 

However, if you planned on going there for food, it is not a place I would recommend. The food is expensive and it is not worth the price you are spending. The menu is quite small and there is no apps that you can get besides ceviche and octopus which is shocking, not even chips and guacamole are offered if you wanted a small side with drinks. 
The llomo saltado was $82 and was way too salty and overall pretty disappointing for the amount of money you pay for it. Overall, for the amount of positive reviews and hype surrounding the restaurant, food wise it was a let down.

I thought everything here was just ok!
Wasn't super impressed by the food. We had the ceviche special to start - it was decent but not super memorable. The pig tails were a unique offering so it was exciting to try, but ultimately I probably wouldn't get them again. The lomo saltado was gigantic and also a unique experience, but the flavors were just meh. The star of the show was really the dessert, the banana mousse, which I highly recommend. Only reason i'd go back would be to get the dessert again. The atmosphere is generally nice but some of the tables are very close together, especially if you're dining as a pair. Service was great and our waitress was lovely.
The food is on another level -- and the prices reflect that fact! Dining here is an almost spiritual experience, to be savored and cherished with dear friends.

The vibes, staff, cocktails and food were stellar! Had the fluke ceviche, pig tails, bok choy, and arroz con mariscos (similar to a paella) and all of them were so so good, wish I had more space in my stomach to enjoy more! Also the cocktail I had with pisco quebranta, apricot, and ginger was divine! Highly recommend this spot!

Llama Inn's atmosphere really enriches your entire dining experience the more you pay attention to detail. 

The main art piece in the back right at first glance appears to just be a bunch of rags, but upon further inspection you realize they are old llama scarves. These scarves are commonly used to keep track of different llamas in a pack! 

As for the food, I wish I had ordered 2 of every ceviche. All 3 had fantastically unique tangy, acidic, and spicy textures that balanced beautifully with the richness of each fish. 

The bok choy salad was also a highlight and was presented BEAUTIFULLY. 

Service was attentive and walked us through each dish explaining taste profiles and what he enjoyed best. 

My only critique is they couldn't tell me the inspiration behind the name of the restaurant (sarcasm)

The chips and dip are a must order; I've never had chips that good and the garlic tzatziki stuff they come with are *chef's kiss* The cariñito, a mezcal cocktail, is a revelation (though I will say I had two and the second one was  too sweet, but I am not crazy about sugar and need my cocktails to fall within a smaller window of sweetness than most people)

We were there for brunch and the bacon egg and cheese burrito and cauliflower sandwich were both delicious! The bok choy as a side salad I loved, and the french fries tasted like mcdonald's fries but better which is just about the highest praise french fries could possibly receive. The tamales with prawns and eggs at the table next to us also looked bomb and I will probably have to come back to try them.
