My only notes are that when you get above $15 I think the cocktails need to be a little more booze forward, but maybe that's just me. Other than that, love.

Came to Llama Inn this evening on a date and the entire experience was wonderful. The ambience was romantic and classy. Our server Gabriel was attentive, charming, and described each dish recommendation with thoughtful detail. We started with a pisco cocktail and shared the salmon ceviche and bok choy salad both of which were delicious. The dressing alone on the salad was worth it - so flavorful. Then we each had the Atlantic Hake dish with the mushroom side and also very yummy and favorful. Our server recommended a Reisling to enjoy with our meal which perfectly complemented the fish. Finally for dessert we enjoyed a parfait type dessert made with Peruvian fruit and shaved ice and it was so unique and light. I've never tried anything quite like it before. Highly recommend llama inn for a lovely dining experience and Peruvian treat.

I came in with a friend on a Tuesday night at 8pm with a reservation, and the place was full! My friend and I each started with a glass of wine, which they let us sample before pouring the full glass, always nice. We then split the quinoa, bacon, cashew, banana as an appetizer. This was quinoa mounded over a center of banana mayo, bacon dices, and cashews that you were meant to dig into not mix. This was definitely a new flavor profile for us but we did like it! The mayo could be a bit overpowering. For entrees we had the atlantic hake sudado, but they had a substitution with monk fish for the hake (which is what drew my friend to this dish!). They said it was well cooked and tender and overall enjoyed their dish. Our other entree was the pork loin. This was well cooked and came with a thickened jus sauce splatter that was delicious. Honestly though their dessert was the true star. We had a cherimoya ice cream/italian ice, topped with pasty cream and dried cherimoya. This was light, refreshing, and indulgent all at the same time! The other dessert was a chocolate ice cream with a banana cream and fosters bananas on it, topped with a cashew brittle. It was intensely rich and creamy with a great pop of banana. 
The service was also great. Very knowledgeable, friendly, and attentive. 
Definitely a pricier spot, prepare to drop some cash on dinner and a few cocktails, but well worth it.

Solid place overall, would go back.

The space: very nice decor, high ceilings with massive windows letting light in, lots of plants and a beautiful wrap around bar in the center.

The service: Friendly and quick 

The food: Everything was delicious. The breakfast burrito was hearty and full of flavor, the fried rice omelette had interesting textures especially with the kick from pickled chilis and the spicy mayo, the mussels was refreshing with the acidity from limes balancing out the cilantro and onions, finally the beef tenderloin was excellent.

The prices: They are pretty out there, the food is fairly priced but the drinks are NOT, would recommend avoiding. Black coffee for 8$, glass of wine for 16-18$, I'll pass.

Overall, this is a great 4.5/5 place for brunch (based on food) but would avoid drinks there

I forgot to write a review a few months ago, but I remember having a good time! I can't recall every dish as clearly, but I remember the fluke and calamari were real stand outs. I also really liked the chicken thigh skewers. We also had a bottle of red that the waiter recommended, and it was delish. 

I would come back, but probably not for the tasting menu. The tasting was a bit much, and I don't think each dish really worked harmoniously with the others. It was just a lot of good stand alone dishes--so I would recommend going for the a la carte option and just picking 2 or 3 things that spark your interest--everything was good.

Great service, nice ambience. Food is pricey, but it was worth the experience. The cuisine consisted of many things I never tried before, but everything was delicious. The flavors were new and interesting and you could tell that everything was well prepared. Would recommend for a special outing.

I would give me half star if I can, I got sick has to cancel my reservation last min.
I called in and explained why I have to cancel, but still got charged for the late cancel fee.
I called in again to explain, hoping they would understand that wasn't on purpose, the person answered the phone just said in a cold tone that this is their policy, and later asked if I want to book another reservation (which i refuse obviously lol)

This restaurant doesn't care about the customer, would never go there with this kind of attitude and experience.

The worst service by a head waiter and manager that I've ever experienced completely overshadowed a fantastic kitchen.

After arriving within the accepted timeframe for a 7:00 reservation, our waiter went out of his way to rush us through dinner, made rude comments when we failed to order our third cocktail, lied about having "run out of dessert" and seemingly only cared about his cover count for the night.

The manager was obviously complicit in the service charade, a simple "could we suggest dessert at the bar" would've gone a long way in smoothing things over but not a chance...a smirk and a condescending "thank you for joining us" was all we got.

The owner should elevate the servers delivering the dinner selections; they were courteous, helpful and pleasant unlike our pompous, pretentious lead waiter and sanctimonious manager who are better suited for wfh careers.

I've been going to Llama Inn for years now and have always had good experiences and I don't write too many reviews. I had the pleasure of meeting the manager Dan and holy crap this guy has no idea what hospitality is. How this guy is in this industry is beyond me . My friends and I will never come here again .

Overall the Llama Inn really gets 2.5 stars. The dishes we had were too sour. The overbearing taste of lime in the fluke ceviche and arroz con mariscos leave no room for the seafood flavor to come out. The seafood is fresh but hard to distinguish due to the strong lime flavor. The dishes are mainly for sharing but are too small. You and a friend can really get 4-5 bites with each dish, no more. The thigh on skewers were good but for two people you only get three. You have to pay another $8 to add an extra skewer. 
Note that three small dishes and one drink will cost you an average of $115. 
The decor is nice but the tables are packed in too close which doesn't provide you with quiet conversations. The service was friendly and comparable to other restaurants. 
With many good restaurant establishments in Williamsburg, there are better alternatives. There are also better Peruvian restaurants in Brooklyn that are comparable and better without the higher price tag.

Was excited to try this place. It has a nice open kitchen / bar layout. However, the prices are outrageous here. 

2 baked oysters for $12. The Lomo Saltado is $82 but has so few cubes of sub-par steak. It's all fries and comes with two sides of carbs. I've had full strips of high quality steak that cost about the same. 

Don't be fooled by the pictures!

Really disappointed with my experience. They seated me and my girlfriend at an eight person communal table on Valentine's Day without any advance notice. The host refused to move us to one of the open two person tables or bar seats that were available at the time. This place is too expensive to be cramming people in like that.

It was good but not typical puervian food. Lomo saltado was great just took a very long time to come out, we were almost the last ones to leave the restaurant. Drinks were good as well. Just waited forever for our main course to come out.

Amazing food and great ambiance. 
Service is a bit slow. But the food made up for the wait.

BE WARNED. Llama Inn was a huge disappointment, the only saving grace was our lovely server. I booked on Resy the outdoor "covered and heated" seating. Sounds so lovely, a warm cozy dinner. It was NOT covered and NOT heated. It was 20 degrees outside and the heaters DID NOT WORK. Asking the staff how this was insane they alluded to the fact that it is a known fact that the heating doesn't work outside. It's New York in February and the management of this restaurant somehow think its ok to lie to their guests and sit them outside with no heat. Not only that but there is 0 ambience outside, the music was glitching and the wind blew the curtains open. I wouldn't know if the food was good because by the time it gets outside it's no longer warm. No they did not comp anything either.

First off, I rarely have this strong of a review for a restaurant. I reached out to management to voice my feedback directly to them before writing a review, but didn't hear back...so here it is:

We came here for dinner with high expectations.

The good: ceviche was fresh and tasty, the bok choy was delicious. Drinks were good.

The bad:
1. RIDICULOUSLY OVERPRICED meat dishes. the pork collar had 4 tiny pieces for $34 and the main steak dish, Lomo Saltado, was very disappointing for $82. The lomo saltado was a few small pieces of steak drenched in salty gravy sauce topped with fries, served with side of rice, bread, small amount of guacamole. For someone who eats out a lot in NYC, I'm used to high prices for certain dishes but this was just ridiculous and felt like robbery. The majority of this dish is low cost ingredients-fries and rice. I actually could not belief the price of this dish for what was served.

2. The service. We had to constantly ask for more water and serving utensils for the dishes. We had an ice cream dessert that melted before a serving utensil was given to us. Our server never came to ask us how any of the dishes were.

Overall, a very disappointing and overpriced meal. If you do come here, stick to drinks, ceviches and probably the vegetable dishes.

We absolutely loved coming here. The food is delicious and the service is even better. We had Rachel and John. They went above and beyond to make sure my 17 month old had everything he needed to stay happy at dinner. We were nervous that such a nice restaurant wouldn't be accommodating to little ones, but I saw plenty of other kids there. It helped that the music was loud enough to drown out baby noises, but not so loud you couldn't hear the people across from you. 

You can't go wrong with the drinks, especially the sangria cocktail. The mushroom rice plate is a must order!

Overall rating 4.9997
.0003 off because of my company

From looking at the low star reviews, I'm pretttty sure this is a Michelin star restaurant. How are people confused that it's expensive? This is a $$$ place. I don't understand.

One of my favorite places in the world is Peru (highly, highly recommend Machu Picchu). This is the best ceviche I've ever had in my life. I actually came to the terms I didn't like ceviche a few years ago. But man oh man, soo good. Get both. It's worth it.

It was a little weird that they don't serve pisco sour on the menu. I think I had to request it to get a variation of it.

I believe I went around 6 or 7 (pre-peak) and it was pretty quiet. I sat near the "bar/ kitchen" but I wish I chose a dining table. The decor is gorg (plants everywhere) & it literally feels like you're in another world than the hustle & bustle of Williamsburg. I'm obsessed.

For the main, my date & I split the Crispy Pig Tails... it, was, interesting. I don't think I could get over the poor tails on the pigs ! Surprisingly a reasonable serving size, but not for me.

I will definitely be coming back & still think about the ceviche.

Food was very good. Had the salmon ceviche and lomo saltado, which appeared to be the current special. Both very tasty and well-executed.

Atmosphere was solid for what it was - vibey, energetic, loud. 

Service was fine - waitress was not particularly attentive, but definitely friendly and helpful whenever she did make the rounds. Can't hold that against her - guessing staff may be overworked (see last point). 

Expensive-ish, but not unexpectedly so. Think the two of us got out of there for about $120, w/ tip but no alcohol.

Minus 1 Star because it was crowded as all get-out. Could barely fit in the front door and had to wait ~10 minutes for our table despite a reservation. Tables were so close together you had to ask your neighbor to move their table to allow space for someone sitting in the window bench to get out of their seat. The positive flipside of them packing so many bodies in is that we were able to change our reservation 2 days prior and still find something on the late side of the dinner hour. Not guaranteed at a lot of places in NY, so that was nice.

In short: good food, good atmosphere, don't come here if you're claustrophobic or in a rush.

I loved this place!!!!! It is a bit expensive, but I think the food is super good. 

+ Lomo saltado: DIY which is SO FUN. They have this egg omelete that you use to wrap around the meat and it was DELICIOUS. I also really liked all the meat as well. It was perfectly cooked + so plentiful with the fries. 
+ Bok choy salad: SOOO GOOOD. I am obsessed!!!! Do not skip on this. 

All the drinks were delicious, it was well decorated restaurant, with a lot of coziness. I can't wait to plan to be back!

First things first, the inside is beautiful, walking into the space... it's beautiful and spacious. Llama Inn opened 7 years ago and can't speak to past service but today, it was amazing, and for a Saturday brunch, that's a biggie. The food is amazing and its not surprising that they are on the James Beard list of nominees. So let's talk food - it's more Peruvian fusion and got-damn I love the vibe. There was nothing that wasn't delicious and even when it didn't make sense, it came together - the salty, the sweet, the sour, and the fat were all balanced in each delicious bite. So worth going and might I suggest go now.

this was a let down. i was excited to try this spot, but the food was underwhelming at best. way overpriced, took ages to get the food and no it wasn't busy, and the spicy chicken sandwich (brunch) was over cooked, not spicy and pretty flavorless. 
service was good, but sadly will not return simply based on the lack of excitement in the food. 
other brunch dishes the table got: breakfast burrito, avocado toast (beautiful presentation but wayyyy overpriced for one piece of toast) 
the vibe was great, the aesthetic is very natural and modern.

The ambiance was beautiful but it was a bit tight inside. 

The portions are small excluding the Lomo salado. It was salty and too dense. It was hard to finish. 

The service was good. They were very attentive. 

I wouldn't go again. There was nothing out of this world where it would make me want to go back again.
$84 for a small plate of prime rib with a  couple rolls, broccoli and sauce on the side? GTFO

Obscenely overpriced. The hostess had an attitude and the waiter was pushy. We spent nearly $300 and we were still hungry. Would not go here again- the portions were super tiny and crazy expensive for what it was. $44 for fried chicken?! And it was like 4 dry pieces? I can't even. The appetizers tasted better but again you're paying like $10 per bite!! We had to go get pizza afterwards because we were all starving. And literally the non alcoholic drink came in a tiny little kiddie cup and that was $15. Half of it was a giant cube of ice and a flower for decoration. It was basically guava juice. Shrinkflation is rampant but this was the most ridiculous I've seen!

Just finished dining here about 15 mins ago, and I must say, TAKE YOUR MONEY ELSEWHERE. 

My partner and I paid $250 for our meal including tips and it definitely was not worth it when that price point is almost the same as having an omakase meal. 

We had 3 drinks, 1 app, and 3 entrees: 
1. First off, the portion sizes were really small. 
2. The drink I had tasted similar to a Moscow mule which they were charging 20 bucks for. 
3. The pork belly app was fine but it definitely had too much sauce on top of it and was not charred enough. 
4. We waited almost 30 mins for our first entree to come out l, which were the clams served on top of the sourdough. Honestly, that was the only best tasting dish we've had out of the 3 entrees. 
5. I understand that they were probably sending the dishes out one at a time so we can eat it while it's made to order, but the wait in between the dishes were really long and we pretty much grew impatient. 
6. The sea bass dish was mediocre. The portion size of the sea bass was ridiculously small compared to its other complimenting component. 
7. The fried chicken was a disappointment. Honestly tasted the same as the fried chicken I could get at Stop&Shop. People can say, the hell would you go to a Peruvian restaurant for fried chicken when they got other options. However, if they are going to put something on the menu, I should at least expect it to be tasty. 
8. Ambiance was okay, since we sat at the bar.. so I don't really expect much. But the service wasn't that amazing to be worth tipping 40 bucks. But sure, I understood the 20% tipping policy.
 
Lastly, I would definitely not be back for another meal.

Llama Inn remains impeccable. I finally made it in time for happy hour (M-F from 5-6:30) and tried:

+ Llama del rey
+ La calzada
+ Cariñito
+ Fog catcher 
+ Fluke ceviche
+ Baked oysters
+ bok choy
+ Iberico pork collar 
+ Beef tongue 
+ Side of fries 
+ Stone fruit dessert 

My favorite cocktails were the llama del rey and fog catcher, while the top dishes were the oysters and bok choy. That bok choy is NYC's best-kept salad secret. Dessert was also awesome!
Food is bland. Would not go back. If I wanted good fusion Peruvian food I'd sooner go to Artesano, where the flavors slap! Rude  female bartender with short hair.

I do not leave reviews no matter how terrible the experience was. I'm leaving this place right now so annoyed. My boyfriend and I spent almost 400$ for an hour and half of dragged out service serving each dish 30 minutes between. My biggest problem was the bartender. She was so cold and rude. I've worked in the service industry for so long. You're supposed to sell the imagery of the dish to the customer and explain everything. When I asked for suggestions she  didn't really know what to say and could kind of care less. For that much money I feel insulted. Explain the dish and really sell the place you work at.

Llama Inn delivers on delicious ceviche and is a great date night vibe. The seating is pretty tight so it can feel quite cozy (FYI for parties of 4+). I only wish the portions were slightly bigger for what they charge.
Usually love it here but they changed the menu a lot, removed lomo saltado & replaced with smaller, equally expensive entrees. Service was fine, disliked the shared table.

I have very mixed feelings on Llama Inn. The space is absolutely gorgeous and the waiter was great. Every bite of food I had was fantastic and the cocktails were solid, HOWEVER, the portions for the price you're paying are absolutely awful. Besides the shareable plates which are +$40, every other dish on the menu is 10 bites of food maximum. Expect to pay at least $100 a person to get a remotely decent meal or fully expect to leave Llama Inn hungry. The value here is just not good
ambience was good, the portions are so small and extremely overpriced. really gave me "The Menu" vibes (the movie) which isn't good....

I think the food here was excellent. Every dish we ordered was delicious, and was certainly satisfying and well prepared. Unfortunately the service specifically from the hostesses was not the best. We were initially told a one hour wait for a table for two, and then two hours later we still had not gotten a call. We went to the hostess stand who had clearly forgotten we were there, as half of the tables were empty. They hastily sat us down at the bar, which was fine, but we would have preferred a table. Overall I would come back for the food, but the service was definitely lacking.

The ambiance and the experience was out of this world. I would post the names of the dishes but I can't pronounce them. Ty made our experience unforgettable and he taught us a lot about Peruvian cuisine, a TRUE historian of fine dining
Meh. It's really good, but it's also really pricey. It's worth checking out but I feel like there are better meals/experiences out there for the price tag.

Pros-Mason our server was excellent! Otherwise there is nothing about this restaurant that would make me want to return. It is a hot reservation  right now- and I think the jokes on us patrons! I love fine dining- but what we had was good,not great food,tiny,tiny portions,ridiculously high prices,communal table and kitchen help (open kitchen)yelling every few minutes. This all resulted in a subpar dining experience.Many better dining options in the neighborhood!!

Service was slow . Food was okay. Chicken was plain no flavor at all, couldn't finish it. Crispy ceviche is basically fried calamari... very disappointing. . Beef dish smothered with sauce and fries ...
Guess Michelin is given to anyone these days . Drinks were excellent.

I took my lady here aka Hot Niki from Duck Duck bar..... That's right, we're dating now, it's official. Not sure if any of you read my review from Duck Duck, but yeah; things worked out pretty damn well for me that night. 

Any who, we went here for the outdoor seating on a nice sunny day. We heard good things and the food was wonderful, everything was plated very beautifully, and it tastes just as good as it looked! Drinks were on point, and the restaurant is just very stunning and beautiful. If you're with a beautiful girl that you want to sit across and admire, this place has big windows with lots of light coming in, and Hot Niki looked stunning.  


Needless to say, the place was a really nice date spot, food and flavors were great, drinks were pretty, and my date was hot.

My only complaint and why I didn't give 5 stars is that we asked to sit on the roof top that looks so nice, the host looked like they were going to let us sit there, but instead gave us regular outdoor seating after asking a waiter or manager. The rooftop wasn't open for any reason in particular, I just think the server didn't want to go up and down the stairs. Not sure why you wouldn't open your rooftop up for your guest on such a nice day, when you don't even have an event or any reason to not be using it. Common guys..... Still a great time and worth it.

I tend towards their seafood dishes and salads. Cute evening date spot with wonderfully attentive staff. Everything is very inventive and the attention to detail is amazing. Things are very artfully plated and presented and they taste really good. My only minor qualm is that the lomo saltado was pretttty salty BUT I have literally tried everything on the menu and it was the one and only thing I didn't love.

Been here twice and it is easily one of my fav neighborhood spots. Their plates are small, which allow you to share a bunch of items. Beautiful, textural, and fragrant dishes. The theme seem to be green/bright acidic flavors juxtaposed with smokey and creamy tones. Love it all.

The main good points were novelty (haven't had high-end peruvian elsewhere in nyc) and the space is lovely. 
I went with a seafood-allergic friend, and that's a bad move, his allergy wiped out most of the menu, including all the mains. So we just had 4 small plates (2 meaty things, 1 cheesy pasta, 1 cheesy asparagus, if you are vegan then there's pretty much nothing for you). 4 small plates and 1 cocktail was over $150 including tip, and we left hungry. Nothing was better than OK, and the asparagus wasn't even that. The pasta dish was different from anything I had had before, like a pesto with different herbs, but the Italian version is more popular for good reason. 
Went to union pool for $4 tacos after, they were tastier than anything we had a llama inn.  
My girlfriend loves this place and thinks it's wonderful, as do most of the people I know who've been there. Maybe we ordered badly....

Great food; excellent atmosphere and service. Started with delicious trumpet mushroom skewers. Also, had scallop skewers which were not quite as good: we went on to have a delicious tiradito and truly outstanding crispy squid in leche de Tigre- the texture and flavor is not to be missed. Finally, we had a larger plate of fried chicken in a yummy sweet sauce. We also enjoyed a small plate of clams, beans and grilled bread with an emphasis on the beans. Prices are not shy but all was very enjoyable. Not drinking but drinks looked good. Loved the plants and music. While the bread clam and bean dish was very tasty - it was a bit heavy for a hot day. Not a fan of incense which was inexplicably lit at one point (and gave me an instant headache), but that only lasted about 20 minutes or so (odd choice). When we went the restaurant was surrounded by earth movers for infrastructure work on the block, but the atmosphere and food was so good that we barely noticed.
Nonsense of a place ... extreme pricing limited menu one bathroom ... tough choice to repeat
Food and service were both phenomenal. Definitely a place for special occasions but a summer rooftop dinner here is well worth it.

pricey, but worth it imo! we had a great server who very thoroughly explained every dish in the prix fixe menu, which were all delicious, especially the fluke ceviche. the drinks were also a standout here. we came close to close so the space was fairly empty which was nice. would recommend sitting indoors rather than on the patio which is right next to the highway.

Llama inn, llama OUT.

Diarrhea for days. Days days days days. Let's have fallen asleep.

A cool bar with good vibes in Williamsburg. I came with a group of 5 and we sat at a booth. 

What we ordered:
- Papi Don't Preach: my favorite drink! I thought it was refreshing. 
- Cool for the Summer
- Llama del Rey
- Bananarama (?): this was too strong for my liking. 
- Another drink that I am forgetting 
- A banana cream cake (?)

Service was great and our group definitely lingered a little bit but they did not rush us at all!
Great  place to share different options from the menu. Everything was flavorful and balanced. Would recommend 100!

Solid 4.5/5 Hipster foodie excellence. Giving them 5 stars because I feel like everyone's knocking off a star for nitpicks and I'll just choose to point them out in the review

Positives:
Cocktails great
Wine list interesting, great picks particularly liked their orange wine by the glass
Food King Trumpet, Mackerel Tiradito, Tallarines Verdes, and Chicken entree - all excellent. Probably the chicken was my favorite but all very good
Dessert I had their Cake with Banana Ice Cream and thank god, it was actually cake and a bunch of ice cream and excellent! Sometimes fancy places 'deconstruct' crap into some crappier thing. No, it was just a great piece of cake and ice cream. 
Staff were doing the Michelin Star Bait things like showing you the bathrooms all the way to the bathroom. I appreciate it.

Negatives:
Hostess sucked. Too cool for school vibes, hey man this isn't a nightclub. Had a go F yourself aloof look when we left too. Weird. This is an easy job just be friendly and happy to have me.
A little too loud. They're going for lively but I think they need to put sound baffling on the ceiling to try and work on the echo. The staff couldn't hear me, it wasn't just us not hearing each other.
Pacing issues with the meal. Weird delays followed by multiple coming out at once awkwardly. It happens.

All in all would def recommend and I would def go back even with the hostess attitude.

Haven't been to Llama Inn in a while & was a little disappointed when I realized they changed the menu BUT I was blown away with all of the new dishes!  Every bite was amazing! 

Our server suggested our dishes & he was spot on! Everything was delicious & super flavorful. The squid & beet ceviches are a must! The pork dish with sweet potato is a hit!  I will miss some of the old dishes on the past menu but the new items were certainly AMAZING! 

The restaurant is a cool local spot in the neighborhood & a must try!

Oh where can I even start ??? This place absolutely blew my mind. We came here for brunch while visiting, this place was a James beard nominee, so we had to give it a try. The ambiance of the place was wonderful and was very tropical inside. Lots of plants and open air space that really set the mood. Our server and host were extremely helpful, guiding with preferred menu choices and cocktails to begin our tasteful journey. We had several appetizers and each one had unique flavor profiles that were rather pleasing to the palette. The oysters had to be my favorite for sure. The cocktails each had select Peruvian liquors that matched well with all of the dishes. We all tried other things on the menu ranging from the pork shoulder, chicken thigh and mushroom toast. Every bite was cherished! I would love to return here. They said their dinner menu was even better. !

Amazing Peruvian infused food. We had a group of six and had almost everything on the menu. The menu is small yet every dish is expertly crafted. This is a must stop in Brooklyn and if weather permits sit outside on the rooftop terrace.

Haven't heard a single bad thing about Llama Inn and it had been on my summer bucket eats so when my friend asked me to brunch, of course I immediately said yes. Should preface this by saying I lived in Peru for about a month and am a huge fan of Peruvian food, but have found it difficult to come by.

We went on Sunday at 2 pm and had a reservation, but it was pretty empty so don't think it's necessary to make one. We asked the server for recommendations and glad we did, because everything was delicious. I'm not much of a drinker for brunch so opted for a drip coffee which was very good. Hard to find good black coffee so I was already pretty impressed with just that.

We split everything between the two of us-- ordered the fluke ceviche to start and the lomo saltado and the big breakfast. The ceviche was very good, which came in leche de tigre. Very tart and a little spicy, accompanied by corn and some sweet potatoes. I found the fish to be a bit of a thick cut, but I think that's just a preference. 

The big breakfast came out next, which has toast, a tamal, pork shoulder, blood sausage, and scrambled eggs. This is a great dish to share as it's plated like a little spread and you can pick at the various items. The meat was very tender and the seasoning was unique and paired wonderfully with the crema. 

The lomo saltado came out next and this thing was massive. It had the meat on the bottom topped with french fries, two eggs, banana and crema. Also comes with a side of rice. The sauce for the meat was also another acidic vinegar-based concoction which was delicious. The fries on top were super crispy and reminiscent of McDonalds fries (my favorite) while the ones on the bottom got soaked up in the vinegar sauce which were delicious with the meat and eggs. It was a lot of food, but there are few things I enjoy as much as a long slow meal with conversation and we did a pretty good job making our way through almost everything after some time. 

We lingered here til past 4:30 and the service here was really great. Also a very cute interior with nice spacing between the seats, making it a relaxed vibe. I'm really not much of a bruncher, but this brunch may have changed my perspective! Overall, I think this goes without saying but if you don't like tart acidic flavors full of lime and vinegar, this spot (or Peruvian cuisine as a whole) may not be to your liking.

Dude.... The squid ceviche with that sauce... the wagyu lomo saltado...omg. Nice bohemian tulum-y vibes. Clay plates and cups not only is the place a vibe but it's one of those rare gems in NY. The food was nothing short of an explosion of flavor in my mouth

On a random side street in Brooklyn, adjacent to a small hotel and a freeway overpass, is an unlikely location to find such a wonderful gem, but Llama Inn is truly a Peruvian oasis in the city.  I went for Saturday brunch with some friends and was absolutely astonished to find plenty of street parking right in front of the restaurant!  Walking in, you're immediately greeted by art with bright, vibrant colors against a cheery white background and tables surrounding a chic central bar.  Once upstairs, it's like you've left Brooklyn.  The rooftop is stunningly gorgeous, with tropical vibes, comfy seating and some areas with more overhead coverage for those not wishing to experience the full brunt of the sun.  It's a real moment.  Unfortunately for my party, although I did have rooftop reservations, the only table available was fully exposed to the sun on a nearly 90 degree Fahrenheit day, so we sashayed our sundresses back inside before imminent make-up melt down could occur.

I started with a Llama Del Rey, a refreshing pisco and red wine based sparkling drink that was reminiscent of red sangria.  Most of the cocktails had cute, cheeky names which added to the festive brunch feeling.  We ordered chips and dip for the table which were quite good.  The chips tasted fresh.  The winning appetizer however, was the ceviche with calamari, lime, red onion and cilantro.  It was zesty and flavorful.  For a main I had a generous sized breakfast platter with scrambled eggs, brioche toast, blood sausage and pork shoulder tamal.  I hurt myself trying to eat it all because it was soooooo good.  I mean I had to do some major dress adjustments to account for my distended abdomen afterwards, but it was worth it!  Biting through the firm texture of the blood sausage casing created a great juxtaposition with the soft, friable, savory filling.  The pork shoulder in the tamale was tender, succulent and bold in flavor.  I can't recall the last time, if ever, I had better pork.  One of my friends had the fried rice omlette which was also delicious.  For desert, I loved the elevated take on flan with crushed macadamia nuts and crème de mint topping.  The sorbet with frozen grapes beautifully assembled on top was another fantastic choice on a warm summer day.

Everyone from the host to the servers was extremely personable and helpful.  The restaurant was also playing a mix of Beyoncé and Aaliyah that morning, so my friends and I had a blast.  If you're looking for a place with fun atmosphere and delicious food, check out this spot.

Great place to go if you're ready to ball out or if someone else is paying. Otherwise, it can get quite pricey for really small portions. Girls gotta eat yknow?

At the end of the meal we were still hungry so ended up getting one more dish but $200+ later we made plans to get a second dinner later in the night haha

Food was INCREDIBLE just some portions were small af for the price. Definitely still worth going to and they were accommodating for gluten free folks!

An experience that was the perfect way to say good bye to my brother visiting from Peru . The colorful and well balanced cocktails  to start a hot day. Delicious and flavorful dishes, the chef expresses traditional Peruvian cuisine and hits it out of the park! Leave room for dessert. We will definitely come back this time to sit at the bar area upstairs.

Wow! This place is absolutely outstanding!

We went for brunch on the later side of the afternoon and it just blew me away. We started with coffee and tea which were both very tasty. The service was extremely attentive and they explained each dish in detail when they were dropped. We ordered the fluke ceviche, lomo saltado, and the big breakfast. The ceviche was so fresh and bright. It was an extremely memorable dish. I loved the flavors of the blood sausage and pork shoulder in the big breakfast, just so tasty. The star of the show was 100% the lomo saltado. Beneath that bed of McDonald's-esque french fries and sauce was this brothy, beautiful stew like dish consistent of bananas and sirloin. Just outstanding.

The ambiance was stunning. The restaurant is just so well thought. We were there for a while and actually didn't notice that the staff had sat down for their family meal before dinner started. The fact that they let us sit there with us and didn't kick us out really says something about this place. They have something really special going here and you should make the visit if you're in or around Williamsburg.

The flavors are really bold and bright, and the ceviche was delicious. The sauces are so good I would buy a bottle as a salad dressing. The only thing is that the portions are really small for the price. Even at a similarly priced restaurant in Williamsburg, I leave pretty full, but here we were still hungry enough to grab pizza after a pretty hefty bill

Started great, we sat at the bar, ordered a few drinks and apps. We finished our apps, and before we had a chance to order a second round of drinks, we were given the bill - even though we didn't ask for it. Before we could clarify that we planned to order more, the bartender walked away. At that point we agreed to go elsewhere. Over priced, pretentious, and as a Peruvian, much better food elsewhere. Forget this place, try Mission Ceviche in the UES.

Order the wagu beef dish. 
But portion is not the same as the photo on the website.
It is a dish over $100.
Charged 160 dollars for 8 cubes of steak and a pile of friends doused in soy sauce. I would advise ordering something else

We came here for a double date on a Saturday night. You already know you're in for a treat at the entrance; the carved wooden door gives way to a beautiful, airy space with tons of plants and an open kitchen.

We each ordered a cocktail; I got the La Santa (which is their take on a daiquiri). I thought it was alright. We ordered the octopus and mushroom antichucos, the crispy squid and scallop ceviche, the Japanese eggplant, pork collar and steelhead trout, and then the wagyu saltado. The food is PHENOMENAL. The flavors dance across palette in a wonderful symphony. The leche for the ceviche is the best I've ever had. It had a little kick to it that really made it stand out. The Lomo Saltado was perfection; there's a whit sauce that comes with it that was absolutely amazing. For dessert, we got the olive oil cake with ice cream and just when we thought the food couldn't get any better, it did! The cake was perfectly moist and the ice cream was indescribable. The service here is top notch and our waiter did a great job making suggestions. Overall, we really enjoyed our meal and everyone left extremely satisfied.

For starters this place is amazing; we did the tasting menu as a large group for a birthday celebration. Each step of the meal was perfectly curated and the food was amazing (sorry didn't take pics). Memorable mentions were the fish skewers, beets, & fried chicken. Got the llomo saltado as an extra add on but could have lived without. The drinks were fast and perfectly curated based on what part of the meal we were on, in total it was a seven course menu of interesting takes and flavors. I can for sure say you won't get a duplicate in Peru but this fusion is as good and a lot of the time better than what I had eaten in Peru. Service was impeccable.
Just buckle up for the price tag at the end of the meal, does it justify, sadly no. It might be indicative of the area but I simply can't point friends in this direction without a $$$$ warning. A bit of a bummer at the end when I couldn't get change for $100, but that's ok.
Service was great. Food was fantastic. Cocktails were on point. Would definitely recommend.

Staffs were very friendly and accommodating. We made reservations however some of our friends were stuck in traffic, the waiter explained to us the menu.

Food was delicious, fresh and healthy.

I would pass on the Crudite, the Bao is interesting if you're not allergic to seafood.

Would recommend trying the Larry and Japanese Sweet Potatoes as savory items and the sweet item to try is Japanese Pancakes, it so sweet and fluffy!

The ambiance is zen especially on a rainy day. Would recommend coming here!

The food at llama inn is so creative & delicious, I honestly didn't have a single bad dish. I came with a group of 5 on a Thursday evening (we had a reservation) and we were seated right away. Each dish is so unique and the flavors are amazing. Everyone was pleased with the food which is not an easy task. We never felt rushed and loved the cozy atmosphere inside. Will definitely be back!
Fire vibes and food. Love to come here even though, I feel like the experience was not the same after the pandemic for me. I miss the anti cuchos and some of the ceviches

Genuinely my favorite restaurant in the city! The lomo saltado is a great dish for sharing, and it's a pretty fun spin on traditional lomo saltado with the combination of rice and French fries (with scallion pancakes to sop up the sauce afterwards). I've also tried their ceviche and a handful of anticuchos and was pleasantly surprised by each dish. 

The drinks are also great (the chicha morada and corn/mezcal cocktails are my personal favorites) and they also boast a wide selection of spirits. It's a bit pricey, but an excellent spot for a night out in Williamsburg.

After securing a same-day Llama Inn reservation, four of us excitedly walked into a vibrant atmosphere on a Saturday night and were seated in a row at a window counter. Unfortunately, I left largely disappointed. 

The beef heart appetizer was the first - and ultimately my favorite - item of the entire meal. Flavorful and tender, one order (two skewers) is perfect for two people to share. The Tuna and Scallop ceviche appetizers were decent, although much of the juices went to waste - I would encourage the restaurant to present small bowls to the patrons ordering ceviche, so that the broth does not have to be awkwardly enjoyed directly from the communal plate.

What brought the entire experience down was the Wagyu Saltado, their "signature" dish. First, this was extremely salty. When I say this, I do not mean "bringing out the flavor" salty - I mean that it is overwhelmingly salty to the point where it is difficult to enjoy. Also, the amount of meat per person was barely more than the amount of meat per person from the previously-mentioned skewers. Yes, the dish was served with lots of filler: rice, fries, guac, and unlimited scallion pancakes (the latter of which was tasty), but to give so little meat and charge $160 (!!!) is absolutely absurd and a pure ripoff.

We ordered the olive oil cake with banana ice cream for desert - the ice cream itself was great, but the olive oil cake also was outrageously salty.

I have no complaints about the service and staff, but the combination of exorbitant prices and underwhelming quality simply cannot justify a higher rating.

Trendy spot for Peruvian food in Brooklyn. I would highly recommend having a reservation here, especially for the weekends. The food was decent and definitely unique. We came here with a group of four and shared all the dishes.

We started off with cocktails, 2 different ceviches, and beef heart skewers. Definitely some of the most unique ceviche flavors I have had - both were incredibly refreshing. We then split the lomo saltado - the most highly anticipated dish of the night. Unfortunately 3/4 of us found it incredibly salty and the steak to fry ratio was completely off considering the price (we probably each had 2 morsels of beef). We finished with the olive oil cake which was okay, nothing to write home about. 

Overall cool spot to check out but will probably not be returning any time soon.

I'm very disappointed so many things changed since the last time I visited this place 5 years ago - the food was good and affordable not sure why they made this place not delicious and with crazy prices. I ordered the lomo saltado - it's $115 dollars when it was $40 dollars before. Let me tell you it's a joke - so little pieces of onions, crushed in French fries on top and so little steak and rice. The chicha morada is $12 dollars and it had so much ice that after few minutes I could barely taste it anymore and for $12 bucks like it's an alcoholic drink. The appetizers were the only good part

Not sure why this place doesn't have 4+ stars!?!? I'm a total food snob and this place blew me away. Had a reservation with a dear friend, ordered the scallops, the king trumpet skewers, duck sausage, and the pork. Every bite was flavorful perfection, and the service was fantastic. This was a month ago and I'm still thinking about it. Highly recommend.

The place is beneath the flyover so expect noise when you are approaching the restaurant. Food is decent, a friend of mine and I ordered some of the appetizers and entree to share. I like that they simplify it down their menu just to a single paper and double sided. On one end you have the cocktails and beer menu and on the other end you have food menu.

Absolutely wonderful place for dinner when in the big apple. Located in Williamsburg in Brooklyn. You enter the doors and are greeted by the moody low lighting, aromas of excellent food, and good vibing music. The hostess was friendly and accommodating. I recommend having a reservation when coming to this place as it is a smaller restaurant. The table ahead of us was taking a little longer to wrap up so we were offered bar seating until the table was ready. I ordered a cariñito and highly recommend. I came here with 3 friends. We ordered 2 dishes from the top section- the beef heart and trumpet. They came on 2 skewers each. That is enough to share a skewer with one another person. They were both flavored wonderfully. The beef heart was a bit salty but I like that. Then we got one dish from the ceviche. We got the tuna ceviche. The tuna was so tender and flavored to perfection. It is a small plate so enough for everyone to have a bite or so- but it is a lump piece of tuna. For the third section on the menu we got two items- Japanese eggplant and a fish and corn dish. Also amazing. The Japanese dish was a tad larger which was nice.  Lastly and most importantly- the Lomo Saltado. This is a must get. It is $100 but it is worth it. It is a large portion of food. It comes with potato pancakes that are heavenly and piping hot on the plate still, guac, rice, sauce, jalapeños, and the large dish of tender and juicy meat and fries and sauce. 10/10 recommend. The service was top notch. Make a rezzy here.

It's nice to see a restaurant back at the top of its game. It's a gorgeous interior, the Lomo is maybe the most delectable thing in North Brooklyn, their apps are all good too. Don't skip those mushroom skewers.

I really liked their new martini, and I thought even their service was more on point and focused than I've ever seen it. Five stars, so grateful it's here, still not quite interested in returning for brunch though.

Went for dinner and was immediately seated at their bar area where you are able to watch them prep the food. A great experience! Good ambiance and music and not too loud so conversation flowed great. The scallop ceviche is a must!

Peruvian restaurant with heavy Asian influences done in a strange way. 

+scallop: fresh scallops in a very very spicy sauce and very spicy candied ginger. Hard dish to eat
+pig tails: the soy flavored sauce felt really off. Like, the flavors were sweet but not a good kind. I also didn't enjoy the consistency of the sauce. Wish it had been stickier. 
+mackerel: nice fish with good sauce. I love corn flavored things. Strongly disliked the cheese on the side but I think that just might be me being unfamiliar with this type of flavor 
+pork collar: our favorite of the night. Pork was flavored and cooked perfectly. Very tender. Sauce was underwhelming though and I didn't love the onion with the sweet potato

While trying to get into this restaurant is annoying, the flavors are incredible and the ambience is very chic. The service was pretty good, nothing to really write about, which consisted of over-the-top Brooklyn hipster types which you can interpret any way you'd like. The space is very cool but very tight. Felt very cramped but that's also what's to be expected. We really enjoyed the quinoa salad with banana. The flavors mingled in an exceptionally pleasant way. The branzino was also amazingly delicious. We had some other fishy things as apps that were good. Beef Tenderloin Stir was just okay. Too many fries, kinda soggy. We had cocktails at the bar first which were lovely and wine at the table. Overall, worth the wait.
Cute lil Peruvian (i think) grill with potent, inventive cocktails, charming front of house staff & tasty food. Cute bar to grab drinks & small plates.

Delicious food. 
Inventive menu. 
A bit over priced. 
But an amazing dinner with a great buzzy atmosphere.

The food was well presented but in very small portions. the uncaring unfriendly staff created an unsettling experience. It was suppose to be a birthday celebration. Also, be prepare for Michelin star prices

We were recommended this place over a year ago by a friend, and finally went to check it out, however based on the reviews I was definitely a little suspicious of what our meal would entail....but boy was it good. 

I don't know what anyone is talking about but service was great and the food was AMAZING. 

Forewarning - yes, it's pricey, and for the smaller dishes I would say it's approaching being too expensive for the portions. HOWEVER, the taste of the food makes it so worth it. I would go back and spend all my money again. 

Service: I definitely saw reviews of people being rushed or not getting served. That was not what I experienced. Not only was our server attentive - we were needy and they provided! We ordered two extra dishes (beet salad, lomo saltado) on at random intervals throughout the meal because we saw them being prepped and wanted them. We asked if it was too late to add, and if it was no worries, they heard us, inquired, and were able to get it out to us without any delay in service or eye rolls. That's going above and beyond! 

Drinks we had:
- Llama Del Ray: similar to a sangria, very good
- Chupetini: truly one shot, but for $10 to essentially what is a martini condensed, not bad, and the stuffed olive was delicious
- Chiri Colada: refreshing colada! Would def recommend if you're looking for something bright
- Bottle of Albarin: refreshing skin contact wine. be warned, they offer mainly bottles of wine, and they are expensive. But we got about 5 glasses out of this so in the long run it's cheaper than the cocktails. 


Food we had:
- King Trumpet Skewers (amazing! must get)
- Beef Heart Skewers (also amazing! get!)
- Grilled shrimp (it was good - but it's one baby shrimp, so for the price, I unfortunately think this one is skippable)
- Scallop Ceviche (please get, so so so good. I would drink that broth if they gave it to me in a cup)
- Tuna Ceviche (so fresh and bright, not a big orange person but the mandarin was the perfect touch in the dish)
- Beet Salad (didn't even order this at first but sat at chefs counter and watched it get made and had to get. Super delicious combo of flavors!)
- Maine Mussels (surprised me! i thought it would be mussels with toast on the side, but boy was this good. super hearty and comforting, the cilantro is *chefs kiss*)
- Pork Collar (wow wow wow, this was probably the most bang for your buck dish when it comes to small plates and again the flavor was amazing)

and finally...the apparently hotly debated.. Lomo Saltado

- Not too salty (maybe I got a good batch? Maybe people don't know what salting a dish means?)
- Super filling, great for sharing
- $100 yes, pricey! BUT it's good for sharing!! so $50 PP or less is not egregious to me
- scallion pancakes are so so yummy
- could've used a bigger portion of pickled ingredients
- the extra sauce was good, but the sauce that really made it was the super flavor packed steak broth sitting on the bottom of the plate
- contrary to other reviews, i though we got a huge portion of meat, and it was cooked to perfection!


Decided on the lomo saltado instead of dessert, so can't comment on that...but we will be back!

Wish I had more pics of food but I ate it too quickly!

The food is good in that it is slightly different flavors than a standard tapas place, but it wasn't something that made me want more or seconds. The beef heart and mushroom skewers were pretty good. At the end of the day you are paying a premium for the ambience rather than the food.

Llama inn rightfully is noted as one of NYT top 100 restaurants this year. They rotate the menu seasonally and every season has always been phenomenal. They mostly always have a (few) ceviches on the menu, some crudo as snacks and the Peruvian classic lomo saltado. The cocktails are delicious. I always have the llama del rey. I normally make a reservation but it's spacious, so you can normally get a spot a few days in advance. It is easily of my favorite restaurants in williamsburg.

No issues with reservations! We chose to sit at the bar on the rooftop! Service was excellent. Reviews said portions were small for the price but we split an appetizer and main course and didn't leave hungry! Drinks were excellent as well!
Cool ambiance. Came here for dinner and drinks with friends. We shared the lomo saltado which was sooooooo salty we couldn't finish it.

I arrived and sat at the bar, then ordered four dishes. The food was decent, the atmosphere was great, and the rooftop was a delightful oasis. One thing I would suggest for improvement is the delivery time of the food. I had to wait 20 minutes for a beet salad, and I think they may have forgotten about it until I mentioned it to my waiter. Overall, it was an okay experience.

The food was amazing. The cuisine is asian inspired Peruvian. I had the jalapeños tequeños and lamb sausage. Both were amazing. I highly recommend the lamb sausage. I had their vegetarian ceviche and it was quite good, but a little too sour. But still quite enjoyable.

The service was great. The staff is very knowledgeable. They make sure you are taken care of.

The ambiance is great. It's classy and good for a date night. There are Peruvian accents all around.

I'm sorry, but this place is overpriced, even by NYC standards. They don't post a sample menu on their website, so I had no idea what to expect.  Granted, most of the dishes were unusual, visually appealing and tasty.  But I would not have gone if I had known that the prices were SO high for tiny amounts of food.  We left hungry.

Well you can never go wrong with Peruvian food and this place did pay a good homage.... so if you're in the mood and in the area or have a date, I would highly recommend. Given that Peruvian food on its own is just incredibly delicious and my opinion some of the best cuisine you can get, even if done OK I was expecting a little more from this restaurant ... When you're putting fusion next to the original, the fusion version better blow me out of the water and that's not really what I got. it was essentially Peruvian food with a twist, if that makes any sense . We had initially started with the lamb sausage (6/10) which was delicious however I expected a little more of a different experience than what I got . It kind of tasted like a hotdog....nothing to crazy or different .  The crispy calamari ceviche(7/10)  was something I've never had before but I would not order it again since the flavors were the same of a regular ceviche just with more texture due to the fried battered calamari(Yass girl give us nothing vibe). I'd rather stick to the original version of ceviche.  The play with textures on this dish was nice but I'm sorry it did not WOW me. I also ordered the pork shoulder(9/10) which had an amazing charr and I truly appreciated how well it was executed. I was told this dish was inspired by escabeche which considering this I feel like this one is one of the best dishes that you order here and say oh wow this is Peruvian fusion. One of my favorite things about this location is the rooftop, it's nicely decorated with a vast amount of plants that I think is the best setting for summer night dinner ( yes one whole star has been allocated on here because of that rooftop)

Great food. Got the snow peas, roasted beet salad, pork collar, and flan. The snow peas was pretty unique, I felt like the beet salad wasn't anything special but still good, the pork collar was great because it wasn't a super fatty piece of meat which is what I prefer. The dessert was a flan with some kind of mint sauce on top. It wasn't too sweet and pretty refreshing. Definitely recommend it.

Service was pretty slow. Also had to wait a while between the snow peas app and mains.

The low rating is due to the absolutely ridiculous service. I was there for lunch on Sunday July 14, party of 7 for a birthday celebration. We were seated and the brunch menu was on the table. 15 minutes later, nobody showed up to say they are our waiter and ask for drinks order. We flagged down the hostess who willingly took our order. The drinks arrived about 10 minutes later but the person delivering them said he is not the waiter. 5 minutes later a waitress showed up and took our orders. Another 15 minutes for appetizers to arrive. We wanted extra pita bread for the hummus dish. Had to flag down the hostess again because the waitress was MIA. Another 10 minutes for the pita bread to arrive. Basically one pita bread cut into 4 pieces for which we were charged $5 (!)
Another 30-35 minutes for the main course to arrive and NOT ONCE did the waitress come back to see if we wanted more drinks or if all was ok. 
The food was good but quite overpriced. 
I would not return because of poor service and overpriced.

We opted for the Trust the Chef ($80 per person) which came with 9 dishes for us to try. Food was good, however, one dish was the prawn and they definitely could have at least given 2 prawns  instead of just 1 little prawn for 3 people to share. For drinks, we got the La Santa and Llama Del Rey and they were both good. Service from the bussers was attentive like refilling water and clearing the table. The waiter who took our order was just okay.

If I had to sum up Llama Inn, it'd be: trying too hard to be hip and not worth the price tag. While the food at Llama Inn wasn't bad, it was definitely not worth the $100 for the lomo saltado nor the $50 for the Maine lobster. I also didn't like that the server tried to get us to order more by saying that she thought we didn't order enough for 4 people and that they preferred to put in all orders at once. Almost as if trying to prey on any anxiety and goad us into adding more. (FYI - the amount we ordered was just fine for 4 and we weren't hungry after, but if we had ended up hungry, we also thought it'd be better to stop for good pizza nearby given how much the food was compared to the portion sizes.) Drinks were also just okay to me - I think if they're trying to do "hip" drinks right with an Asian influence, they should take notes from Breeze, a Szechuan restaurant in Greenpoint. 

Gulf shrimp with parmesan: this was good, but not memorable. It was arguably a bit dry as well

Lamb sausage: comes with 2 pieces; also good but not memorable. If you're looking for quality lamb, look elsewhere. The lamb was definitely shareable between four people (it's basically two mini lamb hotdogs), but they tried to convince us for 3 minutes to order an extra order so each of us could have our own hot dog even though two of us are not the biggest lamb fans. As they were walking away, we had to clarify a final time to make it clear we only wanted one order 

Crispy squid ceviche: a "modern" take on Peruvian food as the squid came fried. I think this one was actually yummy, albeit a bit sour, but there was a healthy number of calamari and I thought this was reasonably priced for what I was getting. To be honest though, I'd recommend the Inkan's (another similarly rated Peruvian restaurant) ceviche over this one

Maine lobster: this was a new item on the menu. Was cooked with Asian influences, and I think was probably the group's favorite dish of the night. Not worth $50 though, as you can buy a similar tasting dish at other Asian restaurants without the hefty price tag. Think Red Sorghum (in LIC) or any number of Chinese restaurants in Manhattan

Lomo saltado: I cannot believe they charge $100 for this. There were maybe 6-8 pieces of beef or so at the bottom. Some of the pancakes were burnt and inedible. Our group laughed that it's sad the best part of the meal might have been the rice, which was basically just rice that had been buttered (was pretty good but who can go wrong with buttered rice?). The guac notes also did not taste well with the tamari or other soy sauce flavors of the dish. The fries were great and perfectly crispy, but why am I paying $100 for a dish that's majority fries...? If you're looking for someplace that actually does lomo saltado well and is reasonably priced for the amount of food you're getting, try Jora 

Tldr: I probably wouldn't come here again. I'm not quite sure they've nailed the Peruvian and Asian fusion quite right, and I think there are a lot of other restaurants that do Peruvian food and Asian influenced food better for higher quality and a much more reasonable price point

I'd agree with most of the other reviews saying that while the food is quite good for the most part, it is overpriced and some of the dishes were a little off. Does seem that they're trying too hard to be cool and hip with the peruvian/asian fusion. Service was nice though and the vibe of the place was cool.

My friend and I had a lovely dinner at Llama Inn. We got the Lamb Sausage snack, the Roasted Beets, the Pork Shoulder Escabeche, and the Arroz con Mariscos, and the Flan for dessert. Overall the food was delicious. Our favorite was the Roasted Beets dish, which was well balanced in flavor and texture.  I also enjoyed the Flan - it was uniquely prepared and was not overly sweet. The only downside is that the lime flavor for thr Arroz con Marisco was a bit overpowering, although the seafood was fresh and delicious.

We also got a round of cocktails, which were excellent. The staff were also friendly and attentive. The space itself was very slick with some cute branding by their llama logo. And there is a nice outdoors space. All in all, it is a nice experience, and I would recommend!

Have been wanting to try this place for the longest time and finally got a chance. This place is medium sized and was packed during a Friday night. It's a great date spot or a night out with friends. For food, my friend and I tried the lamb sausage snack, the roasted beets salad, the pork shoulder escabeche, and the arroz con mariscos. My favorite of the night was the beet dish! It had a great combination of flavors. In some cases, some dishes were a bit overpoweringly sour or salty in some areas, but overall still prepared well good.

Well, it is in a nice neighborhood in Brooklyn and the restaurant has nice decor. However the food... , "nada que ver". Started off with a crispy squid ceviche at $26. It was a bowl of Leche  de Tigre with a side of calamari. We ordered chicha morada for $13 each. The glass was only about 4/5 full and 1/4 of that was froth and not chicha . It was not sweet enough. The anticuchos were two pieces for $16 and it was too spicy to eat. Didn't even taste like beef heart. The lamb sausage for $16 came out like two pieces of mini breakfast sausage on a mini roll. The pork escabeche was so so at best. 

Maybe the food here is good, but it wasn't tonight

Cute, quaint spot , perfect for date night 

If you want to watch your pockets, I would suggest that you skip the initial appetizers, for the price and portion we could've done without. But the medium and Lodge play where the star of the show although they come with the price tag.( $100 for the Lomo ) every bite  seemed to be worth it. The lobster if you're a seafood lover was amazing and the sauce it's cooked in you could literally pour that on everything .  Will definitely be coming back here .

This was a really delicious, creative meal with plenty of vegetarian choices. It's expensive, but worth it.

Snow peas - had a really nice crunch to the peas themselves, and from the toasty quinoa topping. The sauce had a fresh, herbal flavor.

Jalapenos - a crispy fillo pastry like texture, with a creamy interior and a delicious, tangy sauce on the side. Like an elevated jalapeno popper.

Asparagus ceviche - the asparagus was fragrant and had a nice snap to the texture. The leche de tigre is a chilled potato and leek soup, with some fresh tartness to call back to a regular ceviche. The parmesan crisp added a nice crunch and savory, cheesy flavor.

Roasted beets - creamy, tart, and just the right amount of sweet. The beets had just the right balance of earthy flavor. The greens lighten up the dish just the right amount.

Mint "flan" - I almost skipped dessert and am really glad I didn't, because this was probably the best dish. The custard is incredibly soft, not as firm as typical flan. The syrup wasn't too sweet, and the layer of foam and mint syrup on top added a unique touch.

I have meant to check this restaurant out for some time and I finally made it. A visually appealing restaurant from the moment you enter with lots of greenery. Friendly and helpful staff, explained the Peruvian tapas style meal to us. Drinks were delicious. Started with the gulf shrimp which was very tasty but a little awkward to eat as a group of 4 since it was one shrimp and required removal from the shell. The lamb sausage was spectacular and easy to share. We also had (not photographed) the roasted beets salad and pork shoulder, both amazing. Finished with the arroz con mariscos which was absolutely phenomenal. Too full for dessert. Maybe next time.

Great vibe and food was not bad. $98 for lomo saltado personally not worth it in my opinion very salty and you can find mom and pop Peruvian places for cheaper and better. Jalapeño mozzarella sticks were good tho never had something like that before but we ate it before we got a photo. Our waiter was very nice and helped us ordered enough food for the table that we were able to split :)

So i've heard about this place for years & decided to go here for a GNO. 1) Vibes are amazing. You can tell the decor and all other things (silverware, plates, glasses) were carefully picked out & it makes the experience better. + if you get the corner booth seat because it is great people watching. 2) Drinks are on point. Super yummy and balanced. 3) Loved the apps we got - the squid ceviche is a must. Cauliflower was good but not as memorable as the squid ceviche. I could have drank the squid ceviche sauce. 4) Finally the main - the $100 Lomo Saltado. Don't get me wrong here, the dish was absolutely delicious. The meat was like butter it was so tender, but $100 is extremelyyyy steep for the dish. There's not THAT much meat under the bed of fries, but super delicious. Worth trying once!

Llama Inn - A Peruvian Feast in Williamsburg

We spent a night indulging in Llama Inn's bold, inventive flavors, and every bite was pure magic. From cocktails that impressed to dishes that made us pause and appreciate, this spot in Williamsburg is a must-visit for any foodie.

Cocktails That Set the Tone:

 Chiri Colada - Tropical vibes and smooth as silk.
 Supertini - Bold and refined.
 La Santa - Sweet with a subtle kick.
 Un Preview - Tart, smooth, and unforgettable.

Standout Dishes:

Beef Heart - Grilled perfection with ají panca and rocoto salsa.

Smoked Steelhead Trout - Balanced with huacatay, yuzu, and crispy potato.

Crispy Squid Ceviche - Crunchy and refreshing with celery and corn.

Salmon Tiradito - Vibrant, with silky salmon, roe, avocado, and carrot.

Maine Lobster - Decadent, served with jasmine rice and long beans.

Lucuma Flan - Smooth, creamy, and a perfect finish.


And let's not forget the savory potato chips with dip--crunchy, addictive, and the perfect snack to keep the night going!

Vibes & Service:

Llama Inn's ambiance hits just right: warm, rustic, and effortlessly cool. Whether it's for a special occasion or just a spontaneous night out, this is the spot for bold food, inventive cocktails, and impeccable service. We'll be back soon--because one night isn't nearly enough.

First name Llama, last name Inn. Known for its playful Peruvian flair, this trendy Williamsburg spot feels fittingly inspired by Peru's beloved mascot, the llama--Machu Picchu vibes included.

I stopped in on my way to a birthday in Brooklyn after a friend recommended it. Arriving to a packed house, I asked if there were any seats at the bar for drinks and dinner, and they were able to seat us quickly. We had a two-hour window due to reservations, so if you're visiting on a busy night, walk-ins are possible, but reservations are definitely recommended.

I ordered a drink while waiting for my friend, and ended up having two before they arrived. The cocktails were fantastic, especially their small-but-mighty martini--it may look tiny, but it packs a punch! (Consider yourself warned; it made the next morning a little rough, though we admittedly kept the night going afterward.)

The appetizers were fresh and thoughtfully crafted, with a clear emphasis on quality ingredients. Just keep in mind, the dishes are small; after four or five plates, we still felt a bit peckish. So, if you're hungry, go for a few extra proteins or carbs to fill up.

All in all, Llama Inn had great prices, quick service, and a fun atmosphere. I'd definitely recommend it for anyone looking for a lively night in Williamsburg with delicious food and cute cocktails.

This restaurant was absolutely stunning on the inside! Greenery everywhere with the bar in the center of the room & kitchen open for watching. The service was great and helped with recommendations. Our food was amazing, everything was so flavorful. The rice main was incredible and lots of seafood within. We also LOVED the crudo. Definitely recommend this spot!

Been here a few times since last year and recently was disappointed. Restaurant was able to accommodate my party of 7 but seemed to be just the bare minimum. Was told to be out by 8pm but service was kind of slow with gaps in-between the food. Food overall was very filling for the 80pf but didn't have the Wow-factor I used to love about this place. What fell flat for me was the whole reason our party was there to celebrate a Birthday which our waiter wasn't aware until the very end of the night.
Great ambiance! Food was delicious! We came here to celebrate our wedding anniversary and absolutely loved it. Def will be back!

I was expecting more from the meal that my partner and I got from this establishment. I expected the food to taste as good as the pictures looked from other eaters but sadly the meal did not meet expectations. I did, however, like our server (who seemed knowledgeable) and the atmosphere (which was dim and intimate).

Sad to say this will probably be my last time dining here. 

Llama Inn used to be a place where you can order anything on the menu and EVERYTHING was stupid delicious and amazing. 

Now as prices have gone up, service and quality has definitely gone down. 

We had issues with our two steaks and had to send both back. Then they came back out at two different times and at two different temperatures after we were told "it just comes medium". 

The ambiance is great and I guess that's what you're paying for. 

Previously we'd take a car to Llama Inn and home as a treat for a great dinner but now it's just another overly expensive night out going.

Gorgeous interior and absolute gems on the wait staff! The food is also incredible, but way way way over priced. The Latino in me was appalled at paying $100 for lomo saltado. The dish barely had any meat in it anyway basically paying $100 for mostly fries. It was delicious yes, but I don't think I could justify over paying that much again. Likely a one and done here or would come back with like 4 people and split it. Unfortunately loses a star for the price.

I came here one evening on a whim and was fortunately able to get a spot (highly recommend reservations here if you can!). The interior of the restaurant is dim and spacious, but the music was a bit loud when I went so it was hard to hear the person I was with.

We got the crispy squid ceviche, catch of the day, and the black sesame dessert. Everything was delicious. I highly recommend the crispy squid ceviche as it came with a nice dipping (?) broth that I absolutely loved. The catch of the day was soft, tender, and had an amazing sauce. And, the black sesame was an unexpected dessert/flavor to try at this Peruvian spot, but I loved it. Portions are a bit small, but everything was worth it.

Overall pretty good. Pretty small menu though. We had the pea appetizer, the mango curry, the calimari/squid ceviche, the steak tartar, and the catch of the day. The calamari, steak tartar, and pea appetizer were amazing. The rest was ok. They had chicha morada as a drink which was exciting, you don't see that often.
My favorite restaurant in the city 8 years and counting! Everything is always amazing
